readings.text: 1 In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth. 2 Now the earth was formless and empty, darkness was over the surface of the deep, and the Spirit of God was hovering over the waters.

3 And God said, "Let there be light," and there was light. 4 God saw that the light was good, and he separated the light from the darkness. 5 God called the light "day," and the darkness he called "night." And there was evening, and there was morning—the first day.
God makes the sky, the land and seas, plants and trees, the sun, moon and stars, the fish and birds, and all the animals. Each time, God saw that it was good.

26 Then God said, "Let us make mankind in our image, in our likeness, so that they may rule over the fish in the sea and the birds in the sky, over the livestock and all the wild animals, and over all the creatures that move along the ground."
27 So God created mankind in his own image, in the image of God he created them; male and female he created them.

28 God blessed them and said to them, "Be fruitful and increase in number; fill the earth and subdue it. Rule over the fish in the sea and the birds in the sky and over every living creature that moves on the ground."

29 Then God said, "I give you every seed-bearing plant on the face of the whole earth and every tree that has fruit with seed in it. They will be yours for food. 30 And to all the beasts of the earth and all the birds in the sky and all the creatures that move along the ground—everything that has the breath of life in it—I give every green plant for food." And it was so.
31 God saw all that he had made, and it was very good. And there was evening, and there was morning—the sixth day.

story: Long, long ago, before there were any people, animals, trees or even a sun, there was God. God has always been there. Everything else was dark and empty.
Then God spoke: "Let there be light!" And light appeared, just because God said so. He called the light "day" and the dark "night." That was the very first day.

God kept creating. He spread out the big blue sky. He gathered the water into seas and made dry land appear. He filled the land with plants, flowers and fruit trees. He put the bright sun in the sky for daytime and the moon and stars for nighttime. He filled the oceans with fish and giant sea creatures, and he filled the sky with birds. Then he made every kind of animal: puppies and horses, lions and bugs. Every time, God looked at what he made and saw that it was good.

Then God made something extra special: people. He made them in his own image, which means people are made to be like God in special ways. We can love, think, create, talk with God and take care of his world. God blessed the people and gave them a job: take care of everything he made.
At the end of the sixth day, God looked at everything and saw that it was very good.
weeks.enochLine: God made everything, and God made me!
enochActivities: Activity: "God Made It!" pointing game. Walk around the house or yard. Point at things God made (the sky, a tree, a dog, Mommy, Daddy, Jordyn, Elijah, Enoch!) and say together, "God made it!"
God gave people a job: taking care of his world. For extra fun, have Enoch draw his favorite animal God made.
elijahQuestions: When God said, "Let there be light," what happened?
After God made each thing, what did he see about it? At the end of the sixth day, what did he see about all that he had made?
God made a huge number of different animals. Which one do you think is the coolest, and what does it show you about how creative God is?
God made people "in his image." What is one way you can be like God this week, maybe by being kind, telling the truth, or helping someone?
jordynQuestions: Verse 3 says God simply spoke and light appeared. What does that tell us about how powerful God is compared to anything else?
What do you think it means to be made "in the image of God"? How should that change the way we treat people, including people who are hard to get along with?
God gave people the job to "rule over" and care for creation. How is ruling God's way, like a good caretaker, different from just being in charge?
weeks.jordynApplication: Everyone you meet this week, on your volleyball team, at school, or at home, is made in God's image. Pick one person who might feel left out or overlooked and do something on purpose to show them they matter: an encouraging word, a high-five after a play, or sitting with them. Your worth comes from the God who made you on purpose and saw that it was very good, not from how well you play or what others think.
elijahAnswers: There was light (Genesis 1:3).
After each part of creation he saw that it was good. At the end, he saw that all he had made was very good (v. 31).
Any animal is fine. The point is God's creativity: variety, beauty, and design show how wise and imaginative he is.
Examples: being kind, telling the truth, helping at home, caring for a pet or creation. "In his image" means we can love, create, speak truth, and care for others the way God does.
jordynAnswers: God's word alone has power to create. Nothing else is that powerful; he is not limited by tools, time, or materials.

Being made in God's image means people have God-given dignity and worth. We should treat everyone with respect and kindness, even people who are hard to get along with, because they bear his image too.
God's kind of ruling is serving and caring for what he made, not bossing people around for selfish gain. Like a good shepherd or caretaker, not a bully.
weeks.applicationCheck: Look for one concrete person she can encourage this week (teammate, classmate, sibling) and celebrate that her worth comes from God, not performance.
weeks.prayer: Dear God, thank you for making the whole world: the light, the sky, the oceans, the animals, and us. Thank you for making each person in our family in your image and on purpose. Help us remember that you made everything and that everything belongs to you. Help us take good care of your world and treat everyone with kindness, because they are made by you too. We love you. In Jesus' name, Amen.

dailies.label: Day 2
dailies.focus: Before anything else, God was there.
dailies.verse: In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth. Now the earth was formless and empty, darkness was over the surface of the deep, and the Spirit of God was hovering over the waters.
dailies.enoch: Point up for the heavens and down for the earth, and say, "God made it all!"
dailies.elijah: Before God made light and everything else, what was the earth like?
dailies.elijahAnswer: It was formless and empty, and dark (Genesis 1:2).
dailies.jordyn: Verse 2 says the Spirit of God was hovering over the waters before anything was made. What does that show about God?
dailies.jordynAnswer: God was already there before anything existed. He was present and ready to bring order and life out of emptiness, so everything comes from him.
dailies.action: Start with a blank piece of paper. Each person adds one thing God made, and together you watch the empty page fill up.
dailies.prayer: Dear God, you were there before anything else, and you will always be. Thank you for making the heavens and the earth. Help us remember that everything comes from you, and help us trust you because you never change. In Jesus' name, Amen.
dailies.teach: The very first words of the Bible are "In the beginning God." Before there were mountains, oceans, animals, or people, God was already there. He did not have a beginning; he has always been. Then God created the heavens and the earth. At first the earth was formless and empty, and it was dark, but the Spirit of God was hovering over the waters, like a bird over its nest, ready to bring life. Psalm 90:2 says, "from everlasting to everlasting you are God." Everything else had a start, but God did not, and everything comes from him.
dailies.enochActivity: Close your eyes and say, "It's dark!" Then open them wide and say, "God was always there!"
dailies.elijah2: Find it in the passage: In verse 1, what two big things did God create?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: God created "the heavens and the earth" (verse 1).
dailies.jordyn2: Verse 1 says "In the beginning God created." What is the difference between God making something and a person making something? Why does it matter that God had no beginning?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: People make things out of stuff that already exists, but God created the heavens and the earth when there was nothing else (verse 1). Because God had no beginning, he doesn't depend on anything; everything depends on him, so he is the one we can trust most.
dailies.passageText: 1 In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth. 2 Now the earth was formless and empty, darkness was over the surface of the deep, and the Spirit of God was hovering over the waters.

dailies.label: Day 3
dailies.focus: God spoke, and light appeared.
dailies.verse: And God said, "Let there be light," and there was light.
dailies.enoch: When Mom or Dad turns a light on, say, "God made the light!"
dailies.elijah: When God said, "Let there be light," what happened?
dailies.elijahAnswer: There was light (Genesis 1:3).
dailies.jordyn: God did not need tools or materials to make the light. What does that show about his power?
dailies.jordynAnswer: God's word alone has power to create. Nothing else is that powerful.
dailies.action: Turn the lights off, then on, and say together, "Let there be light!"
dailies.prayer: Dear God, thank you for speaking light into the darkness. Thank you for making day and night and for being in charge of every one of them. When we feel scared in the dark, help us remember that you made the light and that you are always with us. In Jesus' name, Amen.
dailies.teach: The earth was dark and empty, and then God spoke. He said, "Let there be light," and there was light. God didn't need a switch, a fire, or any tools; his words were enough. God looked at the light and saw that it was good. Then he separated the light from the darkness and gave them names: he called the light "day" and the darkness "night." That was the very first day. God brings light and order where there was darkness, and he still does that in our hearts today.
dailies.enochActivity: Turn a flashlight on and off. Each time it turns on, say, "Let there be light!"
dailies.elijah2: Find it in the passage: In verse 5, what did God call the light, and what did he call the darkness?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: He called the light "day," and the darkness he called "night" (verse 5).
dailies.jordyn2: In verse 4, God saw that the light was good and separated it from the darkness. Why do you think God named the day and the night? What does that show about how God runs his world?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: Naming them shows God is in charge of them; they belong to him (verse 5). God brings order, not confusion: light and darkness each have their place. It shows he runs his world with wisdom and care, and every day and night is under his control.
dailies.passageText: 3 And God said, “Let there be light,” and there was light. 4 God saw that the light was good, and he separated the light from the darkness. 5 God called the light “day,” and the darkness he called “night.” And there was evening, and there was morning—the first day.

dailies.label: Day 4
dailies.focus: God made people in his image and gave them a job.
dailies.verse: Then God said, "Let us make mankind in our image, in our likeness, so that they may rule over the fish in the sea and the birds in the sky, over the livestock and all the wild animals, and over all the creatures that move along the ground."
dailies.enoch: Give yourself a hug and say, "God made me special!"
dailies.elijah: Who did God make in his image, and what job did he give them?
dailies.elijahAnswer: God made people (mankind) in his image. He gave them the job of ruling over the fish, birds, and animals — caring for his world (Genesis 1:26).
dailies.jordyn: God said people should "rule over" the animals and the earth. What kind of ruling does God want?
dailies.jordynAnswer: God's kind of ruling is serving and caring for what he made, like a good caretaker, not a bully.
dailies.action: Name one way your family can take care of something God made this week, like a pet, a plant, or the yard.
dailies.prayer: Dear God, thank you for making all the animals and for making people in your image. Thank you for trusting us with the job of caring for your world. Help us be kind to animals and take good care of everything you made. In Jesus' name, Amen.
dailies.teach: On the sixth day, God filled the land with living creatures: livestock like cows and sheep, creatures that move along the ground, and wild animals, each according to its kind. God saw that it was good. Then God did something different. He said, "Let us make mankind in our image, in our likeness." Notice God says "us" and "our," a hint of the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit we will learn about next week. People are the only creatures made in God's image, and God gave them a job: to rule over the fish, birds, and animals by taking good care of his world for him.
dailies.enochActivity: Pretend to be a farmer feeding and petting the animals. Say, "I take care of God's world!"
dailies.elijah2: Find it in the passage: In verse 24, name the three kinds of land creatures God made.
dailies.elijahAnswer2: The livestock, the creatures that move along the ground, and the wild animals (verse 24).
dailies.jordyn2: In verse 26, God says, "Let us make mankind in our image, in our likeness." How is making people different from the way God made the animals in verses 24–25?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: God made the animals according to their kinds and saw that they were good (verses 24–25), but only people were made in God's image and likeness and given the job of ruling over the creatures (verse 26). People are special to God in a way animals are not, and that gives us both worth and responsibility.
dailies.passageText: 24 And God said, “Let the land produce living creatures according to their kinds: the livestock, the creatures that move along the ground, and the wild animals, each according to its kind.” And it was so. 25 God made the wild animals according to their kinds, the livestock according to their kinds, and all the creatures that move along the ground according to their kinds. And God saw that it was good. 26 Then God said, “Let us make mankind in our image, in our likeness, so that they may rule over the fish in the sea and the birds in the sky, over the livestock and all the wild animals, and over all the creatures that move along the ground.”

dailies.label: Day 5
dailies.focus: God made you on purpose, in his image.
dailies.verse: So God created mankind in his own image, in the image of God he created them; male and female he created them.
dailies.enoch: Point to Mommy, Daddy, Jordyn, Elijah, and yourself, and say, "God made you!"
dailies.elijah: God made people "in his image." What is one way you can be like God today?
dailies.elijahAnswer: Examples: being kind, telling the truth, helping at home, or caring for someone. "In his image" means we can love, create, speak truth, and care for others the way God does.
dailies.jordyn: Everyone you meet is made in God's image. How should that change the way you treat someone who is hard to get along with today?
dailies.jordynAnswer: We should treat them with respect and kindness, because they have God-given dignity and worth too, even when they are hard to get along with.
dailies.action: Do one kind thing on purpose tonight for someone in your family.
dailies.prayer: Dear God, thank you for making each of us in your image, on purpose and with a purpose. Thank you for making us male and female and for blessing us. Help us treat everyone with kindness and respect today, because every person is made by you. In Jesus' name, Amen.
dailies.teach: Verse 27 tells us three times that God created people in his image. He made them male and female, both equally in his image. Being made in God's image means we are like God in ways animals are not: we can know him, love, tell the truth, make things, and care for others. Then God blessed the man and woman and gave them a big job: to fill the earth and rule over every living creature, caring for it for him. Psalm 139:14 says, "I praise you because I am fearfully and wonderfully made." That means you are not an accident; God made you on purpose.
dailies.enochActivity: Look in a mirror and say, "God made me on purpose!" Then smile at someone in your family and say, "God made you too!"
dailies.elijah2: Find it in the passage: In verse 28, what did God do for the man and woman right after he made them?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: God blessed them and spoke to them (verse 28).
dailies.jordyn2: Verse 27 says God made people "male and female" and both in his image. What does that teach us about how boys and girls, men and women, should treat one another? How could that change how you treat people at school or on your team?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: Both are made in God's image (verse 27), so both have the same worth and deserve respect. No one is better or less than another because of being a boy or a girl. Any real example works for the second part, like including others, not mocking, and being kind to teammates.
dailies.passageText: 27 So God created mankind in his own image, in the image of God he created them; male and female he created them. 28 God blessed them and said to them, “Be fruitful and increase in number; fill the earth and subdue it. Rule over the fish in the sea and the birds in the sky and over every living creature that moves on the ground.”

dailies.label: Day 6
dailies.focus: God saw all that he had made, and it was very good.
dailies.verse: God saw all that he had made, and it was very good. And there was evening, and there was morning—the sixth day.
dailies.enoch: Fold your hands and say, "Thank you, God, for making the world!"
dailies.elijah: At the end of the sixth day, what did God see about all that he had made?
dailies.elijahAnswer: He saw that it was very good (Genesis 1:31).
dailies.jordyn: God saw that his finished world was very good. How can you treat God's world, and the people in it, like they are very good gifts from him?
dailies.jordynAnswer: We can thank God for what he made, take care of his world, and treat people with kindness because he made them on purpose.
dailies.action: Take a quiet moment together to thank God for one thing he made that you love.
dailies.prayer: Dear God, you saw all that you had made, and it was very good. Thank you for giving us food, family, and everything we need, even before we ask. Help us thank you every day and take good care of what you have made. In Jesus' name, Amen.
dailies.teach: At the end of the sixth day, God gave people and animals food to eat: seed-bearing plants and trees with fruit for people, and green plants for the animals. God provided everything his creatures needed. Then God looked at everything he had made, the light, the sky, the land and seas, the plants, the sun, moon, and stars, the fish, birds, animals, and people, and he saw that it was very good. Every other day God said his work was good, but after making people, he said it was very good. Today we thank God in prayer for his very good world and for making us.
dailies.enochActivity: Hold up a piece of fruit and say, "Thank you, God, for good food!"
dailies.elijah2: Find it in the passage: In verse 29, what did God give people for food?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: He gave them "every seed-bearing plant on the face of the whole earth and every tree that has fruit with seed in it" (verse 29).
dailies.jordyn2: God gave food to people and animals (verses 29–30) before anyone asked. What does that show about God's heart? What is something God provides for you that you could thank him for more often?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: It shows God is generous and caring; he knows what his creatures need and gives it (verses 29–30). Any real answer works for the second part, like food, family, a home, health, friends, or the chance to play sports.
dailies.passageText: 29 Then God said, “I give you every seed-bearing plant on the face of the whole earth and every tree that has fruit with seed in it. They will be yours for food. 30 And to all the beasts of the earth and all the birds in the sky and all the creatures that move along the ground—everything that has the breath of life in it—I give every green plant for food.” And it was so. 31 God saw all that he had made, and it was very good. And there was evening, and there was morning—the sixth day.

dailies.label: Day 7
dailies.focus: Remember: God made everything, and he made you on purpose.
dailies.verse: In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.
dailies.enoch: Look around and name one thing you can see that God made.
dailies.elijah: Name three things God made during the creation week.
dailies.elijahAnswer: Any three: light, sky, land and seas, plants and trees, sun, moon and stars, fish and birds, animals, and people (Genesis 1).
dailies.jordyn: What job did God give people when he made them?
dailies.jordynAnswer: God gave people the job to care for his world, ruling as good caretakers, not as bullies.
dailies.action: Play a quick "God made it!" pointing game around the room, then each person shares a favorite thing from this week.
dailies.prayer: Dear God, thank you for making the whole world and for making us on purpose. Thank you for the gift of rest and for blessing the seventh day. Help us remember that you made everything, and help us enjoy you and care for your world every day. In Jesus' name, Amen.
dailies.teach: Today we look back at our creation week. In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth. He spoke light into the darkness, filled the world with plants, animals, and people, and made people in his image to care for his world. When he finished, he saw that it was very good. Then, on the seventh day, God rested from all his work. He wasn't tired; God never gets tired. He rested because his work was complete, and he blessed the seventh day and made it holy, a special day to enjoy him. Next week we will learn who this God is: one God in three persons.
dailies.enochActivity: Lie down on the floor, stretch, and say, "God made everything, and it was very good!"
dailies.elijah2: Find it in the passage: In Genesis 2:2, what did God do on the seventh day?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: He rested: "on the seventh day he rested from all his work" (Genesis 2:2).
dailies.jordyn2: Genesis 2:3 says God blessed the seventh day and made it holy. Why do you think God gave us a pattern of work and rest? How could your family use a day of rest to enjoy God?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: God finished his work and rested, not because he was tired, but to set a good pattern and make the day special (Genesis 2:2–3). Rest reminds us that we depend on God, not on our own busy work. Any real answer works for the second part, like going to church, family time, or enjoying God's creation together.
dailies.passageText: 1 Thus the heavens and the earth were completed in all their vast array. 2 By the seventh day God had finished the work he had been doing; so on the seventh day he rested from all his work. 3 Then God blessed the seventh day and made it holy, because on it he rested from all the work of creating that he had done.

weeks.bigIdea: There is one God who is Father, Son, and Holy Spirit: three persons, each fully God, forever one God.
weeks.scheduleNote: This is the Week 2 family lesson. The short daily bites are Days 2–7.

howSteps.title: Read together
howSteps.detail: Open the Read tab and read Matthew 3:16–17, Deuteronomy 6:4, Matthew 28:19, and 2 Corinthians 13:14 out loud as a family.

howSteps.title: Talk it through
howSteps.detail: Still on Read, walk through the kid-language explanation so everyone gets the picture.

howSteps.title: Age parts
howSteps.detail: Use Enoch, Elijah, and Jordyn tabs. Keep the Parent key open for yourself.

howSteps.title: Pray
howSteps.detail: Close with the short family prayer on the Prayer tab.

readings.text: 16 As soon as Jesus was baptized, he went up out of the water. At that moment heaven was opened, and he saw the Spirit of God descending like a dove and alighting on him. 17 And a voice from heaven said, "This is my Son, whom I love; with him I am well pleased."
Hear, O Israel: The LORD our God, the LORD is one.
Therefore go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit,
May the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit be with you all.

story: There is only one God. He is not one god among many. The Bible says, "The LORD our God, the LORD is one."

This one God is three persons: the Father, the Son (Jesus), and the Holy Spirit. Each one is fully God. The Father is God. Jesus is God. The Holy Spirit is God. They are not three gods, and they are not one person putting on three different masks.

We cannot fully understand this, because God is greater than we are. People sometimes invent pictures to try to explain it, like water that can be ice, liquid, or steam. Pictures like that always fall short. Ice, water, and steam are forms of the same thing, usually one at a time. But at Jesus' baptism, the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit were all there at the same time, as distinct persons. So we do not lean on a picture. We trust what God has shown us.

At the Jordan River, Jesus was baptized. As soon as he came up out of the water, the Holy Spirit came down on him like a dove, and the Father's voice from heaven said, "This is my Son, whom I love; with him I am well pleased." We meet all three persons at once.

Before Jesus returned to heaven, he told his followers to make disciples of all nations and baptize them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit. That is one name, and three persons.
Paul later blessed the church with all three together: the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, the love of God, and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit.
weeks.enochLine: There is one God: the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit!
enochActivities: Activity: "One and three" finger count. Hold up one finger and say, "One God!" Then hold up three fingers and say, "Father, Son, and Holy Spirit!" Then go back to one finger: "One God!"

Paw Patrol touch: you can make it a mission, like the pups heading out to help. Enoch's mission is to remember who God is. For extra fun, have him draw the baptism story: Jesus in the water, a dove, and a bright sky for the Father's voice. Tell him the picture helps us remember the story, but no picture can show everything about God.
elijahQuestions: What does Deuteronomy 6:4 say about the LORD our God?
At Jesus' baptism in Matthew 3:16–17, who was in the water? Who came down like a dove? Who spoke from heaven?
In Matthew 28:19, Jesus says to baptize people in the name of whom?
2 Corinthians 13:14 names Jesus, God, and the Holy Spirit together in one blessing. What does that show us about God?
jordynQuestions: At Jesus' baptism, all three persons appear at the same time, doing different things. What does that tell us about whether the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit are just three names for one person?
Deuteronomy 6:4 says the LORD is one, and Matthew 28:19 speaks of "the name" of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit. How do those words guard us from thinking there are three gods?
Why is it wiser to say what the Bible shows — one God, three persons — than to explain God with a picture like water, ice, and steam?
weeks.jordynApplication: This week, when you pray before a volleyball game, at school, or at home, speak to the one God as he has made himself known: thank the Father who loves you, trust Jesus the Son who came for you, and ask the Holy Spirit to help you. If a friend asks who Christians worship, you can say simply: we worship one God — the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit.
elijahAnswers: "The LORD our God, the LORD is one." (Deuteronomy 6:4)

Jesus had just been baptized and came up out of the water. The Spirit of God came down like a dove and rested on him. The Father spoke from heaven: "This is my Son, whom I love; with him I am well pleased." (Matthew 3:16–17)
In the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit (Matthew 28:19).
It shows that the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit belong together as the one God. This is one blessing from one God, not three separate gods.
jordynAnswers: They are distinct persons. At the same moment, the Son is baptized, the Spirit descends, and the Father speaks. That is not one person switching roles or names.
There is one God (Deuteronomy 6:4). Jesus speaks of one "name," then names the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit. One name, three persons — not three gods.

Pictures like water, ice, and steam describe one thing taking different forms, often at different times. Other pictures fail in other ways. At Jesus' baptism the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit are all present at once, each fully God, and still one God. Every picture falls short, so we stay with what Scripture shows and admit the mystery with humility.
weeks.applicationCheck: Listen for her naming Father, Son, and Holy Spirit as one God, and notice a specific prayer or conversation this week.
weeks.prayer: Dear God, thank you that you are the one true God. Thank you, Father, for loving us. Thank you, Jesus, for coming to us. Thank you, Holy Spirit, for being with us. We cannot understand everything about you, but we believe what you have shown us. Help our family love you, trust you, and tell the truth about who you are. We love you. In Jesus' name, Amen.

dailies.label: Day 2
dailies.focus: There is one God: the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit.
dailies.verse: Therefore go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit,
dailies.enoch: Hold up one finger and say, "One God!" Then hold up three fingers and say, "Father, Son, and Holy Spirit!"
dailies.elijah: In Matthew 28:19, Jesus says to baptize people in the name of whom?
dailies.elijahAnswer: In the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit (Matthew 28:19).
dailies.jordyn: Why does Jesus say "the name" of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, not "the names"?
dailies.jordynAnswer: One "name" points to one God. The Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit are three persons, not three gods.
dailies.action: Find Matthew 28:19 in a Bible together and point to the three persons named in one "name."
dailies.prayer: Dear God, thank you that you are one God, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. Thank you that you make your people one family. Help us tell others about you and live together in peace as your children. In Jesus' name, Amen.
dailies.teach: On Sunday we learned that there is one God who is three persons: the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit. Our key verse is Jesus' words in Matthew 28:19, where he tells his followers to baptize people "in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit." Today's reading from Ephesians shows the same truth. Paul writes about "one Spirit" (the Holy Spirit), "one Lord" (Jesus the Son), and "one God and Father of all." Three persons are named, but there is still only one God. That is hard to fully understand, and that's okay; God is bigger than our minds, and we believe it because the Bible teaches it.
dailies.enochActivity: Hold up one finger and say, "One God!" Then wiggle three fingers and say, "Father, Son, Holy Spirit!"
dailies.elijah2: Find it in the passage: Ephesians 4:4–6 uses the word "one" many times. Name two "one" things from the list.
dailies.elijahAnswer2: Any two: one body, one Spirit, one hope, one Lord, one faith, one baptism, one God and Father of all (Ephesians 4:4–6).
dailies.jordyn2: Ephesians 4:4–6 names "one Spirit," "one Lord," and "one God and Father of all." How does that match Matthew 28:19? Why do you think Paul keeps repeating the word "one"?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: Both name the Father, the Son (the Lord Jesus), and the Holy Spirit together (Matthew 28:19; Ephesians 4:4–6). Paul repeats "one" to show that God is one and that his people belong together as one family under one God, not divided.
dailies.passageText: 4 There is one body and one Spirit, just as you were called to one hope when you were called; 5 one Lord, one faith, one baptism; 6 one God and Father of all, who is over all and through all and in all.

dailies.label: Day 3
dailies.focus: The LORD our God is one.
dailies.verse: Hear, O Israel: The LORD our God, the LORD is one.
dailies.enoch: Say with the family, "The LORD our God, the LORD is one!"
dailies.elijah: What does Deuteronomy 6:4 tell us about the LORD our God?
dailies.elijahAnswer: "The LORD our God, the LORD is one." (Deuteronomy 6:4)
dailies.jordyn: Why does it matter that Christians worship one God, not three gods?
dailies.jordynAnswer: There is only one God. The Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit are not three gods; they are three persons who are the one God.
dailies.action: When you hear the word "God" today, quietly remember: there is only one God.
dailies.prayer: Dear God, thank you that you are the one true God. Help us love you with all our heart, soul, and strength. Keep your words on our hearts, and help our family talk about you at home, on the road, at bedtime, and every morning. In Jesus' name, Amen.
dailies.teach: Long before Jesus was born, Moses spoke to God's people, Israel, as they got ready to enter the land God promised them. He told them the most important truth of all: "Hear, O Israel: The LORD our God, the LORD is one." All around them, other nations worshiped many pretend gods, but there is only one true God. Then Moses told them how to respond: love the LORD your God with all your heart, soul, and strength. He also told parents to teach these words to their children at home, on the road, at bedtime, and in the morning. That is what our family is doing right now!
dailies.enochActivity: Put your hand on your heart and say, "I love you, God, with all my heart!"
dailies.elijah2: Find it in the passage: In verse 5, what three things should we love the LORD our God with?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: Heart, soul, and strength: "with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength" (verse 5).
dailies.jordyn2: Verse 7 tells parents to talk about God's words "when you sit at home and when you walk along the road, when you lie down and when you get up." Why do you think God wants faith talked about in everyday life, not just at church? What is one ordinary moment you could think about God this week?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: God wants faith to be part of all of life, not just one hour a week (verse 7). Talking about him at home, on the road, at bedtime, and in the morning helps his words stay on our hearts (verse 6). Any real moment works for the second part, like the car ride to school, before practice, or at bedtime.
dailies.passageText: 4 Hear, O Israel: The LORD our God, the LORD is one. 5 Love the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength. 6 These commandments that I give you today are to be on your hearts. 7 Impress them on your children. Talk about them when you sit at home and when you walk along the road, when you lie down and when you get up.

dailies.label: Day 4
dailies.focus: At Jesus' baptism we meet the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit at the same time.
dailies.verse: 16 As soon as Jesus was baptized, he went up out of the water. At that moment heaven was opened, and he saw the Spirit of God descending like a dove and alighting on him. 17 And a voice from heaven said, "This is my Son, whom I love; with him I am well pleased."
dailies.enoch: Who was in the water? (Jesus!) Who came down like a dove? (the Holy Spirit!) Who spoke from heaven? (the Father!)
dailies.elijah: At Jesus' baptism, who was in the water, who came down like a dove, and who spoke from heaven?
dailies.elijahAnswer: Jesus was in the water. The Spirit of God came down like a dove. The Father spoke from heaven (Matthew 3:16–17).
dailies.jordyn: All three persons appear at the same time, doing different things. What does that tell us about whether they are just three names for one person?
dailies.jordynAnswer: They are distinct persons. At the same moment, the Son is baptized, the Spirit descends, and the Father speaks. That is not one person switching roles or names.
dailies.action: Act out the baptism scene in about 30 seconds: one person standing as Jesus, one showing the Spirit coming down like a dove, and one speaking the Father's words.
dailies.prayer: Dear God, thank you that at Jesus' baptism we see you as Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. Thank you, Father, for loving your Son, and thank you for loving us too. Help us trust what you have shown us in your Word. In Jesus' name, Amen.
dailies.teach: Matthew is not the only one who tells about Jesus' baptism; Mark tells it too. Jesus came from Nazareth in Galilee, and John baptized him in the Jordan River. As Jesus was coming up out of the water, he saw heaven being torn open and the Spirit coming down on him like a dove. Then a voice came from heaven: "You are my Son, whom I love; with you I am well pleased." Jesus the Son is in the water, the Holy Spirit comes down like a dove, and the Father speaks from heaven, all at the same time. It is one of the clearest pictures of one God in three persons in the whole Bible.
dailies.enochActivity: Flap your arms like a gentle dove and fly slowly down to land on someone's shoulder. Say, "The Holy Spirit came down like a dove!"
dailies.elijah2: Find it in the passage: In Mark 1:9, which river was Jesus baptized in?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: The Jordan (Mark 1:9).
dailies.jordyn2: In Mark 1:11 the Father says, "You are my Son, whom I love; with you I am well pleased." Jesus had not preached or done miracles yet. What does that tell you about the Father's love?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: The Father loved the Son and was pleased with him before Jesus' public work began (Mark 1:11). His love is not earned by doing big things; it comes first. Those who trust Jesus are loved by the Father too, not because of what they accomplish.
dailies.passageText: 9 At that time Jesus came from Nazareth in Galilee and was baptized by John in the Jordan. 10 Just as Jesus was coming up out of the water, he saw heaven being torn open and the Spirit descending on him like a dove. 11 And a voice came from heaven: “You are my Son, whom I love; with you I am well pleased.”

dailies.label: Day 5
dailies.focus: The Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit bless us together.
dailies.verse: May the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit be with you all.
dailies.enoch: Repeat: "Thank you, Jesus. Thank you, Father. Thank you, Holy Spirit."
dailies.elijah: Which three names do you hear in this blessing?
dailies.elijahAnswer: The Lord Jesus Christ, God (the Father), and the Holy Spirit (2 Corinthians 13:14).
dailies.jordyn: How does this one blessing show that the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit belong together as one God?
dailies.jordynAnswer: It is one blessing, not three separate blessings from three gods. The grace of Jesus, the love of God, and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit come together from the one God.
dailies.action: Read 2 Corinthians 13:14 out loud as a blessing over your family at dinner or bedtime.
dailies.prayer: Dear God, thank you for the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, the love of God, and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit. Help our family encourage one another and live in peace. Thank you that you, the God of love and peace, are with us. In Jesus' name, Amen.
dailies.teach: Paul wrote a letter to the church in the city of Corinth, and these are his last words to them. He told them to rejoice, encourage one another, be of one mind, and live in peace, and he promised that "the God of love and peace will be with you." He told them to greet one another warmly, the way family does. Then he closed with a blessing that names all three persons of God: the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, the love of God the Father, and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit. Fellowship means being close and sharing life together. Christians still use this blessing today, and our family can pray it over each other.
dailies.enochActivity: Give each person in the family a hug and say, "God bless you!"
dailies.elijah2: Find it in the passage: In verse 11, what does Paul say the God of love and peace will do?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: He "will be with you" (verse 11).
dailies.jordyn2: In verse 11, Paul tells the church to "encourage one another, be of one mind, live in peace." Why do you think a blessing about the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit fits right after those instructions? Which one of those instructions is hardest for you at home or with friends?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: The Father, Son, and Holy Spirit live in perfect love and unity, and God's grace, love, and fellowship (verse 14) give us what we need to live in peace with each other (verse 11). Any honest answer works for the second part.
dailies.passageText: 11 Finally, brothers and sisters, rejoice! Strive for full restoration, encourage one another, be of one mind, live in peace. And the God of love and peace will be with you. 12 Greet one another with a holy kiss. 13 All God’s people here send their greetings. 14 May the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit be with you all.

dailies.label: Day 6
dailies.focus: Pray to the one God as Father, Son, and Holy Spirit.
dailies.verse: Therefore go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit,
dailies.enoch: Say, "Thank you, Father. Thank you, Jesus. Thank you, Holy Spirit."
dailies.elijah: What is one thing you can thank God for today: something about the Father, about Jesus, or about the Holy Spirit?
dailies.elijahAnswer: Any true answer is fine: thank the Father for loving us and making us, thank Jesus for coming to us, or thank the Holy Spirit for being with us.
dailies.jordyn: If a friend asked who Christians worship, what would you say in one sentence?
dailies.jordynAnswer: We worship one God — the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit.
dailies.action: Pray once today naming the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit, before school, practice, or bed.
dailies.prayer: Dear Father, thank you for loving us and making us your family. Dear Jesus, thank you for coming to save us and for promising to be with us always. Dear Holy Spirit, thank you for being with us and helping us obey. In Jesus' name, Amen.
dailies.teach: After Jesus rose from the dead, he met his disciples on a mountain in Galilee and gave them their big job before going back to heaven. He told them to go to every nation, make disciples, and baptize them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit. Notice he said "the name," not "the names": one God, three persons. That is what we have learned all week. Jesus also promised, "I am with you always," so his followers never do this job alone. Talking to God is like talking to a family member who is always home: we can pray to the Father, thank Jesus, and ask the Holy Spirit for help, because it is one God who hears us.
dailies.enochActivity: Hold up one finger and say "One God!" Then hold up three fingers, one at a time: "Father, Jesus, Holy Spirit!" Then fold your hands and say a thank-you prayer to God.
dailies.elijah2: Find it in the passage: In verse 20, what does Jesus promise his followers? Why do you think that promise would help them be brave?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: Jesus promises, "I am with you always, to the very end of the age." It helps them be brave because they never have to go anywhere without him.
dailies.jordyn2: Jesus says "in the name" (one name), not "in the names," of the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. What does that small detail teach us? Where could you remember Jesus' promise in verse 20 this week?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: It points to one God in three persons, sharing one name. Any real answer works for the second part, such as before a test, a big game, or a hard conversation, remembering that Jesus said, "I am with you always."
dailies.passageText: 16 Then the eleven disciples went to Galilee, to the mountain where Jesus had told them to go. 17 When they saw him, they worshiped him; but some doubted. 18 Then Jesus came to them and said, “All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to me. 19 Therefore go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, 20 and teaching them to obey everything I have commanded you. And surely I am with you always, to the very end of the age.”

dailies.label: Day 7
dailies.focus: One God, three persons, each fully God.
dailies.verse: Therefore go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit,
dailies.enoch: Do the one-and-three finger count again: "One God!" then "Father, Son, and Holy Spirit!" then "One God!"
dailies.elijah: Are the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit three gods, or one God?
dailies.elijahAnswer: One God. The Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit are three persons, each fully God, not three gods.
dailies.jordyn: Why do pictures like water, ice, and steam fall short of describing God?
dailies.jordynAnswer: Pictures like water, ice, and steam describe one thing taking different forms, often at different times. At Jesus' baptism the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit are all present at once, each fully God, and still one God. Every picture falls short, so we stay with what the Bible shows.
dailies.action: Play the finger-count game three times, then each person shares one thing they learned about God this week.
dailies.prayer: Dear God, thank you that you are one God: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. Thank you, Father, for loving your Son, and thank you, Jesus and Holy Spirit, for coming close to us. Help our family remember what we learned this week and tell the truth about who you are. In Jesus' name, Amen.
dailies.teach: Today we look back at the week. At the start, we read about Jesus being baptized in the Jordan River. Right when he came up out of the water, all three persons of God showed up at once: Jesus the Son came up out of the water, the Spirit of God came down like a dove, and the Father's voice spoke from heaven. That is why we say there is one God in three persons: the Bible shows all three together at the same moment, and it also says there is only one God. Every picture we try, like water, ice, and steam, falls short, so we hold on to what the Bible shows. Later Jesus told his followers to baptize in the one name of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit (our key verse), the same three we see at his baptism.
dailies.enochActivity: Act out Jesus' baptism: crouch down low (Jesus in the water), stand up tall (coming out of the water), flap your hands like a dove (the Holy Spirit), and cup your hands by your mouth to say, "This is my Son, whom I love!" (the Father's voice).
dailies.elijah2: Find it in the passage: In verses 16 and 17, where is each person of God? Why do you think God let people see and hear all three at once?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: Jesus the Son is coming up out of the water, the Spirit of God is coming down like a dove, and the Father is the voice from heaven. God showed all three at once so people would know who Jesus is and that the Father, Son, and Spirit are all there together.
dailies.jordyn2: In verse 17 the Father says, "This is my Son, whom I love." What does that tell you about how the Father and the Son relate? This coming week we learn about God the Father: how could knowing the Father loves the Son help you trust that he loves you?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: The Father loves the Son and is pleased with him; the persons of God are in a real, loving relationship. Any honest answer works for the second part, such as: if the Father's love is that real and personal, I can trust him when I feel left out, stressed, or unsure.
dailies.passageText: 13 Then Jesus came from Galilee to the Jordan to be baptized by John. 14 But John tried to deter him, saying, “I need to be baptized by you, and do you come to me?” 15 Jesus replied, “Let it be so now; it is proper for us to do this to fulfill all righteousness.” Then John consented. 16 As soon as Jesus was baptized, he went up out of the water. At that moment heaven was opened, and he saw the Spirit of God descending like a dove and alighting on him. 17 And a voice from heaven said, “This is my Son, whom I love; with him I am well pleased.”

weeks.title: God the Father
weeks.selectLabel: Week 3 · God the Father
weeks.nextUp: Week 4 · Jesus the Son (Thanksgiving)
weeks.bigIdea: God the Father is a perfect, loving Father who cares for his children, and everyone who trusts in Jesus gets to be his child.
weeks.scheduleNote: This is the Week 3 family lesson. The short daily bites are Days 2–7.

howSteps.title: Read together
howSteps.detail: Open the Read tab and read the five short passages out loud. Let a different person read each one.

howSteps.title: Talk it through
howSteps.detail: Still on Read, walk through the kid-language explanation so everyone gets the picture.

howSteps.title: Age parts
howSteps.detail: Use Enoch, Elijah, and Jordyn tabs. Keep the Parent key open for yourself.

howSteps.title: Pray
howSteps.detail: Close with the short family prayer on the Prayer tab.

readings.text: 26 Look at the birds of the air; they do not sow or reap or store away in barns, and yet your heavenly Father feeds them. Are you not much more valuable than they?

9 "Which of you, if your son asks for bread, will give him a stone? 10 Or if he asks for a fish, will give him a snake? 11 If you, then, though you are evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father in heaven give good gifts to those who ask him!
13 As a father has compassion on his children, so the LORD has compassion on those who fear him;
12 Yet to all who did receive him, to those who believed in his name, he gave the right to become children of God—
1 See what great love the Father has lavished on us, that we should be called children of God! And that is what we are! The reason the world does not know us is that it did not know him.

story: Last week we learned that there is one God in three persons: the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit. This week we get to know the first person, God the Father.

Jesus talked about his Father all the time. When he taught his friends to pray, he told them to start with "Our Father in heaven." That means we can talk to the God who made everything the way a child talks to a dad who loves them.

Jesus pointed to the birds. Birds don't plant gardens or fill up barns with food, but they still eat, because "your heavenly Father feeds them." Then Jesus asked, "Are you not much more valuable than they?" If God takes care of little birds, he will take care of you.

Jesus also said: if a kid asks his dad for bread, the dad won't hand him a rock. If he asks for a fish, the dad won't hand him a snake! Even moms and dads who sometimes do wrong know how to give good gifts. So our Father in heaven, who never does wrong, gives even better gifts to those who ask him.

The Bible says that like a good father has compassion on his children, God has compassion on his people. Compassion means he sees when we are hurting and cares about it. Even the best dads on earth make mistakes sometimes, but God the Father is perfect. He never stops loving, never gets too busy, and never changes.

Here is the best part. How do we become God's children? The Bible says that to everyone who receives Jesus and believes in his name, God gives the right to become children of God. It is a gift, not something we earn.

That is why John wrote, "See what great love the Father has lavished on us, that we should be called children of God! And that is what we are!" Lavished means God poured out his love on us, way more than we need, like a bucket that keeps overflowing.
weeks.enochLine: God is my Father in heaven, and he loves me!
enochActivities: Activity: Bird snack hunt. Go to a window or the backyard and look for birds together. Each time you see one, say, "God feeds the birds, and God takes care of me!" If you have a snack, share it and say thank you to God the Father.

Song idea: sing "Jesus Loves Me," then sing it again changing the first words to "God my Father loves me." Paw Patrol touch: Ryder always takes care of his pups when they need help; God the Father takes even better care of his children, every single day.
elijahQuestions: Jesus said God feeds the birds. What does that tell us about how God takes care of us?
In Jesus' example, would a dad give his son a rock when he asks for bread? Why is that silly? What does it teach us about God?
Who gets to become a child of God, according to John 1:12?
Think of a baseball coach or a dad who cheers for his kid at every game. How is God the Father even better than the best coach or dad you know?
jordynQuestions: Jesus said even imperfect parents give good gifts, so "how much more" will the Father in heaven. What does "how much more" tell you about the difference between earthly parents and God?
1 John 3:1 says the Father has "lavished" his love on us. How is being called God's child different from just being one of the things he made?
Being God's child is a gift we receive by believing in Jesus, not a prize we earn. Why does that matter on days when you feel like you messed up or didn't measure up?
weeks.jordynApplication: In Harry Potter, Harry grows up feeling unwanted until he finds out who he really is and who loved him. Your real identity is even better and it's true: if you trust Jesus, you are a child of God, loved by the Father. This week, before a volleyball match, a test, or anything that makes you nervous, remind yourself: "Whatever happens, I am still God's child." Write 1 John 3:1 on a card and keep it in your bag or on your phone lock screen.
elijahAnswers: God knows what we need and takes care of us. We are worth much more to him than birds (Matthew 6:26).
No, a good dad would never do that. If even earthly dads give good things, God the Father gives his children good gifts too (Matthew 7:9–11).
Everyone who receives Jesus and believes in his name (John 1:12).
Any good answer works: God never misses a game, never gets tired or grumpy, always knows what we need, never stops loving us, and is perfect.
jordynAnswers: "How much more" means God is far better than even the best parent. Earthly parents are sinners who still love their kids; God is perfect, so his love and gifts are perfectly good and never fail.

Everything God made belongs to him, but being his child means a close, family relationship: he loves us as a Father, we belong in his family, we can talk to him anytime, and we share in his home forever. That is love poured out far beyond what we deserve.

Our place in God's family rests on Jesus, not on our performance. When we sin, we confess it and he forgives us; he doesn't kick his children out of the family. That gives security and peace instead of fear or pressure.
weeks.applicationCheck: Ask later in the week whether she wrote the verse down and when she used it. Celebrate that her identity rests on being God's child, not on how she plays or what others think.
weeks.prayer: Dear Father in heaven, thank you for loving us so much that you let us be called your children. Thank you for taking care of us like you take care of the birds, and for giving us good gifts every day. Help each of us trust Jesus and know that we belong to you. Help us talk to you like children who love their Father. In Jesus' name, Amen.

dailies.label: Day 2
dailies.focus: If you trust Jesus, you are God's child, loved by the Father.
dailies.verse: See what great love the Father has lavished on us, that we should be called children of God! And that is what we are!
dailies.enoch: Give Enoch a big hug and say together, "God loves me! I'm his child!"
dailies.elijah: What does the Father call us in 1 John 3:1?
dailies.elijahAnswer: Children of God. And the verse says, "that is what we are!"
dailies.jordyn: What does the word "lavished" tell you about how much God loves his children?
dailies.jordynAnswer: Lavished means poured out generously, far more than needed. God's love isn't stingy or barely enough; it overflows.
dailies.action: Read 1 John 3:1 together three times, getting a little louder each time.
dailies.prayer: Father, thank you for lavishing your great love on us and calling us your children. Help us remember who we are when we feel left out or make mistakes. Make us more like Jesus until the day we see him. In Jesus' name, Amen.
dailies.teach: John wrote this letter to Christians to remind them who they are. He says the Father has lavished, or poured out, great love on us, so that we are called children of God, and then he adds, "And that is what we are!" It is not just a nice name; it is true. On Sunday we learned that God is a perfect, loving Father, and everyone who trusts Jesus gets to be his child. Verse 2 says there is even more coming: when Jesus appears, we will be like him. A newborn baby doesn't earn the family's last name; it is given in love, and that is how the Father gives his children his name.
dailies.enochActivity: Draw a big heart with a stick figure of Enoch inside it. Point to it and say, "I'm God's child!"
dailies.elijah2: Find it in the passage: In verse 2, what will happen when Christ appears? Why is that good news?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: We shall be like him, for we shall see him as he is (verse 2). It is good news because one day we will see Jesus face to face and be like him.
dailies.jordyn2: Verse 1 says the world does not know us because it did not know him. Why might following Jesus sometimes make you feel different from people around you? When this week could you remind yourself that you are God's child, like when you feel left out or make a mistake?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: The world did not know Jesus, so it will not always understand his children either (verse 1). Feeling different is normal, and our worth comes from the Father's love, not from fitting in. Any real situation works for the second part.
dailies.passageText: 1 See what great love the Father has lavished on us, that we should be called children of God! And that is what we are! The reason the world does not know us is that it did not know him. 2 Dear friends, now we are children of God, and what we will be has not yet been made known. But we know that when Christ appears, we shall be like him, for we shall see him as he is. 3 All who have this hope in him purify themselves, just as he is pure.

dailies.label: Day 3
dailies.focus: God the Father cares when his children are hurting.
dailies.verse: As a father has compassion on his children, so the LORD has compassion on those who fear him;
dailies.enoch: Ask Enoch: "What does Daddy do when you get a boo-boo?" Then say, "God cares about me too!"
dailies.elijah: What is compassion? Can you think of a time someone showed you compassion?
dailies.elijahAnswer: Compassion means seeing someone is hurting and caring enough to help. Any real example works.
dailies.jordyn: Why might it help to remember Psalm 103:13 on a hard or sad day?
dailies.jordynAnswer: On hard days we can feel alone, but this verse says God sees us and cares deeply, like a loving father. We can bring our hurts to him.
dailies.action: Tell each other one thing that is hard right now and pray for it together.
dailies.prayer: Father, thank you that you are compassionate and gracious, slow to anger and abounding in love. Thank you for caring when we are hurting and for taking our sins far away. Help us bring our hurts to you instead of carrying them alone. In Jesus' name, Amen.
dailies.teach: King David wrote Psalm 103 as a song praising God for his kindness. In these verses he says the LORD is compassionate and gracious, slow to anger, and abounding in love. God does not treat us as our sins deserve; he removes our sins as far as the east is from the west, farther than anyone could ever travel. Then David says the LORD has compassion on us the way a father does on his children, because he remembers that we are dust: he knows we are small and weak. That is our big idea this week: God the Father is a perfect, loving Father who cares for his children. When a little one falls and scrapes a knee, a good dad doesn't yell; he scoops them up, and God's care is even better than that.
dailies.enochActivity: Put a pretend bandage (a sticker works) on a stuffed animal and pat it gently while you say, "God cares when I'm hurt!"
dailies.elijah2: Find it in the passage: In verse 12, how far does God remove our sins from us? Why do you think David chose east and west to describe it?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: As far as the east is from the west (verse 12). East and west never meet, no matter how far you go, so it is a picture of God taking our sins completely away. Any answer like "super, super far" is great.
dailies.jordyn2: Verse 14 says God "knows how we are formed" and "remembers that we are dust." Why is it comforting that God knows our weaknesses? The next time you mess up, how could verses 10 and 12 change what you do next?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: God is never surprised by our weakness. He knows we are frail and responds with compassion (verses 13–14). When we mess up, we don't have to hide; we can confess to him, because he does not treat us as our sins deserve (verse 10) and removes our sins far from us (verse 12).
dailies.passageText: 8 The LORD is compassionate and gracious, slow to anger, abounding in love. 9 He will not always accuse, nor will he harbor his anger forever; 10 he does not treat us as our sins deserve or repay us according to our iniquities. 11 For as high as the heavens are above the earth, so great is his love for those who fear him; 12 as far as the east is from the west, so far has he removed our transgressions from us. 13 As a father has compassion on his children, so the LORD has compassion on those who fear him; 14 for he knows how we are formed, he remembers that we are dust.

dailies.label: Day 4
dailies.focus: Our Father knows what we need, so we don't have to worry.
dailies.verse: 31 So do not worry, saying, 'What shall we eat?' or 'What shall we drink?' or 'What shall we wear?' 32 For the pagans run after all these things, and your heavenly Father knows that you need them.
dailies.enoch: Point to your food, your drink, and your clothes and say, "God gives me this!"
dailies.elijah: What three things does Jesus say we don't need to worry about?
dailies.elijahAnswer: What we will eat, what we will drink, and what we will wear (Matthew 6:31).
dailies.jordyn: What's one thing you tend to worry about? What would change if you really believed your Father knows you need it?
dailies.jordynAnswer: Any honest answer. Trusting that the Father knows and cares lets us pray about it instead of carrying the worry alone.
dailies.action: At dinner, have everyone name one thing God gave them today.
dailies.prayer: Heavenly Father, thank you for feeding the birds and dressing the flowers, and for caring for us even more. When we worry, help us remember that you know what we need. Teach us to seek you first. In Jesus' name, Amen.
dailies.teach: Jesus said these words in a long teaching on a mountainside, often called the Sermon on the Mount. He pointed to the birds and the flowers: birds don't plant or store food, and flowers don't sew clothes, yet God feeds and dresses them. If the Father takes care of birds and flowers, he will surely take care of his children, who are worth much more. Worrying can't add a single hour to our lives, but trusting our Father frees us to seek first his kingdom. This is the week's big idea again: our Father cares for his children and knows what we need. A player at a volleyball tournament doesn't panic about lunch when Mom already has the cooler in the car; she trusts it's handled.
dailies.enochActivity: Go to a window or step outside and look for a bird or a plant. Point and say, "God feeds the birds, and God takes care of me!"
dailies.elijah2: Find it in the passage: In verse 26, who feeds the birds? Why does Jesus say we don't need to worry?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: Your heavenly Father feeds them (verse 26). We don't need to worry because we are much more valuable than the birds, and our Father knows what we need (verses 26 and 32).
dailies.jordyn2: Verse 33 says to "seek first his kingdom and his righteousness." What does it look like to put God first instead of worrying? What is one worry you can turn into a prayer tonight?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: Seeking first his kingdom means making God and doing what is right our top priority and trusting him with the rest; Jesus promises that "all these things will be given to you as well" (verse 33). Any honest worry works for the second part; help her pray it out loud.
dailies.passageText: 26 Look at the birds of the air; they do not sow or reap or store away in barns, and yet your heavenly Father feeds them. Are you not much more valuable than they? 27 Can any one of you by worrying add a single hour to your life? 28 “And why do you worry about clothes? See how the flowers of the field grow. They do not labor or spin. 29 Yet I tell you that not even Solomon in all his splendor was dressed like one of these. 30 If that is how God clothes the grass of the field, which is here today and tomorrow is thrown into the fire, will he not much more clothe you—you of little faith? 31 So do not worry, saying, ‘What shall we eat?’ or ‘What shall we drink?’ or ‘What shall we wear?’ 32 For the pagans run after all these things, and your heavenly Father knows that you need them. 33 But seek first his kingdom and his righteousness, and all these things will be given to you as well.

dailies.label: Day 5
dailies.focus: Every good gift comes from our Father, who never changes.
dailies.verse: Every good and perfect gift is from above, coming down from the Father of the heavenly lights, who does not change like shifting shadows.
dailies.enoch: Name one toy or treat Enoch loves and say, "Thank you, God, for good gifts!"
dailies.elijah: Where do all good gifts come from, according to James 1:17?
dailies.elijahAnswer: From above, from the Father (James 1:17).
dailies.jordyn: James says the Father "does not change like shifting shadows." Why is that comforting?
dailies.jordynAnswer: Shadows move and change all day, and people's moods change too. God's love and goodness stay the same every day, so we can always count on him.
dailies.action: Thank-you challenge: each person thanks God for five good gifts before bed.
dailies.prayer: Father of the heavenly lights, thank you for every good and perfect gift: our family, our food, our home, and most of all new life through your word. Thank you that you never change. Help us notice your gifts and thank you for them. In Jesus' name, Amen.
dailies.teach: James was a leader in the early church, and he wrote this letter to help Christians live out their faith. He warns, "Don't be deceived": don't believe the lie that God is holding out on you. Every good and perfect gift comes from the Father, who made the lights in the sky. The sun and moon make shadows that shift and move all day, but God does not change; his goodness is the same every day. Verse 18 says he gave us new life through the word of truth, which is the best gift of all. It's a perfect passage for giving thanks, because every good thing on our table and in our home came from our Father's hand.
dailies.enochActivity: Go on a thank-you hunt: walk around the house and touch three good gifts, like your bed, your food, and your family. At each one, say, "Thank you, God!"
dailies.elijah2: Find it in the passage: In verse 17, what does James call God? Why does God never changing make him a good Father?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: The Father of the heavenly lights (verse 17). Because he does not change like shifting shadows, we can count on him to be good to us every single day.
dailies.jordyn2: Verse 16 begins, "Don't be deceived." What lie about God might people believe when life is hard? What is one good gift in your life you've been taking for granted?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: People can be tricked into thinking God isn't good or is holding out on them. James gives the truth: every good and perfect gift is from the Father, and he does not change (verse 17). Any honest answer works for the second part.
dailies.passageText: 16 Don’t be deceived, my dear brothers and sisters. 17 Every good and perfect gift is from above, coming down from the Father of the heavenly lights, who does not change like shifting shadows. 18 He chose to give us birth through the word of truth, that we might be a kind of firstfruits of all he created.

dailies.label: Day 6
dailies.focus: Jesus taught us to talk to God as our Father.
dailies.verse: "This, then, is how you should pray: 'Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name,
dailies.enoch: Fold hands and repeat after a parent: "Our Father in heaven."
dailies.elijah: What words did Jesus teach us to start our prayers with?
dailies.elijahAnswer: "Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name" (Matthew 6:9).
dailies.jordyn: "Hallowed" means treated as holy. Why do you think Jesus put "Father" and "holy" together right at the start?
dailies.jordynAnswer: God is close and loving like a Father, and he is also holy and great. We come to him with confidence and with respect at the same time.
dailies.action: Game: pass a ball around; whoever catches it says the next word of "Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name" until you finish it. Then each person prays one sentence starting with "Our Father."
dailies.prayer: Our Father in heaven, your name is holy. Thank you that we can come to you like children to a loving dad. Give us what we need today, forgive our sins, and help us forgive others. In Jesus' name, Amen.
dailies.teach: In the same mountainside teaching, Jesus showed his followers how to pray. He starts with "Our Father in heaven": we get to talk to the holy God of the universe as our Father. Then the prayer moves through what matters most: honoring God's name, asking for his kingdom and his will, asking for daily bread, asking forgiveness and forgiving others, and asking to be kept from evil. It isn't a set of words to rush through; it is a pattern for how children talk to their Father. Because God is our Father, we can come to him with anything, which is our big idea this week. Like a coach teaching the steps of a good swing, Jesus gives us the steps of a good prayer.
dailies.enochActivity: Make a prayer hand: fold down one finger at a time while a parent says, "Our Father... your name is holy... give us food... forgive us... keep us safe." Then fold your hands and say, "Amen!"
dailies.elijah2: Find it in the passage: In verse 11, what does Jesus tell us to ask for? Why do you think he says "today" and "daily"?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: "Give us today our daily bread" (verse 11). Asking today and every day teaches us to trust God one day at a time and to keep coming back to him.
dailies.jordyn2: Verse 12 asks God to forgive us "as we also have forgiven our debtors." Why do you think forgiving others is part of this prayer? Is there someone you need to forgive this week?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: People God has forgiven should forgive others; holding a grudge doesn't fit with asking God for mercy (verse 12). Any honest answer for the second part; she can ask God for help to forgive.
dailies.passageText: 9 “This, then, is how you should pray: “‘Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name, 10 your kingdom come, your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven. 11 Give us today our daily bread. 12 And forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors. 13 And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one.’

dailies.label: Day 7
dailies.focus: Recap: God the Father loves, cares for, and provides for his children, and we become his children by trusting Jesus.
dailies.verse: See what great love the Father has lavished on us, that we should be called children of God! And that is what we are!
dailies.enoch: Ask, "Who takes care of the birds?" (God!) "Who takes care of you?" (God!)
dailies.elijah: Name two ways God the Father takes care of his children that we learned this week.
dailies.elijahAnswer: He feeds us like the birds, gives good gifts, has compassion when we hurt, knows what we need, and listens when we pray.
dailies.jordyn: How do we become children of God, and why can no one earn it?
dailies.jordynAnswer: By receiving Jesus and believing in his name (John 1:12). It's a gift of God's love, because none of us is good enough on our own; we all need Jesus.
dailies.action: Read 1 John 3:1 together, then each person shares one thing they learned about God the Father this week. Next lesson: Jesus the Son.
dailies.prayer: Father, thank you for loving us, caring for us, giving us good gifts, and teaching us to pray. Thank you for sending Jesus so we could become your children. Help each of us receive him and live as your children. In Jesus' name, Amen.
dailies.teach: Today we look back at our week on God the Father. John's Gospel tells us that Jesus came into the world he made, but many people did not receive him. Yet to all who did receive him and believed in his name, he gave the right to become children of God. Verse 13 says these children are born of God, not because of their family or anything they did. That is why our key verse says, "See what great love the Father has lavished on us!" This week we saw the Father feed the birds, have compassion when we hurt, give good gifts, and teach us to pray, and the best news is that anyone who trusts Jesus is welcomed into his family.
dailies.enochActivity: Play "Who takes care of...?": a parent points to a bird, a flower, a toy, and then Enoch, and Enoch shouts "God!" each time. End with a big family hug.
dailies.elijah2: Find it in the passage: In verse 12, what does Jesus give to everyone who receives him and believes in his name? Why is that the best gift?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: The right to become children of God (verse 12). It's the best gift because we get to belong to God's family forever, with a Father who loves and cares for us.
dailies.jordyn2: Verse 11 says Jesus' own people did not receive him. Why do you think some people turn away from Jesus even when he comes to them? How could you show a friend this week what it looks like to be loved by the Father?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: Some people want to run their own lives, don't believe he is who he says, or don't see their need for him; verse 10 says the world did not recognize him. Any real idea works for the second part: kindness, honesty, staying calm when things go wrong, or inviting a friend to church.
dailies.passageText: 10 He was in the world, and though the world was made through him, the world did not recognize him. 11 He came to that which was his own, but his own did not receive him. 12 Yet to all who did receive him, to those who believed in his name, he gave the right to become children of God— 13 children born not of natural descent, nor of human decision or a husband’s will, but born of God.

weeks.title: Jesus the Son (Thanksgiving)
weeks.selectLabel: Week 4 · Jesus the Son (Thanksgiving)
weeks.nextUp: Week 5 · Advent: God promises a Savior (Isaiah 9:6)
weeks.bigIdea: Jesus is God the Son. He has always been God, and he became a person to save us. He is God's best gift, so we give thanks for him.
weeks.scheduleNote: This is the Week 4 family lesson. The short daily bites are Days 2–7.

howSteps.title: Read together
howSteps.detail: Open the Read tab and read the five short passages out loud. Let a different person read each one.

howSteps.title: Talk it through
howSteps.detail: Still on Read, walk through the kid-language explanation so everyone gets the picture.

howSteps.title: Age parts
howSteps.detail: Use Enoch, Elijah, and Jordyn tabs. Keep the Parent key open for yourself.

howSteps.title: Pray
howSteps.detail: Close with the short family prayer on the Prayer tab.

readings.text: 1 In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. 2 He was with God in the beginning. 3 Through him all things were made; without him nothing was made that has been made.
14 The Word became flesh and made his dwelling among us. We have seen his glory, the glory of the one and only Son, who came from the Father, full of grace and truth.
15 "But what about you?" he asked. "Who do you say I am?" 16 Simon Peter answered, "You are the Messiah, the Son of the living God."
16 For God so loved the world that he gave his one and only Son, that whoever believes in him shall not perish but have eternal life.
15 Thanks be to God for his indescribable gift!

story: Last week we learned about God the Father, who loves us and makes us his children. This week we get to know the second person of the one God: Jesus, God the Son.

John starts his book with something amazing: "In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God." "The Word" is a name for Jesus. Before there were any stars, oceans, or people, Jesus was already there with the Father. Nobody made Jesus. He has always been God, and "through him all things were made."

Then John says, "The Word became flesh and made his dwelling among us." That means God the Son became a real human being. He was born as a baby, grew up, got hungry and tired, and lived with people. Jesus is fully God and fully human at the same time.
One day Jesus asked his friends, "Who do you say I am?" Peter answered, "You are the Messiah, the Son of the living God." Messiah means the Savior God promised to send. Peter was right!

Why did the Son come? Because God loves us. "For God so loved the world that he gave his one and only Son, that whoever believes in him shall not perish but have eternal life." Jesus came to save us from our sin, so that everyone who trusts him can live with God forever.

That is the best gift anyone has ever been given. When we give thanks, the Bible gives us the biggest thank-you of all: "Thanks be to God for his indescribable gift!" Indescribable means so great that words can't fully describe it. That gift is Jesus.
weeks.enochLine: Jesus is God's Son, and he came to save me!
enochActivities: Activity: Gift box. Wrap a small box (or cover a shoebox with a blanket) and put a drawing of baby Jesus or a cross inside. Let Enoch open it and say together, "Jesus is God's best gift!"

Thank-you circle: take turns naming things to thank God for. Every time it's Enoch's turn, he ends with, "Thank you, God, for Jesus!" Paw Patrol touch: when someone needs help, the pups come running. God the Son came all the way from heaven to help and save us.
elijahQuestions: John 1:1 says, "In the beginning was the Word." Who is the Word? Was he there before the world was made?
John 1:14 says, "The Word became flesh." What does that mean Jesus did?
When Jesus asked, "Who do you say I am?", what did Peter answer?
In John 3:16, why did God give his Son, and what does everyone who believes in him get?
jordynQuestions: John 1:1 says the Word was "with God" and the Word "was God." How does that fit with what we learned in Week 2 about one God in three persons?
