howSteps.detail: Use Enoch, Elijah, and Jordyn tabs. Keep the Parent key open for yourself.

howSteps.title: Pray
howSteps.detail: Close with the short family prayer on the Prayer tab.

readings.text: 18 This is how the birth of Jesus the Messiah came about: His mother Mary was pledged to be married to Joseph, but before they came together, she was found to be pregnant through the Holy Spirit. 19 Because Joseph her husband was faithful to the law, and yet did not want to expose her to public disgrace, he had in mind to divorce her quietly. 20 But after he had considered this, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream and said, "Joseph son of David, do not be afraid to take Mary home as your wife, because what is conceived in her is from the Holy Spirit. 21 She will give birth to a son, and you are to give him the name Jesus, because he will save his people from their sins."

22 All this took place to fulfill what the Lord had said through the prophet: 23 "The virgin will conceive and give birth to a son, and they will call him Immanuel" (which means "God with us"). 24 When Joseph woke up, he did what the angel of the Lord had commanded him and took Mary home as his wife. 25 But he did not consummate their marriage until she gave birth to a son. And he gave him the name Jesus.
14 Therefore the Lord himself will give you a sign: The virgin will conceive and give birth to a son, and will call him Immanuel.

story: Last week we learned that the angel Gabriel visited Mary and told her she would have a baby named Jesus, the Son of God. This week we hear the other half of the story: what God told Joseph.

Joseph was the man Mary was pledged to marry, and he came from King David's family. When Joseph found out Mary was going to have a baby, he knew he was not the father. He did not know yet that the baby was from the Holy Spirit. Joseph was faithful to God's law, but he was also kind, so he planned to end the engagement quietly instead of embarrassing Mary in front of everyone.

Then God stepped in. While Joseph was asleep, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream and said, "Joseph son of David, do not be afraid to take Mary home as your wife, because what is conceived in her is from the Holy Spirit." The angel told Joseph to name the baby Jesus, "because he will save his people from their sins." The name Jesus means that the LORD saves.

Matthew tells us this happened to keep a promise God made long ago through the prophet Isaiah, the same promise we read last week: "The virgin will conceive and give birth to a son, and they will call him Immanuel." Immanuel means "God with us." Jesus is not just a good man sent from God; he is God himself, come to be with us.

When Joseph woke up, he did exactly what the angel of the Lord had told him. He took Mary home as his wife, and when the baby was born, Joseph gave him the name Jesus. Joseph trusted God and obeyed right away. Next week, at Christmas, we will read about the night Jesus was born and the shepherds who came to see him.
weeks.enochLine: An angel told Joseph in a dream, "Name the baby Jesus!" Jesus is God with us!
enochActivities: Activity: Dream and wake up. Enoch lies down and pretends to sleep like Joseph. A parent is the angel and whispers, "Do not be afraid! Name the baby Jesus!" Enoch jumps up and says, "Okay, God! I'll obey!"

God with us hug: a parent says, "Who is with us at home?" Enoch says, "God!" "Who is with us in the car?" "God!" "Who is with us when we sleep?" "God!" End with a big family hug and say together, "Jesus is God with us!" Paw Patrol touch: the pups are always ready to help, but Jesus is with us every single minute.
elijahQuestions: Who was Mary pledged to be married to (verse 18)?
How did the angel of the Lord talk to Joseph (verse 20)?
Why was the baby supposed to be named Jesus (verse 21)?
What does the name Immanuel mean (verse 23)?
jordynQuestions: Joseph was "faithful to the law, and yet did not want to expose her to public disgrace" (verse 19). What does that show about the kind of man Joseph was, even before the angel came?
The angel said Jesus "will save his people from their sins" (verse 21). Why is being saved from sin a bigger rescue than being saved from enemies or hard times?
Matthew says the name Immanuel means "God with us" (verse 23). How is Jesus being God with us different from God just sending a message or a helper?
weeks.jordynApplication: Joseph did not argue or put it off. "When Joseph woke up, he did what the angel of the Lord had commanded him" (verse 24), even though people might talk and his plans would change. God speaks to us today through the Bible. This week, when you know what God wants, like being kind, telling the truth, or obeying your parents, try doing it right away instead of later, at school, at volleyball, or at home. And when you feel alone or nervous, remember Jesus' name, Immanuel: God is with you.
elijahAnswers: Joseph (verse 18).
In a dream: "an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream" (verse 20).
Because "he will save his people from their sins" (verse 21).
"God with us" (verse 23).
jordynAnswers: He wanted to do what was right by God's law, but he was also kind and gentle. He did not want to hurt or shame Mary, so he planned to act quietly (verse 19). He loved God and cared about people.

Enemies and hard times hurt us for a while, but sin separates us from God, and we can't fix it ourselves. Jesus came to rescue us from sin itself, so we can be forgiven and belong to God forever (verse 21).
A message or helper would come from God, but Jesus is God himself who came to be with us (verse 23). God didn't stay far away; he came close, became a baby, and lived among us.
weeks.applicationCheck: Ask her later in the week about a time she obeyed God or a parent right away, like Joseph, and how it went. Notice and thank her when she does what is asked the first time.
weeks.prayer: Dear God, thank you for sending an angel to Joseph and for keeping your promise through Isaiah. Thank you for Jesus, who came to save us from our sins, and for being Immanuel, God with us. Help us trust you and obey right away like Joseph did. Remind us that you are always with us, at home, at school, and everywhere we go. In Jesus' name, Amen.

dailies.label: Day 2
dailies.focus: God sent an angel to Joseph in a dream to tell him that Mary's baby was from the Holy Spirit and would save his people from their sins.
dailies.verse: She will give birth to a son, and you are to give him the name Jesus, because he will save his people from their sins.
dailies.enoch: Say with a parent, "The angel said, 'Do not be afraid!' Jesus will save us!"
dailies.elijah: In verse 20, how did the angel of the Lord appear to Joseph?
dailies.elijahAnswer: In a dream: "an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream" (verse 20).
dailies.jordyn: Joseph planned to "divorce her quietly" (verse 19). Why do you think he wanted to do it quietly instead of in front of everyone?
dailies.jordynAnswer: Joseph was faithful to the law, but he did not want to expose Mary to public disgrace (verse 19). He was kind and wanted to protect her from shame, even when he was confused and hurt.
dailies.action: Read verses 20–21 together. Each person says one thing the angel told Joseph.
dailies.prayer: Lord God, thank you for speaking to Joseph when he was worried and did not understand. Thank you that Jesus came to save us from our sins. When we feel worried or confused, help us listen to you and not be afraid. In Jesus' name, Amen.
dailies.teach: Joseph was pledged to marry Mary, and he came from King David's family. Then he found out Mary was going to have a baby, and he knew it was not his. Joseph was faithful to God's law, but he was also kind, so he planned to end the engagement quietly so Mary would not be shamed in front of everyone. Before he did, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream and said, "Joseph son of David, do not be afraid." The angel explained that the baby was from the Holy Spirit and told Joseph to name him Jesus, "because he will save his people from their sins." Last week Mary heard the news from Gabriel; this week God made sure Joseph knew too.
dailies.enochActivity: Lie down and pretend to sleep like Joseph. When a parent whispers, "Do not be afraid!", pop up and say, "Jesus will save us!"
dailies.elijah2: Find it in the passage: In verse 21, what name was Joseph supposed to give the baby? Why that name?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: Jesus, because "he will save his people from their sins" (verse 21).
dailies.jordyn2: The angel called him "Joseph son of David" (verse 20). Why would that matter, remembering what Gabriel told Mary last week about David's throne (Luke 1:32)?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: Gabriel said God would give Jesus "the throne of his father David" (Luke 1:32). Joseph was from David's family, so when he took Mary home and named Jesus, Jesus became part of David's royal family line, just as God promised.
dailies.passageText: 18 This is how the birth of Jesus the Messiah came about: His mother Mary was pledged to be married to Joseph, but before they came together, she was found to be pregnant through the Holy Spirit. 19 Because Joseph her husband was faithful to the law, and yet did not want to expose her to public disgrace, he had in mind to divorce her quietly. 20 But after he had considered this, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream and said, “Joseph son of David, do not be afraid to take Mary home as your wife, because what is conceived in her is from the Holy Spirit. 21 She will give birth to a son, and you are to give him the name Jesus, because he will save his people from their sins.”

dailies.label: Day 3
dailies.focus: Jesus is Immanuel, which means God with us, so God is with us everywhere we go.
dailies.verse: "The virgin will conceive and give birth to a son, and they will call him Immanuel" (which means "God with us").
dailies.enoch: Play "Is God with us?" A parent asks, "Is God with us at the park?" Enoch shouts, "Yes! Jesus is God with us!"
dailies.elijah: Game: Where is God? Take turns naming a place (school, the baseball field, the car, your bed at night). Everyone answers, "God is with us there!" Then: what does Immanuel mean in verse 23?
dailies.elijahAnswer: "God with us" (verse 23).
dailies.jordyn: Verse 22 says "All this took place to fulfill what the Lord had said through the prophet." What does fulfill mean here, and which promise from last week came true?
dailies.jordynAnswer: Fulfill means to make a promise come true. The promise from Isaiah 7:14, that the virgin would give birth to a son called Immanuel, came true when Jesus was born to Mary (verses 22–23).
dailies.action: Play the "Where is God?" game, then read verse 23 together and say "God with us!" in your loudest voice.
dailies.prayer: God, thank you that Jesus is Immanuel, God with us. Thank you that we are never alone, at home, at school, on the field, or in our beds at night. When we feel scared or lonely, help us remember that you are right here. In Jesus' name, Amen.
dailies.teach: Matthew wanted his readers to know that Jesus' birth was not a surprise to God. He wrote, "All this took place to fulfill what the Lord had said through the prophet." That prophet was Isaiah, and the promise is the one we read last week: the virgin will give birth to a son, and they will call him Immanuel. Matthew tells us what Immanuel means: "God with us." That is the biggest news of Christmas. God did not just send a message from far away; in Jesus, God himself came to be with his people. Because Jesus is God with us, the people who trust him are never alone.
dailies.enochActivity: Play hide-and-seek with a parent. When you are found, shout, "God is with me everywhere!"
dailies.elijah2: Find it in the passage: In verse 22, who had said this would happen long ago?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: The Lord had said it "through the prophet" (verse 22). The prophet was Isaiah (Isaiah 7:14).
dailies.jordyn2: Matthew explains that the name Immanuel means "God with us" (verse 23). When is a time you might need to remember that God is with you? How could that change how you act?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: Any honest answer works, like a hard test, a big game, a new place, or feeling left out. Remembering that God is with us (verse 23) can help us be brave, calm, and kind instead of afraid.
dailies.passageText: 22 All this took place to fulfill what the Lord had said through the prophet: 23 “The virgin will conceive and give birth to a son, and they will call him Immanuel” (which means “God with us”).

dailies.label: Day 4
dailies.focus: Jesus came from the family of Abraham and David, just as God had planned for many generations.
dailies.verse: This is the genealogy of Jesus the Messiah the son of David, the son of Abraham:
dailies.enoch: Say with a parent, "Jesus is from King David's family!"
dailies.elijah: In verse 1, Jesus is called the son of which two people?
dailies.elijahAnswer: He is called "the son of David, the son of Abraham" (verse 1).
dailies.jordyn: Verse 17 counts fourteen generations, three times. What does that long family list show about God's plan for Jesus?
dailies.jordynAnswer: It shows God was working through many generations, from Abraham to David to the exile to the Messiah (verse 17). Jesus' coming was planned and carried out by God over a very long time; nothing was an accident.
dailies.action: Count to fourteen together three times, once for each part of verse 17. Then talk about one person in your own family who taught you about God.
dailies.prayer: Lord, thank you that you planned for Jesus to come for a very long time, through Abraham and David and many families. Thank you that you keep your promises from generation to generation. Help our family love and follow you, and pass our faith on to the people after us. In Jesus' name, Amen.
dailies.teach: Matthew starts his book with a long family tree, called a genealogy. It begins, "This is the genealogy of Jesus the Messiah the son of David, the son of Abraham." God had promised Abraham long ago that the whole world would be blessed through his family, and he promised King David that one of his sons would rule forever. Matthew lists the generations one by one, all the way to Joseph, the husband of Mary, and Jesus, who is called the Messiah. Then he counts them: fourteen generations, three times. Messiah means the Chosen King God promised to send. Jesus' family tree shows that God kept his word, step by step, through hundreds of years.
dailies.enochActivity: Stack fourteen blocks into a tall tower and say, "God planned Jesus for a long, long time!"
dailies.elijah2: Find it in the passage: In verse 16, who was Joseph's wife, and who was her son?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: Mary was Joseph's wife, and her son was "Jesus who is called the Messiah" (verse 16).
dailies.jordyn2: Matthew calls Jesus "the son of David, the son of Abraham" (verse 1). Why do you think Matthew started with those two names instead of just saying Jesus was born?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: God made big promises to Abraham and to David, and the Messiah was supposed to come from their families. Starting with them shows right away that Jesus is the promised one and that God kept those promises (verses 1, 17).
dailies.passageText: 1 This is the genealogy of Jesus the Messiah the son of David, the son of Abraham: 2 Abraham was the father of Isaac, Isaac the father of Jacob, Jacob the father of Judah and his brothers, 16 and Jacob the father of Joseph, the husband of Mary, and Mary was the mother of Jesus who is called the Messiah. 17 Thus there were fourteen generations in all from Abraham to David, fourteen from David to the exile to Babylon, and fourteen from the exile to the Messiah.

dailies.label: Day 5
dailies.focus: When Joseph woke up, he obeyed God right away, and we can obey God right away too.
dailies.verse: When Joseph woke up, he did what the angel of the Lord had commanded him and took Mary home as his wife.
dailies.enoch: Play "Right away!" A parent gives a simple job, like "Touch your nose!" Enoch does it fast and says, "I obey right away, like Joseph!"
dailies.elijah: In verse 24, what did Joseph do when he woke up?
dailies.elijahAnswer: He did what the angel of the Lord had commanded him and took Mary home as his wife (verse 24).
dailies.jordyn: Joseph obeyed as soon as he woke up (verse 24). What might have made it hard for him to obey, and why do you think he did it anyway?
dailies.jordynAnswer: People might not understand, and his own plans had changed (verse 19). He obeyed because he trusted that God's message was true and that God's plan was good (verses 20–21, 24).
dailies.action: Challenge: Today, when a parent asks you to do something, do it the first time, right away, like Joseph. At bedtime, share one time you obeyed right away.
dailies.prayer: Lord, thank you for Joseph, who trusted you and obeyed right away. Help us hear what you say in the Bible and do it without arguing or waiting. Give us brave, willing hearts to follow you, even when it is hard. In Jesus' name, Amen.
dailies.teach: Joseph had a big choice to make when he woke up from his dream. He could keep his old plan, or he could trust what the angel of the Lord had told him. Matthew says, "When Joseph woke up, he did what the angel of the Lord had commanded him and took Mary home as his wife." He did not argue, wait, or ask for more time. Later, when the baby was born, Joseph gave him the name Jesus, just as the angel said. The Bible praises this kind of obedience; Psalm 119:60 says, "I will hasten and not delay to obey your commands." Joseph shows us that trusting God and obeying God go together.
dailies.enochActivity: Run to a parent as fast as you can when they call your name, and say, "I'm here! I'll obey!"
dailies.elijah2: Find it in the passage: In verse 25, what name did Joseph give the baby? Was that the name the angel told him?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: Jesus (verse 25). Yes, it was the name the angel told him to give (verse 21).
dailies.jordyn2: Psalm 119:60 says, "I will hasten and not delay to obey your commands." What is one thing you know God wants you to do that you have been putting off? What would obeying right away look like this week?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: Any honest answer works, like apologizing to someone, doing chores without being reminded, or being kind to a sibling. Joseph obeyed as soon as he woke up (verse 24), and quick obedience shows we trust God.
dailies.passageText: 24 When Joseph woke up, he did what the angel of the Lord had commanded him and took Mary home as his wife. 25 But he did not consummate their marriage until she gave birth to a son. And he gave him the name Jesus.

dailies.label: Day 6
dailies.focus: At Christmas we celebrate that Jesus, the Word, became a person and came to live with us, full of grace and truth.
dailies.verse: The Word became flesh and made his dwelling among us. We have seen his glory, the glory of the one and only Son, who came from the Father, full of grace and truth.
dailies.enoch: Pray with a parent, "Thank you, God, for baby Jesus! Happy birthday, Jesus!"
dailies.elijah: In verse 14, what did the Word become?
dailies.elijahAnswer: Flesh, which means a real human person. "The Word became flesh and made his dwelling among us" (verse 14).
dailies.jordyn: Verse 12 says those who receive Jesus and believe in his name get "the right to become children of God." How does that connect to the name Immanuel?
dailies.jordynAnswer: Immanuel means God with us (Matthew 1:23). Jesus came close to us (verse 14) so we could come close to God and become his children by believing in him (verse 12).
dailies.action: Prayer time: Light a candle or turn on the tree lights. Read verse 14 together, then each person thanks God for one thing about Jesus coming to us.
dailies.prayer: Father, thank you for sending Jesus, the Word, to become a person and live among us. Thank you that he is full of grace and truth and that everyone who receives him becomes your child. As we celebrate Christmas, fill our home with joy and help us welcome Jesus with our whole hearts. In Jesus' name, Amen.
dailies.teach: John tells the Christmas story in a different way from Matthew and Luke. He calls Jesus "the Word," the one through whom the whole world was made. Then he says something amazing: "The Word became flesh and made his dwelling among us." That means God the Son became a real human baby and lived with people, just like the name Immanuel says. Sadly, many people did not recognize or receive him. But everyone who receives Jesus and believes in his name is given the right to become a child of God. That is the best gift of Christmas, and today we thank God for it in prayer.
dailies.enochActivity: Hold a pretend present, open it slowly, and say, "Jesus is God's best gift!"
dailies.elijah2: Find it in the passage: In verse 12, what did Jesus give to all who received him and believed in his name?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: He gave them "the right to become children of God" (verse 12).
dailies.jordyn2: Verses 10–11 say the world did not recognize Jesus and his own did not receive him. Why do you think people miss Jesus, even at Christmas? How can your family make room for Jesus this Christmas?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: People can be busy, distracted, or not want to change, so they miss him (verses 10–11). Any real answer works for the second part, like reading the Christmas story together, praying before opening gifts, or serving someone in need.
dailies.passageText: 10 He was in the world, and though the world was made through him, the world did not recognize him. 11 He came to that which was his own, but his own did not receive him. 12 Yet to all who did receive him, to those who believed in his name, he gave the right to become children of God— 13 children born not of natural descent, nor of human decision or a husband’s will, but born of God. 14 The Word became flesh and made his dwelling among us. We have seen his glory, the glory of the one and only Son, who came from the Father, full of grace and truth.

dailies.label: Day 7
dailies.focus: Recap: God told Joseph in a dream that Mary's baby was from the Holy Spirit; Jesus saves us from our sins and is Immanuel, God with us.
dailies.verse: "The virgin will conceive and give birth to a son, and they will call him Immanuel" (which means "God with us").
dailies.enoch: Ask, "Who had a dream?" (Joseph!) "What does Immanuel mean?" (God with us!)
dailies.elijah: Name two things the angel told Joseph in his dream this week.
dailies.elijahAnswer: Any two: do not be afraid to take Mary home as your wife (verse 20); the baby is from the Holy Spirit (verse 20); she will give birth to a son (verse 21); name him Jesus (verse 21); he will save his people from their sins (verse 21).
dailies.jordyn: This week we read Matthew 1, Isaiah 7:14, and John 1. What does the whole week show about who Jesus is?
dailies.jordynAnswer: Jesus is the son of David and son of Abraham God promised (Matthew 1:1), the Savior who saves his people from their sins (Matthew 1:21), and Immanuel, God with us (Matthew 1:23), the Word who became flesh (John 1:14). God planned it long ago and kept his word (Isaiah 7:14).
dailies.action: Read verses 20–23 together, then each person shares one thing they learned about Joseph or about Jesus this week. Next lesson: Christmas: Jesus is born, the shepherds.
dailies.prayer: Father, thank you for telling Joseph the good news and for keeping your promise through Isaiah. Thank you that Jesus saves us from our sins and that he is Immanuel, God with us. Help us trust you and obey right away like Joseph. Thank you that you are with us always. In Jesus' name, Amen.
dailies.teach: Today we look back at our week. Joseph found out Mary was going to have a baby and planned to end their engagement quietly, but an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream. The angel said the baby was from the Holy Spirit and that Joseph should name him Jesus, because he will save his people from their sins. Matthew shows this kept God's promise through Isaiah, that the virgin's son would be called Immanuel, which means "God with us." When Joseph woke up, he obeyed right away. At the very end of Matthew's book, Jesus promises, "And surely I am with you always, to the very end of the age." Next week we will read about the night Jesus was born and the shepherds who came to see him.
dailies.enochActivity: Act out the story: a parent is the angel and whispers in Enoch's ear while he pretends to sleep, "Name the baby Jesus!" Enoch wakes up, rocks a pretend baby, and says, "Jesus, God with us!"
dailies.elijah2: Find it in the passage: In verse 24, what did Joseph do when he woke up? What does that show about him?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: He did what the angel of the Lord had commanded him and took Mary home as his wife (verse 24). It shows he trusted God and obeyed right away.
dailies.jordyn2: Last week Mary said, "I am the Lord's servant" (Luke 1:38), and this week Joseph obeyed as soon as he woke up (verse 24). What do Mary and Joseph teach you about trusting God, and where do you want to trust him more?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: Both believed God's message and obeyed even when it was hard and people might not understand (Luke 1:38; Matthew 1:24). Any honest answer works for the second part; God is with us as we learn to trust him (verse 23).
dailies.passageText: 18 This is how the birth of Jesus the Messiah came about: His mother Mary was pledged to be married to Joseph, but before they came together, she was found to be pregnant through the Holy Spirit. 19 Because Joseph her husband was faithful to the law, and yet did not want to expose her to public disgrace, he had in mind to divorce her quietly. 20 But after he had considered this, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream and said, “Joseph son of David, do not be afraid to take Mary home as your wife, because what is conceived in her is from the Holy Spirit. 21 She will give birth to a son, and you are to give him the name Jesus, because he will save his people from their sins.” 22 All this took place to fulfill what the Lord had said through the prophet: 23 “The virgin will conceive and give birth to a son, and they will call him Immanuel” (which means “God with us”). 24 When Joseph woke up, he did what the angel of the Lord had commanded him and took Mary home as his wife. 25 But he did not consummate their marriage until she gave birth to a son. And he gave him the name Jesus.

weeks.planTitle: Christmas: Jesus is born, the shepherds
weeks.title: Christmas: Jesus is born, the shepherds
weeks.selectLabel: Week 8 · Christmas: Jesus is born, the shepherds
weeks.nextUp: Week 9 · The wise men worship Jesus
weeks.bigIdea: Jesus, the Savior God promised, was born in Bethlehem and laid in a manger, and the angels told the shepherds this good news of great joy for all the people, so they hurried to see him and went home praising God.
weeks.scheduleNote: This is the Week 8 family lesson. The short daily bites are Days 2–7.

howSteps.title: Read together
howSteps.detail: Open the Read tab and read Luke 2:1–20 out loud in three parts: the birth, the angels and the shepherds, and the shepherds' visit. Let a different person read each part.

howSteps.title: Talk it through
howSteps.detail: Still on Read, walk through the kid-language explanation so everyone gets the picture.

howSteps.title: Age parts
howSteps.detail: Use Enoch, Elijah, and Jordyn tabs. Keep the Parent key open for yourself.

howSteps.title: Pray
howSteps.detail: Close with the short family prayer on the Prayer tab.

readings.text: 1 In those days Caesar Augustus issued a decree that a census should be taken of the entire Roman world. 2 (This was the first census that took place while Quirinius was governor of Syria.) 3 And everyone went to their own town to register. 4 So Joseph also went up from the town of Nazareth in Galilee to Judea, to Bethlehem the town of David, because he belonged to the house and line of David. 5 He went there to register with Mary, who was pledged to be married to him and was expecting a child. 6 While they were there, the time came for the baby to be born, 7 and she gave birth to her firstborn, a son. She wrapped him in cloths and placed him in a manger, because there was no guest room available for them.

8 And there were shepherds living out in the fields nearby, keeping watch over their flocks at night. 9 An angel of the Lord appeared to them, and the glory of the Lord shone around them, and they were terrified. 10 But the angel said to them, "Do not be afraid. I bring you good news that will cause great joy for all the people. 11 Today in the town of David a Savior has been born to you; he is the Messiah, the Lord. 12 This will be a sign to you: You will find a baby wrapped in cloths and lying in a manger." 13 Suddenly a great company of the heavenly host appeared with the angel, praising God and saying, 14 "Glory to God in the highest heaven, and on earth peace to those on whom his favor rests."

15 When the angels had left them and gone into heaven, the shepherds said to one another, "Let's go to Bethlehem and see this thing that has happened, which the Lord has told us about." 16 So they hurried off and found Mary and Joseph, and the baby, who was lying in the manger. 17 When they had seen him, they spread the word concerning what had been told them about this child, 18 and all who heard it were amazed at what the shepherds said to them. 19 But Mary treasured up all these things and pondered them in her heart. 20 The shepherds returned, glorifying and praising God for all the things they had heard and seen, which were just as they had been told.

story: Last week an angel told Joseph in a dream to take Mary home as his wife and to name her baby Jesus, because he will save his people from their sins. This week we read about the night Jesus was born.

The ruler of the Roman world, Caesar Augustus, ordered a census, which means everyone had to be counted. Each person went to their own town to sign up. Joseph belonged to King David's family, so he traveled with Mary from Nazareth to Bethlehem, the town of David. Mary was expecting her baby, and while they were in Bethlehem, Jesus was born. There was no guest room for them, so Mary wrapped baby Jesus in cloths and laid him in a manger, the box animals eat from.

That same night, shepherds were out in the fields keeping watch over their sheep. Suddenly an angel of the Lord appeared, and the glory of the Lord shone around them. They were terrified! But the angel said, "Do not be afraid. I bring you good news that will cause great joy for all the people." The Savior had been born in the town of David. He is the Messiah, the Lord. The sign was a baby wrapped in cloths and lying in a manger.

Then a great company of angels appeared, praising God and saying, "Glory to God in the highest heaven, and on earth peace to those on whom his favor rests." The King of heaven was not born in a palace. God chose to send his Son as a tiny baby in a humble place, and he told the good news first to ordinary shepherds.

The shepherds said, "Let's go to Bethlehem and see this thing that has happened, which the Lord has told us about." They hurried off and found Mary, Joseph, and the baby lying in the manger, just as the angel said. Then they told everyone what they had heard about this child, and people were amazed. Mary treasured all these things in her heart. The shepherds went back to their fields glorifying and praising God. Next week we will read about the wise men who followed a star to worship Jesus.
weeks.enochLine: Baby Jesus was born! The angels sang, and the shepherds came to see him!
enochActivities: Activity: Shepherds and angels. Enoch is a shepherd watching pretend sheep (stuffed animals). A parent is the angel and says, "Do not be afraid! Jesus is born!" Enoch hurries across the room to a blanket "manger" with a baby doll inside and says, "I found baby Jesus!"
Glory song: hold hands, raise them high, and sing or say together, "Glory to God! Glory to God! Jesus is born!" Then tiptoe and whisper, "Shh, baby Jesus is sleeping in the manger."
elijahQuestions: What town did Joseph and Mary go to (verse 4)?
Where did Mary lay baby Jesus, and why (verse 7)?
Who did the angel visit that night, and what were they doing (verse 8)?
What did the shepherds do after they saw Jesus (verses 17 and 20)?
jordynQuestions: Jesus is the King, but he was born where there was no guest room and laid in a manger (verse 7). What does that show you about the kind of King Jesus is?
The angel brought the news first to shepherds out in the fields at night (verses 8–11). Why do you think God told ordinary working people first instead of kings or important leaders?
The angel called Jesus "a Savior," "the Messiah," and "the Lord" (verse 11). What does each name tell you about who Jesus is?
weeks.jordynApplication: The shepherds didn't keep the good news to themselves. "When they had seen him, they spread the word concerning what had been told them about this child" (verse 17), and then they went back to their regular work "glorifying and praising God" (verse 20). This week, look for one chance to share something true about Jesus, with a friend, a teammate, or a cousin over the holidays, even something simple like why your family celebrates Christmas. And when you go back to ordinary things like chores or practice, try doing them with a thankful heart, like the shepherds.
elijahAnswers: Bethlehem, the town of David (verse 4).
In a manger, "because there was no guest room available for them" (verse 7).
Shepherds. They were "living out in the fields nearby, keeping watch over their flocks at night" (verse 8).
They spread the word about this child (verse 17), and they went back "glorifying and praising God" (verse 20).
jordynAnswers: Jesus is a humble King. He didn't come with power and riches to be served; he came low and gentle, close to ordinary people (verse 7).

God's good news is for everyone, not just the rich or important. The angel said it was "good news that will cause great joy for all the people" (verse 10). Shepherds were ordinary workers, and God chose them to hear it first and tell others.
Savior means he rescues us from sin. Messiah means he is the promised King God chose. Lord means he is God and rules over everything (verse 11). Jesus is all three at once.
weeks.applicationCheck: Ask her later in the week if she had a chance to share something about Jesus with anyone, and how it went. Thank her for any small step, even just being ready to answer.
weeks.prayer: Dear God, thank you for sending Jesus, our Savior, to be born in Bethlehem. Thank you for the good news of great joy for all the people, including our family. Help us hurry to Jesus like the shepherds and tell others what we know about him. Fill our home with praise this Christmas season. In Jesus' name, Amen.

dailies.label: Day 2
dailies.focus: God brought Joseph and Mary to Bethlehem, the town of David, and there Jesus was born and laid in a manger.
dailies.verse: and she gave birth to her firstborn, a son. She wrapped him in cloths and placed him in a manger, because there was no guest room available for them.
dailies.enoch: Say with a parent, "Baby Jesus slept in a manger!"
dailies.elijah: In verse 4, what town did Joseph and Mary travel to?
dailies.elijahAnswer: Bethlehem, "the town of David" (verse 4).
dailies.jordyn: Caesar Augustus ordered the census (verse 1), but it brought Joseph and Mary to Bethlehem right when Jesus was born. What does that show you about God being in charge, even of rulers?
dailies.jordynAnswer: A ruler gave the order, but God used it to bring Mary and Joseph to Bethlehem, the town of David, just in time (verses 1–6). God is in charge even of powerful rulers and works through everything to keep his promises.
dailies.action: Read verses 4–7 together. Then find a small box or basket and talk about how Jesus, the King, was laid in a manger.
dailies.prayer: Lord God, thank you that you are in charge of everything and that you brought Joseph and Mary to Bethlehem just as you planned. Thank you that Jesus came as a humble baby for us. Help us trust you when plans change and things feel hard. In Jesus' name, Amen.
dailies.teach: Last week Joseph obeyed God and took Mary home as his wife. Now the ruler Caesar Augustus ordered a census, so everyone had to go to their own town to be counted. Joseph belonged to the house and line of David, so he and Mary traveled from Nazareth to Bethlehem, the town of David. While they were there, it was time for the baby to be born. Mary wrapped her firstborn son in cloths and placed him in a manger, a feeding box for animals, because there was no guest room for them. The King of all creation started his life on earth in a very humble place.
dailies.enochActivity: Wrap a baby doll or stuffed animal snugly in a small blanket and lay it in a box or basket. Say, "Jesus is the King, and he slept in a manger!"
dailies.elijah2: Find it in the passage: In verse 7, why did Mary place baby Jesus in a manger?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: "Because there was no guest room available for them" (verse 7).
dailies.jordyn2: Verse 4 says Joseph "belonged to the house and line of David." Why does it matter that Jesus was born in Bethlehem, the town of David?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: Jesus was born in David's town because he is from David's family line (verse 4). Bethlehem is called "the town of David" twice in this chapter (verses 4 and 11), which shows Jesus is the promised King from David's family.
dailies.passageText: 1 In those days Caesar Augustus issued a decree that a census should be taken of the entire Roman world. 2 (This was the first census that took place while Quirinius was governor of Syria.) 3 And everyone went to their own town to register. 4 So Joseph also went up from the town of Nazareth in Galilee to Judea, to Bethlehem the town of David, because he belonged to the house and line of David. 5 He went there to register with Mary, who was pledged to be married to him and was expecting a child. 6 While they were there, the time came for the baby to be born, 7 and she gave birth to her firstborn, a son. She wrapped him in cloths and placed him in a manger, because there was no guest room available for them.

dailies.label: Day 3
dailies.focus: An angel told the shepherds not to be afraid, because he brought good news of great joy for all the people.
dailies.verse: Do not be afraid. I bring you good news that will cause great joy for all the people.
dailies.enoch: Play "Do not be afraid!" Enoch hides behind a pillow like a scared shepherd. A parent says, "Do not be afraid! Good news!" Enoch pops up and shouts, "Jesus is born!"
dailies.elijah: Game: Shepherd's watch. One person is the shepherd and guards a few stuffed-animal sheep while everyone else tries to sneak up. When the shepherd says "Angel!", everyone freezes and the shepherd says verse 10. Then: what did the angel tell the shepherds not to be?
dailies.elijahAnswer: Afraid: "Do not be afraid" (verse 10).
dailies.jordyn: The shepherds "were terrified" when the glory of the Lord shone around them (verse 9). Why do you think the angel's first words were "Do not be afraid"?
dailies.jordynAnswer: God's glory is so great and holy that people are afraid when they see it (verse 9). But the angel came with good news, not to harm them, so he calmed them first: "Do not be afraid" (verse 10). Jesus came so people could come close to God without fear.
dailies.action: Play Shepherd's watch, then read verses 10–11 together and say "Good news of great joy!" together.
dailies.prayer: God, thank you that the angel's message was good news of great joy for all the people. Thank you that because of Jesus, we don't have to be afraid of you. When we feel scared, help us remember your good news. In Jesus' name, Amen.
dailies.teach: On the night Jesus was born, shepherds were living out in the fields near Bethlehem, keeping watch over their sheep in the dark. Suddenly an angel of the Lord appeared, and the glory of the Lord shone around them. The shepherds were terrified! But the angel said, "Do not be afraid." He brought good news that would cause great joy for all the people: a Savior had been born in the town of David, the Messiah, the Lord. Then the angel gave them a sign so they would know they had found the right baby: he would be wrapped in cloths and lying in a manger. Yesterday we read that Mary laid Jesus in a manger, and today God told the shepherds exactly where to look.
dailies.enochActivity: Turn off the lights, then shine a flashlight on the ceiling like the glory of the Lord. Enoch says, "Do not be afraid! Jesus is born!"
dailies.elijah2: Find it in the passage: In verse 12, what sign did the angel give the shepherds so they could find the baby?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: "You will find a baby wrapped in cloths and lying in a manger" (verse 12).
dailies.jordyn2: The angel said the good news was "for all the people" (verse 10) and that the Savior was "born to you" (verse 11). Why is it important that Jesus came for everyone, and also for you personally?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: "For all the people" means no one is left out of God's good news (verse 10). "Born to you" means it is personal: Jesus came for each person who hears, including you (verse 11). He is not just the world's Savior; he can be your Savior.
dailies.passageText: 8 And there were shepherds living out in the fields nearby, keeping watch over their flocks at night. 9 An angel of the Lord appeared to them, and the glory of the Lord shone around them, and they were terrified. 10 But the angel said to them, “Do not be afraid. I bring you good news that will cause great joy for all the people. 11 Today in the town of David a Savior has been born to you; he is the Messiah, the Lord. 12 This will be a sign to you: You will find a baby wrapped in cloths and lying in a manger.”

dailies.label: Day 4
dailies.focus: A great company of angels praised God for sending Jesus, giving glory to God and announcing peace to those on whom his favor rests.
dailies.verse: "Glory to God in the highest heaven, and on earth peace to those on whom his favor rests."
dailies.enoch: Raise your arms high with a parent and say, "Glory to God!"
dailies.elijah: In verse 13, who suddenly appeared with the angel?
dailies.elijahAnswer: "A great company of the heavenly host," a huge crowd of angels (verse 13).
dailies.jordyn: The angels said there would be "peace to those on whom his favor rests" (verse 14). What kind of peace do you think Jesus brings?
dailies.jordynAnswer: Most of all, peace with God. Jesus came as the Savior (verse 11), so people who were far from God because of sin can be made right with him. That peace can also calm our hearts when life feels worried or messy.
dailies.action: Read verses 13–14 together. Then everyone stands, lifts their hands, and says verse 14 together like the angels.
dailies.prayer: God, we join the angels and say glory to you in the highest heaven! Thank you for sending Jesus to bring peace. Help our family live at peace with you and with each other this week. In Jesus' name, Amen.
dailies.teach: Yesterday one angel told the shepherds the good news. Then, suddenly, a great company of the heavenly host appeared, a huge crowd of angels, all praising God together. They said, "Glory to God in the highest heaven, and on earth peace to those on whom his favor rests." Glory means showing how great and wonderful God is. The angels were excited because God was keeping his promise and sending the Savior. Jesus came to bring peace between God and people, so everyone who trusts him can be at peace with God. Heaven celebrated the birth of Jesus, and we get to celebrate too.
dailies.enochActivity: March around the room like a big crowd of angels, arms up high, singing, "Glory to God! Jesus is born!"
dailies.elijah2: Find it in the passage: In verse 13, what were the angels doing?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: They were "praising God" (verse 13).
dailies.jordyn2: The angels gave "glory to God" first (verse 14). What does it look like to give God glory in your everyday life, at school, at volleyball, or at home?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: Giving glory to God means showing others how great he is, like the angels did (verse 14). Any real answer works, such as thanking God when things go well, being honest, working hard without bragging, or being kind to a teammate.
dailies.passageText: 13 Suddenly a great company of the heavenly host appeared with the angel, praising God and saying, 14 “Glory to God in the highest heaven, and on earth peace to those on whom his favor rests.”

dailies.label: Day 5
dailies.focus: The shepherds hurried to find Jesus, and then they spread the word about him to everyone.
dailies.verse: When they had seen him, they spread the word concerning what had been told them about this child, and all who heard it were amazed at what the shepherds said to them.
dailies.enoch: Say with a parent, "Let's go see Jesus!" Then tell one person, "Jesus is born!"
dailies.elijah: In verse 16, how did the shepherds go to Bethlehem: slowly or quickly?
dailies.elijahAnswer: Quickly: "they hurried off" (verse 16).
dailies.jordyn: The shepherds said, "Let's go to Bethlehem and see this thing that has happened" (verse 15). What does their quick response teach you about how to respond when God shows you something true?
dailies.jordynAnswer: They believed the angel's message and acted on it right away instead of waiting (verses 15–16). When God shows us something true in his Word, the best response is to believe it and act on it, not put it off.
dailies.action: Challenge: this week, each person tells one person outside the family one true thing about Jesus from the Christmas story, like "Jesus is the Savior" or "The angels said it was good news for all the people." Share how it went at dinner.
dailies.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank you that the shepherds hurried to find you. Give us that same excitement about you. Help each of us be brave and kind as we tell someone about you this week. In Jesus' name, Amen.
dailies.teach: After the angels went back into heaven, the shepherds didn't sit around wondering. They said to one another, "Let's go to Bethlehem and see this thing that has happened, which the Lord has told us about." They hurried off and found Mary and Joseph, and the baby lying in the manger, exactly as the angel said. Then they couldn't keep quiet! They spread the word about what they had been told about this child, and everyone who heard it was amazed. The shepherds were ordinary workers, but God used them to share the best news ever. God can use us to tell others about Jesus too.
dailies.enochActivity: Run from one side of the room to the other like the hurrying shepherds, find a baby doll in a blanket, then run to a parent and say, "I found Jesus!"
dailies.elijah2: Find it in the passage: In verse 18, how did people feel when they heard what the shepherds said?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: They "were amazed" (verse 18).
dailies.jordyn2: The shepherds told people about Jesus right after they met him (verse 17). Who is one person you could share the Christmas story with, and what would make it easier to do?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: Any honest answer works, like a friend, teammate, or cousin. The shepherds simply told what they had seen and heard (verse 17); you don't need to know everything, just share what you know is true about Jesus.
dailies.passageText: 15 When the angels had left them and gone into heaven, the shepherds said to one another, “Let’s go to Bethlehem and see this thing that has happened, which the Lord has told us about.” 16 So they hurried off and found Mary and Joseph, and the baby, who was lying in the manger. 17 When they had seen him, they spread the word concerning what had been told them about this child, 18 and all who heard it were amazed at what the shepherds said to them.

dailies.label: Day 6
dailies.focus: Mary treasured what God had done in her heart, and the shepherds went home glorifying and praising God.
dailies.verse: The shepherds returned, glorifying and praising God for all the things they had heard and seen, which were just as they had been told.
dailies.enoch: Fold your hands with a parent and say, "Thank you, God, for baby Jesus!"
dailies.elijah: In verse 20, what were the shepherds doing as they went back to their fields?
dailies.elijahAnswer: "Glorifying and praising God" (verse 20).
dailies.jordyn: Verse 19 says Mary "treasured up all these things and pondered them in her heart." What do you think it means to ponder something, and why would Mary do that?
dailies.jordynAnswer: To ponder means to think about something carefully and keep coming back to it. Mary had seen angels' words come true and shepherds arrive with amazing news (verses 17–19), so she kept these things like treasure and thought about what God was doing through her son.
dailies.action: Prayer time: each person finishes the sentence, "God, I praise you for..." with one thing about Jesus or about this Christmas. Then a parent closes in prayer.
dailies.prayer: God, we praise you like the shepherds for all we have heard and seen about Jesus. Thank you that everything happened just as you said. Help us treasure your Word in our hearts like Mary and praise you in our everyday lives. In Jesus' name, Amen.
dailies.teach: After all the excitement, Luke shows us two ways to respond to Jesus. Mary was quiet. She "treasured up all these things and pondered them in her heart," thinking carefully about everything God was doing. The shepherds were loud. They went back to their fields "glorifying and praising God" for everything they had heard and seen. Notice that it was all "just as they had been told." God's word through the angel came true exactly. Whether we think quietly about God or praise him out loud, Jesus is worth our whole hearts, and today we tell him so in prayer.
dailies.enochActivity: Make a "treasure box" with a small box. Put in a picture or a toy sheep and say, "I keep Jesus in my heart like a treasure!"
dailies.elijah2: Find it in the passage: Verse 20 says the things the shepherds heard and saw were "just as they had been told." Who told them?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: The angel of the Lord told them (verses 10–12). The shepherds called it what "the Lord has told us about" (verse 15).
dailies.jordyn2: The shepherds went back to ordinary work, but now they were "glorifying and praising God" (verse 20). How can meeting Jesus change the way you do ordinary things like homework, chores, or practice?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: Their jobs didn't change, but their hearts did (verse 20). Any real answer works, like doing chores without complaining, thanking God during practice, or doing homework carefully as a way to honor him.
dailies.passageText: 19 But Mary treasured up all these things and pondered them in her heart. 20 The shepherds returned, glorifying and praising God for all the things they had heard and seen, which were just as they had been told.

dailies.label: Day 7
dailies.focus: Recap: Jesus the Savior was born in Bethlehem and laid in a manger; angels told the shepherds the good news, and they hurried to see him and went home praising God.
dailies.verse: Today in the town of David a Savior has been born to you; he is the Messiah, the Lord.
dailies.enoch: Ask, "Where did baby Jesus sleep?" (In a manger!) "Who came to see him?" (The shepherds!)
dailies.elijah: Name two things that happened on the night Jesus was born.
dailies.elijahAnswer: Any two: Mary wrapped Jesus in cloths and laid him in a manger (verse 7); an angel appeared to the shepherds (verse 9); the angel told them the good news (verses 10–12); a great company of angels praised God (verses 13–14); the shepherds hurried to find Jesus (verse 16); they spread the word (verse 17); they went home praising God (verse 20).
dailies.jordyn: This week we read all of Luke 2:1–20. What does the whole week show about who Jesus is and why he came?
dailies.jordynAnswer: Jesus is the Savior, the Messiah, and the Lord (verse 11), born in the town of David as God promised (verse 4). He came humbly, in a manger (verse 7), with good news for all the people (verse 10), to bring peace to those on whom God's favor rests (verse 14).
dailies.action: Read verses 10–14 together, then each person shares one thing they learned about Jesus or the shepherds this week. Next lesson: The wise men worship Jesus.
dailies.prayer: Father, thank you for sending Jesus, our Savior, the Messiah, the Lord. Thank you for the good news of great joy for all the people. Help us hurry to Jesus, tell others about him, and praise you every day like the shepherds. In Jesus' name, Amen.
dailies.teach: Today we look back at our week. God used a ruler's census to bring Joseph and Mary to Bethlehem, the town of David, and there Jesus was born and laid in a manger. An angel appeared to shepherds in the fields and said, "Do not be afraid," bringing good news of great joy for all the people: a Savior had been born, the Messiah, the Lord. Then a great company of angels praised God. The shepherds hurried to find Jesus, told everyone about him, and went home glorifying and praising God. Mary treasured all these things in her heart. Next week we will read about the wise men who followed a star to worship Jesus.
dailies.enochActivity: Act out the story: Enoch is a shepherd with a stuffed sheep, a parent is the angel saying, "Do not be afraid! Jesus is born!" Enoch hurries to a baby doll in a box and says, "Glory to God!"
dailies.elijah2: Find it in the passage: In verse 11, what three names did the angel use for Jesus?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: "A Savior," "the Messiah," and "the Lord" (verse 11).
dailies.jordyn2: Last week Joseph obeyed right away, and this week the shepherds hurried to Jesus. What do Joseph and the shepherds teach you about how to respond to God's message?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: Both believed God's message and acted on it without delay (Matthew 1:24; Luke 2:15–16). The shepherds also told others and praised God (verses 17 and 20). Any honest answer about where you want to respond to God more quickly works.
dailies.passageText: 10 But the angel said to them, “Do not be afraid. I bring you good news that will cause great joy for all the people. 11 Today in the town of David a Savior has been born to you; he is the Messiah, the Lord. 12 This will be a sign to you: You will find a baby wrapped in cloths and lying in a manger.” 13 Suddenly a great company of the heavenly host appeared with the angel, praising God and saying, 14 “Glory to God in the highest heaven, and on earth peace to those on whom his favor rests.”

weeks.title: The wise men worship Jesus
weeks.selectLabel: Week 9 · The wise men worship Jesus
weeks.nextUp: Week 10 · The Holy Spirit, our Helper
weeks.bigIdea: God led wise men from far away by a star to find Jesus, the King born in Bethlehem as the prophet promised, and they bowed down, worshiped him, and gave him their treasures, because Jesus is King for all nations.
weeks.scheduleNote: This is the Week 9 family lesson. The short daily bites are Days 2–7.

howSteps.title: Read together
howSteps.detail: Open the Read tab and read Matthew 2:1–12 out loud in two parts, then read the short Micah 5:2 promise. Let a different person read each part.

howSteps.title: Talk it through
howSteps.detail: Still on Read, walk through the kid-language explanation so everyone gets the picture.

howSteps.title: Age parts
howSteps.detail: Use Enoch, Elijah, and Jordyn tabs. Keep the Parent key open for yourself.

howSteps.title: Pray
howSteps.detail: Close with the short family prayer on the Prayer tab.

readings.text: 1 After Jesus was born in Bethlehem in Judea, during the time of King Herod, Magi from the east came to Jerusalem 2 and asked, "Where is the one who has been born king of the Jews? We saw his star when it rose and have come to worship him." 3 When King Herod heard this he was disturbed, and all Jerusalem with him. 4 When he had called together all the people's chief priests and teachers of the law, he asked them where the Messiah was to be born. 5 "In Bethlehem in Judea," they replied, "for this is what the prophet has written: 6 "'But you, Bethlehem, in the land of Judah, are by no means least among the rulers of Judah; for out of you will come a ruler who will shepherd my people Israel.'"

7 Then Herod called the Magi secretly and found out from them the exact time the star had appeared. 8 He sent them to Bethlehem and said, "Go and search carefully for the child. As soon as you find him, report to me, so that I too may go and worship him." 9 After they had heard the king, they went on their way, and the star they had seen when it rose went ahead of them until it stopped over the place where the child was. 10 When they saw the star, they were overjoyed. 11 On coming to the house, they saw the child with his mother Mary, and they bowed down and worshiped him. Then they opened their treasures and presented him with gifts of gold, frankincense and myrrh. 12 And having been warned in a dream not to go back to Herod, they returned to their country by another route.
2 "But you, Bethlehem Ephrathah, though you are small among the clans of Judah, out of you will come for me one who will be ruler over Israel, whose origins are from of old, from ancient times."

story: Last week we read about the night Jesus was born in Bethlehem and the shepherds who hurried to see him. The shepherds lived close by, but this week some visitors come from very far away.

After Jesus was born, Magi, also called wise men, came from the east to Jerusalem. They asked, "Where is the one who has been born king of the Jews? We saw his star when it rose and have come to worship him." They had traveled a long way because God showed them a special star.

King Herod heard this and was disturbed. He did not want another king. He asked the chief priests and teachers of the law where the Messiah would be born. They knew the answer from the prophet Micah, who wrote long before that a ruler who would shepherd God's people Israel would come out of Bethlehem. God had told his people the very town where the King would be born.

Herod secretly sent the wise men to Bethlehem and told them to report back, saying he wanted to worship the child too. But he did not really mean it. The wise men left, and the star went ahead of them until it stopped over the place where the child was. When they saw the star, they were overjoyed!

They came into the house and saw the child with his mother Mary, and they bowed down and worshiped him. Then they opened their treasures and gave him gifts of gold, frankincense, and myrrh. God warned them in a dream not to go back to Herod, so they went home another way. Jesus is not just King for one nation; people from far away came to worship him. Next week we will learn about the Holy Spirit, our Helper.
weeks.enochLine: The wise men followed a star to find Jesus! They bowed down and gave him gifts!
enochActivities: Activity: Follow the star. A parent holds up a paper star (or a flashlight) and walks slowly around the house. Enoch follows as a wise man. When the star stops over a baby doll, Enoch bows down and says, "Jesus is the King!"
Gift time: give Enoch three small boxes or toys to be the gifts. He sets each one down by the baby doll and says, "A gift for King Jesus!" Then hug and say together, "We worship Jesus!"
elijahQuestions: Where did the wise men come from (verse 1)?
What did the wise men see that made them come (verse 2)?
What did the wise men do when they saw the child with Mary (verse 11)?
What three gifts did they give Jesus (verse 11)?
jordynQuestions: The shepherds were from nearby, but the Magi came "from the east," from another land (verse 1). What does it show that people from far away came to worship Jesus?

The chief priests knew from Scripture exactly where the Messiah would be born (verses 4–6), but the Magi are the ones who went to worship him. What is the difference between knowing about Jesus and coming to him?

Herod said, "so that I too may go and worship him" (verse 8), but God warned the Magi not to go back to him (verse 12). How can someone use worship words without really meaning them, and how does God see the heart?
weeks.jordynApplication: The Magi traveled a long way, "bowed down and worshiped him," and "opened their treasures" for Jesus (verse 11). Worship means treating Jesus as the King he is, with our hearts and with what we have. This week, think about what you treasure, like your time, your talents in volleyball or school, or your money, and pick one way to give some of it to Jesus: time to read his Word, encouragement for a teammate, or a gift to someone in need. Do it gladly, the way the Magi were overjoyed (verse 10).
elijahAnswers: From the east (verse 1).
His star: "We saw his star when it rose" (verse 2).
They "bowed down and worshiped him" (verse 11).
Gold, frankincense, and myrrh (verse 11).
jordynAnswers: Jesus is King for every nation, not just one people. Last week the angel said the good news was "for all the people" (Luke 2:10), and here people from a far-off land came to worship him (verses 1–2).

The priests knew the right answer from Micah (verses 5–6), but there is no sign they went to Bethlehem. The Magi traveled far to find Jesus and worship him (verses 9–11). Knowing facts about Jesus matters, but God wants us to come to him and worship him.

Herod said worship words, but he was disturbed by the news (verse 3), met the Magi secretly (verse 7), and God warned them not to return to him (verse 12). He did not truly want to worship; the next verse in Matthew shows he wanted to harm the child (Matthew 2:13). People can say the right words without meaning them, but God sees what is really in the heart.
weeks.applicationCheck: Ask her later in the week what treasure she chose to give to Jesus, like time, encouragement, or a gift, and how it went. Notice and thank her when you see her do it.
weeks.prayer: Dear God, thank you for leading the wise men by a star to find Jesus. Thank you that Jesus is King for all nations, including our family. Help us worship him with our whole hearts and give him our best, like the wise men did. Make us overjoyed to know him. In Jesus' name, Amen.

dailies.label: Day 2
dailies.focus: God led wise men from far away to come looking for Jesus, the one born king of the Jews, so they could worship him.
dailies.verse: Where is the one who has been born king of the Jews? We saw his star when it rose and have come to worship him.
dailies.enoch: Point up high with a parent and say, "Look! A star! Let's go find King Jesus!"
dailies.elijah: In verse 1, what city did the Magi come to first?
dailies.elijahAnswer: Jerusalem (verse 1).
dailies.jordyn: The Magi said they had "come to worship him" (verse 2). Why is it amazing that people from another land came all that way to worship a baby?
dailies.jordynAnswer: They traveled a long way "from the east" (verse 1) to worship a child they had never seen. It shows Jesus is not just a king for one nation; God was already drawing people from far away to worship him (verse 2).
dailies.action: Read verses 1–2 together. Then go outside or look out a window tonight and find a star. Talk about how God used a star to lead the Magi to Jesus.
dailies.prayer: God, thank you for leading the wise men from far away to find Jesus. Thank you that Jesus is King for people from every land. Help us look for Jesus and want to worship him like they did. In Jesus' name, Amen.
dailies.teach: Last week shepherds from nearby hurried to see baby Jesus. Now Matthew tells us about visitors from far away. After Jesus was born in Bethlehem, during the time of King Herod, Magi came from the east to Jerusalem. Magi were wise men, and they asked, "Where is the one who has been born king of the Jews?" They had seen his star when it rose, and they had come to worship him. God used a star to lead them toward his Son.
dailies.enochActivity: Cut out or draw a big yellow star. Hold it high and walk around the room saying, "Follow the star to Jesus!"
dailies.elijah2: Find it in the passage: In verse 2, why did the Magi say they had come?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: "To worship him" (verse 2).
dailies.jordyn2: The Magi called Jesus "king of the Jews" (verse 2), but Herod was already king there (verse 1). Why might that be a problem for Herod?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: Herod wanted to be the only king. A new king born to rule would be a threat to his power (verses 1–2). Jesus is the true King God promised, and that is good news for anyone who welcomes him.
dailies.passageText: 1 After Jesus was born in Bethlehem in Judea, during the time of King Herod, Magi from the east came to Jerusalem 2 and asked, “Where is the one who has been born king of the Jews? We saw his star when it rose and have come to worship him.”

dailies.label: Day 3
dailies.focus: Long before Jesus was born, God told his prophet the exact town where the King would be born: Bethlehem.
dailies.verse: But you, Bethlehem, in the land of Judah, are by no means least among the rulers of Judah; for out of you will come a ruler who will shepherd my people Israel.
dailies.enoch: Play "Where was Jesus born?" A parent asks, and Enoch shouts, "Bethlehem!" Say it fast, slow, loud, and in a whisper.
dailies.elijah: Game: Find Bethlehem. Write "Bethlehem" on a piece of paper and hide it somewhere in the room. Everyone hunts for it, and whoever finds it reads verse 6. Then: where did the chief priests say the Messiah would be born (verse 5)?
dailies.elijahAnswer: "In Bethlehem in Judea" (verse 5).
dailies.jordyn: Herod "was disturbed, and all Jerusalem with him" (verse 3) when he heard a king had been born. Why would good news about God's King upset some people?
dailies.jordynAnswer: Herod wanted to keep his own power, and a new king felt like a threat (verse 3). Jesus is good news, but he is also the King, and people who want to be in charge of their own lives can feel bothered by that.
dailies.action: Play Find Bethlehem, then read verses 5–6 together. Talk about how God kept his promise down to the very town.
dailies.prayer: God, thank you that you told your people long ago where the King would be born, and you kept your word exactly. Thank you that Jesus is the ruler who shepherds his people. Help us trust every promise in your Word. In Jesus' name, Amen.
dailies.teach: When King Herod heard that the Magi were looking for a newborn king, he was disturbed, and all Jerusalem with him. Herod called together the chief priests and teachers of the law and asked where the Messiah was to be born. They knew right away, because a prophet had written it down long before. The answer was Bethlehem in Judea. The prophet called Bethlehem a small place, but said that out of it would come a ruler who would shepherd God's people. Last week we saw shepherds come to Jesus, and here God says Jesus himself is the ruler who will shepherd his people.
dailies.enochActivity: Be a little shepherd: gather stuffed animals into a group and say, "Jesus takes care of us like a shepherd!"
dailies.elijah2: Find it in the passage: In verse 6, what will the ruler from Bethlehem do for God's people?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: He "will shepherd my people Israel" (verse 6).
dailies.jordyn2: Compare Matthew 2:6 with Micah 5:2. Micah says Bethlehem is "small among the clans of Judah," but Matthew says it is "by no means least." Why would a small town become so important?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: Bethlehem was small (Micah 5:2), but the ruler God promised would come from there (Matthew 2:6). Jesus being born there made it great. God often uses small and humble things to do his biggest work, like a baby in a manger.
dailies.passageText: 3 When King Herod heard this he was disturbed, and all Jerusalem with him. 4 When he had called together all the people’s chief priests and teachers of the law, he asked them where the Messiah was to be born. 5 “In Bethlehem in Judea,” they replied, “for this is what the prophet has written: 6 “‘But you, Bethlehem, in the land of Judah, are by no means least among the rulers of Judah; for out of you will come a ruler who will shepherd my people Israel.’”

dailies.label: Day 4
dailies.focus: God's star went ahead of the wise men and stopped over the place where Jesus was, and they were overjoyed.
dailies.verse: When they saw the star, they were overjoyed.
dailies.enoch: Jump up and down with a parent and say, "The star stopped! We found Jesus! Yay!"
dailies.elijah: In verse 9, what did the star do?
dailies.elijahAnswer: It "went ahead of them until it stopped over the place where the child was" (verse 9).
dailies.jordyn: Herod told the Magi to "search carefully for the child" and report back so he could worship too (verse 8). What do you notice about how Herod met with them in verse 7?
dailies.jordynAnswer: He "called the Magi secretly" (verse 7). Doing it in secret is a clue that he was hiding his real plan. He was disturbed about a new king (verse 3), so his words about worship were not honest.
dailies.action: Read verses 9–10 together. Then a parent moves a paper star slowly across the room while everyone follows, and when it stops, everyone cheers like the overjoyed Magi.
dailies.prayer: God, thank you for leading the wise men all the way to Jesus. Lead our family to Jesus too, every day. Fill us with joy like theirs when we think about him. In Jesus' name, Amen.
dailies.teach: Herod called the Magi secretly and found out exactly when the star had appeared. He sent them to Bethlehem and said, "Go and search carefully for the child," and asked them to report back so he could worship him too. But Herod did not really mean it. The Magi went on their way, and the star they had seen when it rose went ahead of them until it stopped over the place where the child was. God himself was guiding them. When they saw the star, they were overjoyed. Finding Jesus is the happiest thing that can happen to anyone.
dailies.enochActivity: Follow the star: a parent holds a flashlight beam on the floor and moves it slowly. Enoch follows it until it stops on a baby doll, then shouts, "Jesus!"
dailies.elijah2: Find it in the passage: In verse 10, how did the Magi feel when they saw the star?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: They "were overjoyed" (verse 10).
dailies.jordyn2: The star led the Magi all the way to Jesus (verse 9). What has God used to lead you closer to Jesus, and how could you help lead someone else to him?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: God guided the Magi step by step (verse 9). Any real answer works, like the Bible, your parents, church, or a friend's example. You can help lead others by being kind, inviting them, or sharing what you know about Jesus.
dailies.passageText: 7 Then Herod called the Magi secretly and found out from them the exact time the star had appeared. 8 He sent them to Bethlehem and said, “Go and search carefully for the child. As soon as you find him, report to me, so that I too may go and worship him.” 9 After they had heard the king, they went on their way, and the star they had seen when it rose went ahead of them until it stopped over the place where the child was. 10 When they saw the star, they were overjoyed.

dailies.label: Day 5
dailies.focus: The wise men bowed down, worshiped Jesus, and gave him their treasures, and God protected them on the way home.
dailies.verse: On coming to the house, they saw the child with his mother Mary, and they bowed down and worshiped him. Then they opened their treasures and presented him with gifts of gold, frankincense and myrrh.
dailies.enoch: Bow down with a parent and say, "Jesus, you are my King!"
dailies.elijah: In verse 11, who did the Magi see in the house?
dailies.elijahAnswer: "The child with his mother Mary" (verse 11).
dailies.jordyn: The Magi "bowed down and worshiped him" first, and then they gave gifts (verse 11). Why do you think worship comes before the gifts?
dailies.jordynAnswer: Gifts mean the most when they come from a heart that already honors Jesus as King. The Magi bowed and worshiped him first (verse 11), and their gifts showed what they believed about him. God wants our hearts, not just our stuff.
dailies.action: Challenge: this week, each person gives one "treasure" to Jesus. Ideas: give some of your money to church or someone in need, give time to help without being asked, or give a toy to a child who needs it. Share at dinner what you gave.
dailies.prayer: Jesus, you are our King. We bow down and worship you. Help us give you our best, our time, our money, and our hearts, gladly like the wise men did. Thank you for protecting your people and leading them home. In Jesus' name, Amen.
dailies.teach: The star led the Magi to the house, and they saw the child with his mother Mary. Right away they bowed down and worshiped him. Then they opened their treasures and gave him gifts of gold, frankincense, and myrrh. These were expensive gifts, the kind you would give a king. Then God warned them in a dream not to go back to Herod, so they went home to their own country by another route. Just like God spoke to Joseph in a dream, God spoke to the Magi to keep them and Jesus safe. Today our challenge is to give Jesus a treasure of our own.
dailies.enochActivity: Wrap a small toy in paper or a cloth. Enoch carries it to a baby doll, bows down, and says, "A gift for King Jesus!"
dailies.elijah2: Find it in the passage: In verse 12, why didn't the Magi go back to Herod?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: They had been "warned in a dream not to go back to Herod" (verse 12).
dailies.jordyn2: The Magi "opened their treasures" for Jesus (verse 11). What is one treasure you have, like time, a talent, or money, that you could give to Jesus this week, and how?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: Any honest answer works, like time reading the Bible, using volleyball to encourage a teammate, or giving money to help someone. Worship with gifts starts with bowing our hearts to Jesus (verse 11).
dailies.passageText: 11 On coming to the house, they saw the child with his mother Mary, and they bowed down and worshiped him. Then they opened their treasures and presented him with gifts of gold, frankincense and myrrh. 12 And having been warned in a dream not to go back to Herod, they returned to their country by another route.

dailies.label: Day 6
dailies.focus: The wise men bowed before Jesus, and one day every knee will bow and every tongue will say that Jesus Christ is Lord.
dailies.verse: that at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, in heaven and on earth and under the earth, and every tongue acknowledge that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.
dailies.enoch: Kneel down with a parent and say, "Jesus is Lord!"
dailies.elijah: In verse 10, what will every knee do at the name of Jesus?
dailies.elijahAnswer: Every knee will bow (verse 10).
dailies.jordyn: The Magi bowed to Jesus as a child (Matthew 2:11), and Philippians says one day every knee will bow (verse 10). What is the difference between choosing to bow to Jesus now and bowing later?
dailies.jordynAnswer: One day everyone will acknowledge that Jesus Christ is Lord (verses 10–11). The Magi chose to worship him gladly now (Matthew 2:10–11). Bowing now is joyful worship from a heart that trusts him, and it is the best way to live.
dailies.action: Prayer time: everyone kneels or bows their head. Each person says, "Jesus, you are Lord," and thanks him for one thing. Then a parent closes in prayer.
dailies.prayer: Lord Jesus, we bow before you like the wise men did. You have the name that is above every name. We say with our mouths and believe in our hearts that you are Lord, to the glory of God the Father. Help us worship you every day. In Jesus' name, Amen.
dailies.teach: Yesterday the Magi bowed down and worshiped the child Jesus. Today we read what Paul wrote many years later about Jesus. God exalted Jesus to the highest place and gave him the name that is above every name. One day, at the name of Jesus, every knee will bow, in heaven and on earth and under the earth, and every tongue will say that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father. The Magi were some of the very first to bow to Jesus. Today we join them by bowing in prayer and telling Jesus that he is our Lord.
dailies.enochActivity: Practice bowing: stand up tall, then kneel down low and say, "Jesus is King! Jesus is Lord!" Do it three times.
dailies.elijah2: Find it in the passage: In verse 11, what will every tongue say about Jesus?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: "That Jesus Christ is Lord" (verse 11).
dailies.jordyn2: Verse 9 says God gave Jesus "the name that is above every name." What does it mean for Jesus' name to be above every other name, and how should that change the way we use his name?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: No one is greater than Jesus; his name is above every name (verse 9), and every knee will bow to him (verse 10). So we use his name with honor, in prayer and praise, and never carelessly or as a joke.
dailies.passageText: 9 Therefore God exalted him to the highest place and gave him the name that is above every name, 10 that at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, in heaven and on earth and under the earth, 11 and every tongue acknowledge that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.

dailies.label: Day 7
dailies.focus: Recap: God led the wise men by a star to Jesus, the King born in Bethlehem as promised, and they worshiped him and gave him their treasures.
dailies.verse: Where is the one who has been born king of the Jews? We saw his star when it rose and have come to worship him.
dailies.enoch: Ask, "What did the wise men follow?" (A star!) "What did they do when they found Jesus?" (They bowed down and worshiped him!)
dailies.elijah: Name two things the wise men did in this week's story.
dailies.elijahAnswer: Any two: came from the east to Jerusalem (verse 1); asked where the king of the Jews was (verse 2); followed the star (verse 9); were overjoyed (verse 10); bowed down and worshiped Jesus (verse 11); gave gold, frankincense, and myrrh (verse 11); went home by another route (verse 12).
dailies.jordyn: This week we read Matthew 2, Micah 5:2, and Philippians 2. What does the whole week show about who Jesus is?
dailies.jordynAnswer: Jesus is the King of the Jews the Magi came to worship (Matthew 2:2), the ruler from Bethlehem God promised long ago (Micah 5:2; Matthew 2:6), and the Lord whose name is above every name, before whom every knee will bow (Philippians 2:9–11). He is worthy of our worship and our treasures (Matthew 2:11).
dailies.action: Read verses 9–11 together, then each person shares one thing they learned about the wise men or about Jesus this week. Next lesson: The Holy Spirit, our Helper.
dailies.prayer: Father, thank you for leading the wise men to Jesus and for keeping your promise about Bethlehem. Thank you that Jesus is King for all nations and Lord over everything. Help us seek him, worship him with joy, and give him our best. In Jesus' name, Amen.
dailies.teach: Today we look back at our week. After Jesus was born, Magi came from the east to Jerusalem asking where the newborn king of the Jews was, because they had seen his star and came to worship him. King Herod was disturbed, and the chief priests showed from the prophet that the ruler who would shepherd God's people would come from Bethlehem. The star went ahead of the Magi and stopped over the place where the child was, and they were overjoyed. They bowed down, worshiped Jesus, and gave him gold, frankincense, and myrrh. God warned them in a dream, and they went home another way. Next week we will learn about the Holy Spirit, our Helper.
