readings.text: 1 After the Sabbath, at dawn on the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary went to look at the tomb. 2 There was a violent earthquake, for an angel of the Lord came down from heaven and, going to the tomb, rolled back the stone and sat on it. 3 His appearance was like lightning, and his clothes were white as snow. 4 The guards were so afraid of him that they shook and became like dead men. 5 The angel said to the women, “Do not be afraid, for I know that you are looking for Jesus, who was crucified. 6 He is not here; he has risen, just as he said. Come and see the place where he lay. 7 Then go quickly and tell his disciples: ‘He has risen from the dead and is going ahead of you into Galilee. There you will see him.’ Now I have told you.” 8 So the women hurried away from the tomb, afraid yet filled with joy, and ran to tell his disciples. 9 Suddenly Jesus met them. “Greetings,” he said. They came to him, clasped his feet and worshiped him. 10 Then Jesus said to them, “Do not be afraid. Go and tell my brothers to go to Galilee; there they will see me.”

11 Now Mary stood outside the tomb crying. As she wept, she bent over to look into the tomb 12 and saw two angels in white, seated where Jesus’ body had been, one at the head and the other at the foot. 13 They asked her, “Woman, why are you crying?” “They have taken my Lord away,” she said, “and I don’t know where they have put him.” 14 At this, she turned around and saw Jesus standing there, but she did not realize that it was Jesus. 15 He asked her, “Woman, why are you crying? Who is it you are looking for?” Thinking he was the gardener, she said, “Sir, if you have carried him away, tell me where you have put him, and I will get him.” 16 Jesus said to her, “Mary.” She turned toward him and cried out in Aramaic, “Rabboni!” (which means “Teacher”). 17 Jesus said, “Do not hold on to me, for I have not yet ascended to the Father. Go instead to my brothers and tell them, ‘I am ascending to my Father and your Father, to my God and your God.’” 18 Mary Magdalene went to the disciples with the news: “I have seen the Lord!” And she told them that he had said these things to her.

36 While they were still talking about this, Jesus himself stood among them and said to them, “Peace be with you.” 37 They were startled and frightened, thinking they saw a ghost. 38 He said to them, “Why are you troubled, and why do doubts rise in your minds? 39 Look at my hands and my feet. It is I myself! Touch me and see; a ghost does not have flesh and bones, as you see I have.” 40 When he had said this, he showed them his hands and feet. 41 And while they still did not believe it because of joy and amazement, he asked them, “Do you have anything here to eat?” 42 They gave him a piece of broiled fish, 43 and he took it and ate it in their presence. 44 He said to them, “This is what I told you while I was still with you: Everything must be fulfilled that is written about me in the Law of Moses, the Prophets and the Psalms.” 45 Then he opened their minds so they could understand the Scriptures. 46 He told them, “This is what is written: The Messiah will suffer and rise from the dead on the third day, 47 and repentance for the forgiveness of sins will be preached in his name to all nations, beginning at Jerusalem. 48 You are witnesses of these things. 49 I am going to send you what my Father has promised; but stay in the city until you have been clothed with power from on high.”

story: Last week we shouted “Hosanna!” — “LORD, save us!” — as Jesus entered Jerusalem. This week we see how he saves. Jesus died, just as we have already learned. Early on the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary went to look at the tomb.

There was a great earthquake. An angel of the Lord came, rolled back the stone, and sat on it. The angel said to the women, “Do not be afraid, for I know that you are looking for Jesus, who was crucified. He is not here; he has risen, just as he said. Come and see the place where he lay.” Then the women hurried away, afraid yet filled with joy, and ran to tell his disciples. Suddenly Jesus met them. “Greetings,” he said. They clasped his feet and worshiped him. Jesus said, “Do not be afraid. Go and tell my brothers to go to Galilee; there they will see me.”

Mary stood outside the tomb crying. Jesus said to her, “Mary.” She turned and cried out, “Rabboni!” (which means “Teacher”). Mary Magdalene went to the disciples with the news: “I have seen the Lord!”

That same day Jesus himself stood among his friends and said to them, “Peace be with you.” He showed them his hands and his feet. He told them that the Messiah would suffer and rise from the dead on the third day, and that they were witnesses of these things. He would send what the Father had promised.

So we say what the angel said: “He is not here; he has risen, just as he said.” The tomb is empty. Jesus is alive. He gives his friends peace, and he sends them to tell the good news. Next week we will see how those friends become a family: the church, God’s family.
weeks.enochLine: The tomb is empty! Jesus is alive!
enochActivities: Activity: The empty place. Help a grown-up open a box or a doorway, look inside, and say, “He is not here; he has risen, just as he said.”
Activity: Go and tell. Run to someone in the room and say: Jesus is alive!
elijahQuestions: In Matthew 28:6, what did the angel tell the women about Jesus?
In Matthew 28:8–9, what did the women do, and whom did they meet on the way?
In John 20:18, what news did Mary Magdalene take to the disciples?
In Luke 24:36, what did Jesus say when he stood among his friends?
jordynQuestions: The angel says, “He is not here; he has risen, just as he said.” Why does it matter that the tomb was empty, and that Jesus himself met the women?
Mary Magdalene tells the disciples, “I have seen the Lord!” (John 20:18). How is going and telling part of believing that Jesus is risen?
Jesus says, “Peace be with you,” and “You are witnesses of these things” (Luke 24:36, 48). How does the risen Jesus sending his friends get us ready for next week, when we talk about the church?
weeks.jordynApplication: Jesus is risen (Matthew 28:6). This week, tell someone the good news — “He is not here; he has risen, just as he said” — and receive his peace. Next week we will see how his friends become a family: the church, God’s family.
elijahAnswers: “He is not here; he has risen, just as he said.” (Matthew 28:6).
They hurried away from the tomb, afraid yet filled with joy, and ran to tell his disciples. Suddenly Jesus met them (Matthew 28:8–9).
“I have seen the Lord!” (John 20:18).
“Peace be with you.” (Luke 24:36).
jordynAnswers: The tomb was empty because Jesus is alive, just as he said (Matthew 28:6). He is not only a memory. He met the women himself and told them, “Go and tell” (Matthew 28:9–10).
Jesus told Mary to go and tell his brothers (John 20:17–18). Believing that he is risen means we do not keep the news to ourselves. We say, with Mary, “I have seen the Lord!”

The risen Jesus gives his friends peace and sends them as witnesses (Luke 24:36, 48). Next week we will see how those friends become a family — the church, God’s family — who keep telling the good news.
weeks.applicationCheck: Ask her later in the week whether she told someone that Jesus is risen, and whether she received his peace. If it is fitting, share one way you told the good news this week too, and thank God together that the tomb is empty.
weeks.prayer: Father, thank you that Jesus died, and that the tomb is empty. He is not here; he has risen, just as he said. Give us his peace, and help us tell the good news that Jesus is alive. In Jesus’ name, Amen.

dailies.label: Day 2 · Passage
dailies.focus: At dawn on the first day of the week, the women find the tomb empty. The angel says, “He is not here; he has risen, just as he said.”
dailies.verse: He is not here; he has risen, just as he said. Come and see the place where he lay.
dailies.enoch: Help a grown-up look in an open box and say, “He is not here; he has risen, just as he said.”
dailies.elijah: In Matthew 28:1, who went to look at the tomb at dawn on the first day of the week?
dailies.elijahAnswer: Mary Magdalene and the other Mary (Matthew 28:1).
dailies.jordyn: The angel says Jesus “has risen, just as he said” (Matthew 28:6). Why do those last four words matter?
dailies.jordynAnswer: Jesus had already told them he would rise. The empty tomb keeps his word. He is alive, just as he said.
dailies.action: Tell someone today, “He is not here; he has risen, just as he said.”
dailies.prayer: Father, thank you that the tomb is empty. Jesus has risen, just as he said. Help us believe it and tell it. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
dailies.teach: After the Sabbath, at dawn on the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary went to look at the tomb. An angel of the Lord rolled back the stone and said, “Do not be afraid, for I know that you are looking for Jesus, who was crucified. He is not here; he has risen, just as he said. Come and see the place where he lay.” The women hurried away, afraid yet filled with joy, and ran to tell his disciples. Suddenly Jesus met them and said, “Do not be afraid. Go and tell my brothers to go to Galilee; there they will see me.”
dailies.enochActivity: Clap and say: Jesus is alive!
dailies.elijah2: In Matthew 28:6, what two things did the angel tell the women to know and to do?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: Jesus is not here; he has risen, just as he said. And, “Come and see the place where he lay.”
dailies.jordyn2: The women are “afraid yet filled with joy” as they run to tell (Matthew 28:8). What does it look like to tell the good news with both wonder and joy?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: They do not stay at the empty tomb. They run to tell, and Jesus meets them on the way (Matthew 28:8–10). Wonder does not have to cancel joy, and joy does not have to pretend there is no wonder.
dailies.passageText: 1 After the Sabbath, at dawn on the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary went to look at the tomb. 2 There was a violent earthquake, for an angel of the Lord came down from heaven and, going to the tomb, rolled back the stone and sat on it. 3 His appearance was like lightning, and his clothes were white as snow. 4 The guards were so afraid of him that they shook and became like dead men. 5 The angel said to the women, “Do not be afraid, for I know that you are looking for Jesus, who was crucified. 6 He is not here; he has risen, just as he said. Come and see the place where he lay. 7 Then go quickly and tell his disciples: ‘He has risen from the dead and is going ahead of you into Galilee. There you will see him.’ Now I have told you.” 8 So the women hurried away from the tomb, afraid yet filled with joy, and ran to tell his disciples. 9 Suddenly Jesus met them. “Greetings,” he said. They came to him, clasped his feet and worshiped him. 10 Then Jesus said to them, “Do not be afraid. Go and tell my brothers to go to Galilee; there they will see me.”

dailies.label: Day 3 · Game
dailies.focus: The women run from the empty tomb to tell the good news, and Jesus meets them on the way.
dailies.verse: So the women hurried away from the tomb, afraid yet filled with joy, and ran to tell his disciples.
dailies.enoch: Run to a grown-up in the room and say: Jesus is alive!
dailies.elijah: In Matthew 28:10, what did Jesus tell the women to do?
dailies.elijahAnswer: “Do not be afraid. Go and tell my brothers to go to Galilee; there they will see me.”
dailies.jordyn: Jesus meets the women as they go to tell (Matthew 28:9–10). What does that show you about following the angel’s words?
dailies.jordynAnswer: They obey and go, and the risen Jesus meets them himself. The good news is not only that the tomb is empty. Jesus is alive, and he is with them as they go and tell.
dailies.action: Play a go-and-tell race: run to someone at home and say: Jesus is risen!
dailies.prayer: Jesus, thank you that you met the women as they ran to tell. Take away our fear, and send us to tell that you are alive. In your name, Amen.
dailies.teach: The women hurried away from the tomb, afraid yet filled with joy, and ran to tell his disciples. Suddenly Jesus met them. “Greetings,” he said. They came to him, clasped his feet and worshiped him. Then Jesus said to them, “Do not be afraid. Go and tell my brothers to go to Galilee; there they will see me.” The first thing the risen Jesus gives them is peace, and a message to carry.
dailies.enochActivity: Help a grown-up clap a rhythm and say, “He is not here; he has risen, just as he said.”
dailies.elijah2: In Matthew 28:9, what did the women do when Jesus met them?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: They came to him, clasped his feet and worshiped him.
dailies.jordyn2: Why is it good news that the first people sent to tell that Jesus is risen are these women, running from an empty tomb?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: God let them be the first to see that Jesus is alive and the first to be sent: “Go and tell” (Matthew 28:10). The good news starts with witnesses who have met the risen Jesus.
dailies.passageText: So the women hurried away from the tomb, afraid yet filled with joy, and ran to tell his disciples. Suddenly Jesus met them. “Greetings,” he said. They came to him, clasped his feet and worshiped him. Then Jesus said to them, “Do not be afraid. Go and tell my brothers to go to Galilee; there they will see me.”

dailies.label: Day 4 · Passage
dailies.focus: On the road to Emmaus, two friends walk with Jesus without knowing him. They recognize him when he breaks the bread.
dailies.verse: They asked each other, “Were not our hearts burning within us while he talked with us on the road and opened the Scriptures to us?”
dailies.enoch: Break a piece of bread (or a cracker) with a grown-up and say: Jesus is with us.
dailies.elijah: In Luke 24:31, when did the two friends recognize Jesus?
dailies.elijahAnswer: When he was at the table with them, he took bread, gave thanks, broke it and began to give it to them. Then their eyes were opened and they recognized him (Luke 24:30–31).
dailies.jordyn: Their hearts burned while Jesus opened the Scriptures on the road (Luke 24:32). Why does Jesus use the Scriptures, not only a surprise ending, to show who he is?
dailies.jordynAnswer: He helps them see that what happened was already written. The risen Jesus is the one the Scriptures were talking about, and he opens them so his friends can understand.
dailies.action: Ask a grown-up to read a few verses about Jesus with you, and thank God that he opens the Scriptures.
dailies.prayer: Jesus, walk with us as you walked with your friends. Open the Scriptures to us, and help us recognize you. In your name, Amen.
dailies.teach: That same day two of them were going to a village called Emmaus. Jesus himself came up and walked with them, but they were kept from recognizing him. He explained what was said in all the Scriptures concerning himself. When he was at the table with them, he took bread, gave thanks, broke it and began to give it to them. Then their eyes were opened and they recognized him, and he disappeared from their sight. They asked each other, “Were not our hearts burning within us while he talked with us on the road and opened the Scriptures to us?”
dailies.enochActivity: Walk around the room with a grown-up and say: Jesus walks with us.
dailies.elijah2: In Luke 24:32, what did the two friends say to each other after they recognized Jesus?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: “Were not our hearts burning within us while he talked with us on the road and opened the Scriptures to us?”
dailies.jordyn2: After they recognized Jesus, they went back to tell the others (Luke 24:33–35). How does that fit with the empty tomb’s “Go and tell”?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: The same good news keeps moving. The women ran from the tomb. These two return to Jerusalem and tell how Jesus was recognized when he broke the bread (Luke 24:35).
dailies.passageText: 13 Now that same day two of them were going to a village called Emmaus, about seven miles from Jerusalem. 14 They were talking with each other about everything that had happened. 15 As they talked and discussed these things with each other, Jesus himself came up and walked along with them; 16 but they were kept from recognizing him. 17 He asked them, “What are you discussing together as you walk along?” They stood still, their faces downcast. 18 One of them, named Cleopas, asked him, “Are you the only one visiting Jerusalem who does not know the things that have happened there in these days?” 19 “What things?” he asked. “About Jesus of Nazareth,” they replied. “He was a prophet, powerful in word and deed before God and all the people. 20 The chief priests and our rulers handed him over to be sentenced to death, and they crucified him; 21 but we had hoped that he was the one who was going to redeem Israel. And what is more, it is the third day since all this took place. 22 In addition, some of our women amazed us. They went to the tomb early this morning 23 but didn’t find his body. They came and told us that they had seen a vision of angels, who said he was alive. 24 Then some of our companions went to the tomb and found it just as the women had said, but they did not see Jesus.” 25 He said to them, “How foolish you are, and how slow to believe all that the prophets have spoken! 26 Did not the Messiah have to suffer these things and then enter his glory?” 27 And beginning with Moses and all the Prophets, he explained to them what was said in all the Scriptures concerning himself. 28 As they approached the village to which they were going, Jesus continued on as if he were going farther. 29 But they urged him strongly, “Stay with us, for it is nearly evening; the day is almost over.” So he went in to stay with them. 30 When he was at the table with them, he took bread, gave thanks, broke it and began to give it to them. 31 Then their eyes were opened and they recognized him, and he disappeared from their sight. 32 They asked each other, “Were not our hearts burning within us while he talked with us on the road and opened the Scriptures to us?” 33 They got up and returned at once to Jerusalem. There they found the Eleven and those with them, assembled together 34 and saying, “It is true! The Lord has risen and has appeared to Simon.” 35 Then the two told what had happened on the way, and how Jesus was recognized by them when he broke the bread.

dailies.label: Day 5 · Challenge
dailies.focus: Thomas was not there when Jesus first came. Jesus comes again, and Thomas believes: “My Lord and my God!”
dailies.verse: Because you have seen me, you have believed; blessed are those who have not seen and yet have believed.
dailies.enoch: Point to your eyes, then to your heart, and say: I believe Jesus is alive!
dailies.elijah: In John 20:25, what did Thomas say he would have to see before he would believe?
dailies.elijahAnswer: “Unless I see the nail marks in his hands and put my finger where the nails were, and put my hand into his side, I will not believe.”
dailies.jordyn: Jesus does not shame Thomas. He comes and says, “Stop doubting and believe” (John 20:27). What kind of Lord does that show him to be?
dailies.jordynAnswer: He is kind and true. He comes to Thomas, shows that he is really alive, and invites him to believe. Thomas answers, “My Lord and my God!” (John 20:28).
dailies.action: If you are struggling to believe, tell a grown-up honestly, and ask Jesus to help you trust him. If you believe, thank him that he blesses those who have not seen and yet have believed.
dailies.prayer: Jesus, you are Lord and God. Help us believe even when we have not seen you with our eyes. Thank you that you come to your friends with peace. In your name, Amen.
dailies.teach: Thomas was not with the disciples when Jesus came. The others told him, “We have seen the Lord!” But he said he would not believe unless he saw the nail marks and put his hand into Jesus’ side. A week later Jesus came, though the doors were locked, and said, “Peace be with you!” He said to Thomas, “Put your finger here; see my hands. Reach out your hand and put it into my side. Stop doubting and believe.” Thomas said, “My Lord and my God!” Then Jesus told him, “Because you have seen me, you have believed; blessed are those who have not seen and yet have believed.”
dailies.enochActivity: Hold out your hands and say: Jesus is really alive.
dailies.elijah2: In John 20:28–29, what did Thomas say, and whom did Jesus bless?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: Thomas said, “My Lord and my God!” Jesus said, “blessed are those who have not seen and yet have believed.”
dailies.jordyn2: We have not seen Jesus the way Thomas did. How can John 20:29 be a blessing for you this week?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: Jesus blesses those who have not seen and yet have believed. We trust the witnesses God has given us in Scripture, and we believe that Jesus is risen even though we have not seen him with our eyes.
dailies.passageText: 24 Now Thomas (also known as Didymus), one of the Twelve, was not with the disciples when Jesus came. 25 So the other disciples told him, “We have seen the Lord!” But he said to them, “Unless I see the nail marks in his hands and put my finger where the nails were, and put my hand into his side, I will not believe.” 26 A week later his disciples were in the house again, and Thomas was with them. Though the doors were locked, Jesus came and stood among them and said, “Peace be with you!” 27 Then he said to Thomas, “Put your finger here; see my hands. Reach out your hand and put it into my side. Stop doubting and believe.” 28 Thomas said to him, “My Lord and my God!” 29 Then Jesus told him, “Because you have seen me, you have believed; blessed are those who have not seen and yet have believed.”

dailies.label: Day 6 · Prayer
dailies.focus: The risen Jesus stands among his friends, says “Peace be with you,” and sends them.
dailies.verse: Again Jesus said, “Peace be with you! As the Father has sent me, I am sending you.”
dailies.enoch: Hold out your hands like a greeting and say, “Peace be with you.”
dailies.elijah: In John 20:19, what did Jesus say when he came and stood among the disciples?
dailies.elijahAnswer: “Peace be with you!” (John 20:19).
dailies.jordyn: The doors were locked for fear, and Jesus came and said, “Peace be with you!” (John 20:19). How is his peace different from just feeling safe behind a locked door?
dailies.jordynAnswer: His peace comes with him, even when the doors are locked. Then he sends them: “As the Father has sent me, I am sending you” (John 20:21). Peace is not only for hiding. It is for going.
dailies.action: Pray “Peace be with you” for someone who is afraid, and tell them Jesus is alive.
dailies.prayer: Jesus, thank you that you stand among your friends and say, “Peace be with you.” Give us your peace, and send us to tell that you are risen. In your name, Amen.
dailies.teach: On the evening of that first day of the week, the disciples were together with the doors locked for fear. Jesus came and stood among them and said, “Peace be with you!” Again he said, “Peace be with you! As the Father has sent me, I am sending you.” In Luke, he stands among them and says, “Peace be with you.” He tells them they are witnesses of these things, and that he is going to send what the Father has promised. The risen Jesus gives peace, and he sends his friends.
dailies.enochActivity: Sit still for a quiet moment with a grown-up and whisper: Jesus, give us your peace.
dailies.elijah2: In Luke 24:48–49, what does Jesus call his friends, and what does he promise to send?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: He says, “You are witnesses of these things.” He is going to send what the Father has promised (Luke 24:48–49).
dailies.jordyn2: How does “Peace be with you” and “I am sending you” get us ready to talk about the church next week?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: The risen Jesus gathers his friends, gives them peace, and sends them as witnesses (John 20:21; Luke 24:48). Next week we will see how those friends become a family: the church, God’s family.
dailies.passageText: 19 On the evening of that first day of the week, when the disciples were together, with the doors locked for fear of the Jewish leaders, Jesus came and stood among them and said, “Peace be with you!” 20 After he said this, he showed them his hands and side. The disciples were overjoyed when they saw the Lord. 21 Again Jesus said, “Peace be with you! As the Father has sent me, I am sending you.” 22 And with that he breathed on them and said, “Receive the Holy Spirit. 23 If you forgive anyone’s sins, their sins are forgiven; if you do not forgive them, they are not forgiven.” 36 While they were still talking about this, Jesus himself stood among them and said to them, “Peace be with you.” 37 They were startled and frightened, thinking they saw a ghost. 38 He said to them, “Why are you troubled, and why do doubts rise in your minds? 39 Look at my hands and my feet. It is I myself! Touch me and see; a ghost does not have flesh and bones, as you see I have.” 40 When he had said this, he showed them his hands and feet. 41 And while they still did not believe it because of joy and amazement, he asked them, “Do you have anything here to eat?” 42 They gave him a piece of broiled fish, 43 and he took it and ate it in their presence. 44 He said to them, “This is what I told you while I was still with you: Everything must be fulfilled that is written about me in the Law of Moses, the Prophets and the Psalms.” 45 Then he opened their minds so they could understand the Scriptures. 46 He told them, “This is what is written: The Messiah will suffer and rise from the dead on the third day, 47 and repentance for the forgiveness of sins will be preached in his name to all nations, beginning at Jerusalem. 48 You are witnesses of these things. 49 I am going to send you what my Father has promised; but stay in the city until you have been clothed with power from on high.”

dailies.label: Day 7 · Recap
dailies.focus: Of first importance: Christ died for our sins, was buried, and was raised on the third day. He appeared, and he is the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep.
dailies.verse: But Christ has indeed been raised from the dead, the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep.
dailies.enoch: Give a grown-up a hug and say: Jesus is risen, and he is alive!
dailies.elijah: In 1 Corinthians 15:3–4, what three things does Paul pass on as of first importance?
dailies.elijahAnswer: That Christ died for our sins according to the Scriptures, that he was buried, and that he was raised on the third day according to the Scriptures.
dailies.jordyn: Paul says Christ appeared to many witnesses (1 Corinthians 15:5–8), and that he is “the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep” (1 Corinthians 15:20). What hope does that give?
dailies.jordynAnswer: Jesus really rose, and many people saw him. Firstfruits means more life is coming: “For as in Adam all die, so in Christ all will be made alive” (1 Corinthians 15:22).
dailies.action: Tell someone the good news of first importance: Jesus died, was buried, and was raised. Next week we will see how his friends become the church, God’s family.
dailies.prayer: Father, thank you that Jesus died for our sins, was buried, and was raised on the third day. He is not here; he has risen, just as he said. Give us his peace, and make us ready to live as his family. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
dailies.teach: This week we learned that Jesus is risen. The tomb is empty: “He is not here; he has risen, just as he said.” He met Mary, walked to Emmaus, stood among his friends, and said, “Peace be with you.” Paul says this is of first importance: Christ died for our sins, was buried, and was raised on the third day, and he appeared. Christ has indeed been raised from the dead, the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep. Next we will see how his friends become a family: the church, God’s family.
dailies.enochActivity: Wave and say: Jesus is alive, and he gives us peace!
dailies.elijah2: In 1 Corinthians 15:22, what two things does Paul set side by side?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: “For as in Adam all die, so in Christ all will be made alive.”
dailies.jordyn2: What is one way you will live this week like someone who belongs to the risen Jesus, as we get ready to talk about the church?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: Answers will vary: telling someone Jesus is risen, receiving his peace, trusting him though we have not seen him, or looking toward his family, the church. The same risen Jesus who met his friends still gathers and sends them.
dailies.passageText: 3 For what I received I passed on to you as of first importance: that Christ died for our sins according to the Scriptures, 4 that he was buried, that he was raised on the third day according to the Scriptures, 5 and that he appeared to Cephas, and then to the Twelve. 6 After that, he appeared to more than five hundred of the brothers and sisters at the same time, most of whom are still living, though some have fallen asleep. 7 Then he appeared to James, then to all the apostles, 8 and last of all he appeared to me also, as to one abnormally born. 20 But Christ has indeed been raised from the dead, the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep. 21 For since death came through a man, the resurrection of the dead comes also through a man. 22 For as in Adam all die, so in Christ all will be made alive.

weeks.title: The church: God's family
weeks.selectLabel: Week 22 · The church: God's family
weeks.nextUp: Week 23 · Jesus goes back to heaven
weeks.bigIdea: The church is God’s family. Jesus says, “Love one another.” We are members of his household, and his friends devote themselves to the apostles’ teaching, to fellowship, to the breaking of bread, and to prayer.
weeks.scheduleNote: This is the Week 22 family lesson. The short daily bites are Days 2–7.

howSteps.title: Read together
howSteps.detail: Open the Read tab and read John 13:34–35 out loud, then Ephesians 2:19–22, then Acts 2:42–47.

howSteps.title: Talk it through
howSteps.detail: Still on Read, walk through the kid-language explanation so everyone gets the picture.

howSteps.title: Age parts

readings.text: 34 “A new command I give you: Love one another. As I have loved you, so you must love one another. 35 By this everyone will know that you are my disciples, if you love one another.”

19 Consequently, you are no longer foreigners and strangers, but fellow citizens with God’s people and also members of his household, 20 built on the foundation of the apostles and prophets, with Christ Jesus himself as the chief cornerstone. 21 In him the whole building is joined together and rises to become a holy temple in the Lord. 22 And in him you too are being built together to become a dwelling in which God lives by his Spirit.

42 They devoted themselves to the apostles’ teaching and to fellowship, to the breaking of bread and to prayer. 43 Everyone was filled with awe at the many wonders and signs performed by the apostles. 44 All the believers were together and had everything in common. 45 They sold property and possessions to give to anyone who had need. 46 Every day they continued to meet together in the temple courts. They broke bread in their homes and ate together with glad and sincere hearts, 47 praising God and enjoying the favor of all the people. And the Lord added to their number daily those who were being saved.

story: Last week we heard the good news: Jesus is risen. He stood among his friends, said, “Peace be with you,” and sent them to tell that he is alive. This week we see how those friends become a family: the church, God’s family.

Before he went to the cross, Jesus gave his friends a new command: “Love one another. As I have loved you, so you must love one another. By this everyone will know that you are my disciples, if you love one another.” The church is not a club you join to look impressive. It is a family that loves the way Jesus loves.

Paul writes to the church that “you are no longer foreigners and strangers, but fellow citizens with God’s people and also members of his household,” and that in Jesus we belong. We are being built together to become a dwelling in which God lives by his Spirit. No one in this family is a stranger at the door.

This is what that family looked like. They devoted themselves to the apostles’ teaching and to fellowship, to the breaking of bread and to prayer. All the believers were together and had everything in common. They broke bread in their homes and ate together with glad and sincere hearts, praising God. And the Lord added to their number daily those who were being saved.
So we love one another, we belong to God’s household, and we keep meeting, learning, sharing, and praying. Next week we will see Jesus go back to heaven, and we will hear that he will come again.
weeks.enochLine: The church is God’s family, and we belong!
enochActivities: Activity: A family circle. Help a grown-up hold hands in a circle and say: We are God’s family!
Activity: Love one another. Give someone a hug, a smile, or a share of a snack, and say: Jesus loves you.
elijahQuestions: In John 13:34, what new command did Jesus give his friends?
In Ephesians 2:19, what does Paul say we are, if we are no longer foreigners and strangers?
In Acts 2:42, what four things did the believers devote themselves to?
In Acts 2:46, where did they break bread, and how did they eat together?
jordynQuestions: Jesus says everyone will know we are his disciples “if you love one another” (John 13:35). What makes that different from just being nice once in a while?
Ephesians 2:19 says we are members of his household. How does that change the way you think about church — not as a place you visit, but as a family you belong to?

The first believers devoted themselves to teaching, fellowship, breaking bread, and prayer (Acts 2:42). Which of those do you most want to practice this week, and how does this family get us ready for next week, when Jesus goes back to heaven?
weeks.jordynApplication: The church is God’s family (Ephesians 2:19; Acts 2:42). This week, love someone in the family the way Jesus loved you, and keep meeting, learning, and praying together. Next week we will see Jesus go back to heaven.
elijahAnswers: “Love one another. As I have loved you, so you must love one another.” (John 13:34).
“fellow citizens with God’s people and also members of his household” (Ephesians 2:19).
The apostles’ teaching, fellowship, the breaking of bread, and prayer (Acts 2:42).
They broke bread in their homes and ate together with glad and sincere hearts (Acts 2:46).
jordynAnswers: Jesus ties our love to his love: “As I have loved you, so you must love one another” (John 13:34). It is a new command for a family, not a mood. People will know we belong to him by that love (John 13:35).
A visitor can come and go. A member of the household belongs (Ephesians 2:19). Church is the family Jesus is building, and in him we are not strangers.

Answers will vary among the four gifts in Acts 2:42. This family belongs to the risen Jesus, who will soon go back to heaven. We keep loving, belonging, and meeting as his people until he comes again.
weeks.applicationCheck: Ask her later in the week whether she practiced love in the family — a welcome, a share, a prayer, or staying to learn. If it is fitting, share one way you belonged to God’s household this week too, and thank him together that you are not strangers.
weeks.prayer: Father, thank you that the church is your family. Teach us to love one another as Jesus has loved us. Thank you that we are members of your household, not strangers. Help us keep learning, sharing, meeting, and praying together. In Jesus’ name, Amen.

dailies.label: Day 2 · Passage
dailies.focus: Jesus gives his friends a new command: love one another as he has loved them.
dailies.verse: A new command I give you: Love one another. As I have loved you, so you must love one another.
dailies.enoch: Give someone a hug or a smile and say: Jesus loves you, and I love you too.
dailies.elijah: In John 13:35, how will everyone know that we are Jesus’ disciples?
dailies.elijahAnswer: “By this everyone will know that you are my disciples, if you love one another.”
dailies.jordyn: Jesus says, “As I have loved you, so you must love one another” (John 13:34). What is one way his love for you can shape how you treat someone in God’s family today?
dailies.jordynAnswer: His love is the pattern, not only the reason. We do not invent our own standard. We love as he has loved us — patiently, kindly, and in truth.
dailies.action: Do one loving thing today for someone in your family or church family, and tell them Jesus loves them.
dailies.prayer: Jesus, thank you for loving us first. Help us love one another as you have loved us, so that people will know we are yours. In your name, Amen.
dailies.teach: Jesus said, “A new command I give you: Love one another. As I have loved you, so you must love one another. By this everyone will know that you are my disciples, if you love one another.” The church is God’s family, and this is the family’s way: we love each other with the love we have first received from Jesus.
dailies.enochActivity: Help a grown-up draw a heart and say: Love one another.
dailies.elijah2: In John 13:34, what two things does Jesus say about this new command?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: He gives it: “Love one another.” And he shows the pattern: “As I have loved you, so you must love one another.”
dailies.jordyn2: Why does Jesus call this a new command, if loving your neighbor was already in the law?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: The measure is new: “As I have loved you, so you must love one another.” His disciples are a family known by that love, not only by a rule they already knew.
dailies.passageText: 34 “A new command I give you: Love one another. As I have loved you, so you must love one another. 35 By this everyone will know that you are my disciples, if you love one another.”

dailies.label: Day 3 · Game
dailies.focus: God’s family practices love: we welcome, share, and treat one another as people who belong.
dailies.verse: By this everyone will know that you are my disciples, if you love one another.
dailies.enoch: Play a welcome game: open your arms at the door and say: You belong! We are God’s family!
dailies.elijah: In John 13:34, whose love is the pattern for our love?
dailies.elijahAnswer: Jesus’ love: “As I have loved you, so you must love one another.”
dailies.jordyn: If someone new walked into your church family this week, what would “love one another” look like in a real welcome, not only a wave?
dailies.jordynAnswer: Answers will vary: sit with them, share, learn their name, pray for them, or make sure they are not left standing alone. Love is how people know we belong to Jesus (John 13:35).
dailies.action: Welcome someone today — at home, at the table, or at church — as a member of the family, not as a stranger.
dailies.prayer: Father, thank you that we belong in your family. Teach us to welcome and to love, so that everyone can see we are Jesus’ disciples. In his name, Amen.
dailies.teach: Jesus’ new command is not only words. “Love one another” looks like a welcome, a share, a seat at the table. This is how everyone will know we are his disciples. The church is God’s family, and families practice love on ordinary days, not only on special ones.
dailies.enochActivity: Share a snack with someone and say: God’s family shares.
dailies.elijah2: Why does Jesus say “Love one another,” not only love people in general?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: He is talking to his friends as a family. We must love one another — the people Jesus has put with us — as he has loved us (John 13:34–35).
dailies.jordyn2: How can a family “game” of welcome actually be a way of obeying Jesus, not only playing?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: Practicing a welcome trains our hearts to treat people as members of the household, not as interruptions. The game is practice for the real command: love one another.
dailies.passageText: 34 “A new command I give you: Love one another. As I have loved you, so you must love one another. 35 By this everyone will know that you are my disciples, if you love one another.”

dailies.label: Day 4 · Passage
dailies.focus: In Jesus we are not foreigners or strangers. We are members of God’s household.
dailies.verse: you are no longer foreigners and strangers, but fellow citizens with God’s people and also members of his household
dailies.enoch: Point to your house, then to your heart, and say: I belong in God’s family.
dailies.elijah: In Ephesians 2:19, what two things are we, if we are no longer foreigners and strangers?
dailies.elijahAnswer: “fellow citizens with God’s people and also members of his household,”
dailies.jordyn: Ephesians 2:21–22 says we are being built together to become a dwelling in which God lives by his Spirit. What does it mean that God is building you into this house with other people, not by yourself?
dailies.jordynAnswer: The church is not a pile of separate stones. In Jesus we are “being built together to become a dwelling in which God lives by his Spirit.” Belonging to him means belonging with his people.
dailies.action: Tell someone today: You belong. We are members of God’s household.
dailies.prayer: Father, thank you that in Jesus we are not strangers. We are members of your household. Build us together, and live among us by your Spirit. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
dailies.teach: Paul says, “you are no longer foreigners and strangers, but fellow citizens with God’s people and also members of his household,” The church is God’s family and God’s house. In Jesus we are being built together to become a dwelling in which God lives by his Spirit. No one who belongs to Jesus is left outside the door.
dailies.enochActivity: Help a grown-up stack blocks into a little house and say: God is building his family.
dailies.elijah2: In Ephesians 2:20, what is the church built on?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: It is “built on the foundation of the apostles and prophets, with Christ Jesus himself as the chief cornerstone.”
dailies.jordyn2: If Jesus is the chief cornerstone (Ephesians 2:20), what happens to a church family that tries to build on something else — a favorite leader, a feeling, or a crowd?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: The house will not stand true. The family belongs together only because it is built on Jesus, with the foundation of the apostles and prophets. He holds the household in place.
dailies.passageText: 19 Consequently, you are no longer foreigners and strangers, but fellow citizens with God’s people and also members of his household, 20 built on the foundation of the apostles and prophets, with Christ Jesus himself as the chief cornerstone. 21 In him the whole building is joined together and rises to become a holy temple in the Lord. 22 And in him you too are being built together to become a dwelling in which God lives by his Spirit.

dailies.label: Day 5 · Challenge
dailies.focus: God’s family is one body with many parts. Each one belongs, and each one is needed.
dailies.verse: Now you are the body of Christ, and each one of you is a part of it.
dailies.enoch: Wiggle your fingers and toes and say: Many parts, one body. I belong!
dailies.elijah: In 1 Corinthians 12:27, what does Paul say you are, and what is each one of you?
dailies.elijahAnswer: “Now you are the body of Christ, and each one of you is a part of it.”
dailies.jordyn: Paul says the body is not made of one part but of many (1 Corinthians 12:14). What is the danger of thinking, “I do not belong to the body,” or of thinking, “I don’t need you!”?
dailies.jordynAnswer: If you say you don’t belong, you talk as if the body can throw a part away. If you say you don’t need others, you talk as if one part could be the whole body. In Christ, every part is needed, and no one is leftover.
dailies.action: Thank one person in God’s family today for the part they are, and ask how you can help.
dailies.prayer: Father, thank you that we are the body of Christ, and each one of us is a part of it. Teach us not to hide, and not to look down on anyone. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
dailies.teach: Just as a body, though one, has many parts, so it is with Christ. The eye cannot say to the hand, “I don’t need you!” And the head cannot say to the feet, “I don’t need you!” God has placed the parts in the body, every one of them, just as he wanted them to be. “Now you are the body of Christ, and each one of you is a part of it.” In God’s family, you belong, and you are needed.
dailies.enochActivity: Do a simple team job with a grown-up — one holds, one places — and say: We need each other.
dailies.elijah2: In 1 Corinthians 12:18, who decided where each part should be?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: “God has placed the parts in the body, every one of them, just as he wanted them to be.”
dailies.jordyn2: How does “each one of you is a part of it” (1 Corinthians 12:27) help a shy person and a strong person in the same church family?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: The shy person is not extra. The strong person is not the whole body. Both belong, and both are needed, because God placed every part just as he wanted.
dailies.passageText: 12 Just as a body, though one, has many parts, but all its many parts form one body, so it is with Christ. 13 For we were all baptized by one Spirit so as to form one body—whether Jews or Gentiles, slave or free—and we were all given the one Spirit to drink. 14 Even so the body is not made up of one part but of many. 15 Now if the foot should say, “Because I am not a hand, I do not belong to the body,” it would not for that reason stop being part of the body. 16 And if the ear should say, “Because I am not an eye, I do not belong to the body,” it would not for that reason stop being part of the body. 17 If the whole body were an eye, where would the sense of hearing be? If the whole body were an ear, where would the sense of smell be? 18 But in fact God has placed the parts in the body, every one of them, just as he wanted them to be. 19 If they were all one part, where would the body be? 20 As it is, there are many parts, but one body. 21 The eye cannot say to the hand, “I don’t need you!” And the head cannot say to the feet, “I don’t need you!” 22 On the contrary, those parts of the body that seem to be weaker are indispensable, 23 and the parts that we think are less honorable we treat with special honor. And the parts that are unpresentable are treated with special modesty, 24 while our presentable parts need no special treatment. But God has put the body together, giving greater honor to the parts that lacked it, 25 so that there should be no division in the body, but that its parts should have equal concern for each other. 26 If one part suffers, every part suffers with it; if one part is honored, every part rejoices with it. 27 Now you are the body of Christ, and each one of you is a part of it.

dailies.label: Day 6 · Prayer
dailies.focus: God’s family devotes itself to the apostles’ teaching, to fellowship, to the breaking of bread, and to prayer.
dailies.verse: They devoted themselves to the apostles’ teaching and to fellowship, to the breaking of bread and to prayer.
dailies.enoch: Fold your hands with a grown-up and say: We pray together. We are God’s family.
dailies.elijah: In Acts 2:44, how were the believers together?
dailies.elijahAnswer: “All the believers were together and had everything in common.”
dailies.jordyn: They met in the temple courts and broke bread in their homes with glad and sincere hearts (Acts 2:46). Why does God’s family need both the large gathering and the table at home?
dailies.jordynAnswer: The family learns and praises together, and it also shares life up close — eating, praying, and caring in homes. Both belong to a household, not only to a crowd.
dailies.action: Pray today with someone in your family, and thank God that the church is his household.
dailies.prayer: Father, thank you for a family that learns, shares, eats, and prays together. Make our hearts glad and sincere, and add to your family those who are being saved. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
dailies.teach: The first believers devoted themselves to the apostles’ teaching and to fellowship, to the breaking of bread and to prayer. They were together and had everything in common. Every day they continued to meet together in the temple courts. They broke bread in their homes and ate together with glad and sincere hearts, praising God. And the Lord added to their number daily those who were being saved. This is what God’s family looks like.
dailies.enochActivity: Sit at the table with a grown-up, break a piece of bread or a cracker, and thank God for his family.
dailies.elijah2: In Acts 2:47, what did the Lord do as they praised God?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: “And the Lord added to their number daily those who were being saved.”
dailies.jordyn2: How does a family that prays and meets together get us ready for next week, when we will see Jesus go back to heaven?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: Jesus’ friends are already a family — learning, sharing, and praying. Next week he goes back to heaven, and this family will keep belonging to him until he comes again.
dailies.passageText: 42 They devoted themselves to the apostles’ teaching and to fellowship, to the breaking of bread and to prayer. 43 Everyone was filled with awe at the many wonders and signs performed by the apostles. 44 All the believers were together and had everything in common. 45 They sold property and possessions to give to anyone who had need. 46 Every day they continued to meet together in the temple courts. They broke bread in their homes and ate together with glad and sincere hearts, 47 praising God and enjoying the favor of all the people. And the Lord added to their number daily those who were being saved.

dailies.label: Day 7 · Recap
dailies.focus: The church is God’s family: one in heart, built by Jesus, not giving up meeting together.
dailies.verse: All the believers were one in heart and mind. No one claimed that any of their possessions was their own, but they shared everything they had.
dailies.enoch: Give a grown-up a hug and say: We are God’s family, and Jesus is building his church!
dailies.elijah: In Matthew 16:18, what does Jesus say he will build?
dailies.elijahAnswer: “I will build my church, and the gates of Hades will not overcome it.”
dailies.jordyn: Hebrews 10:24–25 says we should consider how to spur one another on toward love and good deeds, not giving up meeting together. Why is that a fitting end to a week about God’s family?
dailies.jordynAnswer: A family keeps showing up. We belong to one another, so we do not give up meeting, and we keep encouraging one another as we look to the Day.
dailies.action: Plan to meet with God’s family, and tell someone: Jesus is building his church, and we belong.
dailies.prayer: Father, thank you that the church is your family. Jesus is building his church, and we are members of your household. Teach us to love one another and not give up meeting together. Get our hearts ready for next week, when we see Jesus go back to heaven. In his name, Amen.
dailies.teach: This week we learned that the church is God’s family. Jesus said, “Love one another.” We are members of his household, not strangers. The first believers devoted themselves to teaching, fellowship, breaking bread, and prayer. They were one in heart and mind, and they shared. Jesus said, “I will build my church, and the gates of Hades will not overcome it.” So we do not give up meeting together. Next week we will see Jesus go back to heaven, and we will hear that he will come again.
dailies.enochActivity: Wave and say: God’s family meets together, and we belong!
dailies.elijah2: In Hebrews 10:25, what should we not give up, and what should we keep doing?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: We should not give up meeting together, but keep encouraging one another — and all the more as we see the Day approaching.
dailies.jordyn2: What is one way you will live this week like a member of God’s household, as we get ready to see Jesus go back to heaven?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: Answers will vary: loving one another, welcoming someone, taking your part in the body, praying with the family, or not giving up meeting together. The same Jesus who is building his church will go back to heaven, and this family belongs to him.
dailies.passageText: All the believers were one in heart and mind. No one claimed that any of their possessions was their own, but they shared everything they had. And I tell you that you are Peter, and on this rock I will build my church, and the gates of Hades will not overcome it. And let us consider how we may spur one another on toward love and good deeds, not giving up meeting together, as some are in the habit of doing, but encouraging one another—and all the more as you see the Day approaching.

howSteps.title: Read together
howSteps.detail: Open the Read tab and read Acts 1:6–11 out loud, then Luke 24:50–53, then Matthew 28:16–20.

howSteps.title: Talk it through
howSteps.detail: Still on Read, walk through the kid-language explanation so everyone gets the picture.

readings.text: 6 Then they gathered around him and asked him, “Lord, are you at this time going to restore the kingdom to Israel?” 7 He said to them: “It is not for you to know the times or dates the Father has set by his own authority. 8 But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit comes on you; and you will be my witnesses in Jerusalem, and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the ends of the earth.” 9 After he said this, he was taken up before their very eyes, and a cloud hid him from their sight. 10 They were looking intently up into the sky as he was going, when suddenly two men dressed in white stood beside them. 11 “Men of Galilee,” they said, “why do you stand here looking into the sky? This same Jesus, who has been taken from you into heaven, will come back in the same way you have seen him go into heaven.”

50 When he had led them out to the vicinity of Bethany, he lifted up his hands and blessed them. 51 While he was blessing them, he left them and was taken up into heaven. 52 Then they worshiped him and returned to Jerusalem with great joy. 53 And they stayed continually at the temple, praising God.

16 Then the eleven disciples went to Galilee, to the mountain where Jesus had told them to go. 17 When they saw him, they worshiped him; but some doubted. 18 Then Jesus came to them and said, “All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to me. 19 Therefore go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, 20 and teaching them to obey everything I have commanded you. And surely I am with you always, to the very end of the age.”

story: Last week we learned that the church is God’s family. Jesus’ friends loved one another, belonged to his household, and kept meeting, learning, sharing, and praying. This week we see Jesus go back to heaven, and we hear the promise that he will come again.

After he rose from the dead, Jesus appeared to his friends for forty days and spoke about the kingdom of God. He told them not to leave Jerusalem, but to wait for the gift his Father promised. They asked if he was going to restore the kingdom to Israel at that time. He said it was not for them to know the times or dates the Father has set. Then, after he said this, he was taken up before their very eyes, and a cloud hid him from their sight.

They were looking intently up into the sky as he was going, when suddenly two men dressed in white stood beside them. “Men of Galilee,” they said, “why do you stand here looking into the sky? This same Jesus, who has been taken from you into heaven, will come back in the same way you have seen him go into heaven.”

Luke also tells us that Jesus led them out toward Bethany, lifted up his hands, and blessed them. While he was blessing them, he left them and was taken up into heaven. Then they worshiped him and returned to Jerusalem with great joy, and they stayed continually at the temple, praising God.

Before he went, Jesus said, “All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to me.” He sent them to make disciples of all nations, and he promised, “And surely I am with you always, to the very end of the age.” So Jesus went back to heaven, and he will come again. He is with us always. He told his friends to wait for the Father’s promise. Next week we will see God send the Holy Spirit, and the church will begin in a new way.
weeks.enochLine: Jesus went back to heaven, and he will come again!
enochActivities: Activity: Look up. Help a grown-up look up for a moment, then say: Jesus went back to heaven, and he will come again!
Activity: Jesus is with us. Hold a grown-up’s hand and say: Jesus is with me always.
elijahQuestions: In Acts 1:9, what happened after Jesus finished speaking?
In Acts 1:11, what did the two men dressed in white say this same Jesus will do?
In Luke 24:50–51, what was Jesus doing when he was taken up into heaven?
In Matthew 28:20, what promise does Jesus give his friends?
elijahAnswers: He was taken up before their very eyes, and a cloud hid him from their sight (Acts 1:9).
“This same Jesus, who has been taken from you into heaven, will come back in the same way you have seen him go into heaven.” (Acts 1:11).
He lifted up his hands and blessed them, and while he was blessing them, he left them and was taken up into heaven (Luke 24:50–51).
“And surely I am with you always, to the very end of the age.” (Matthew 28:20).
jordynQuestions: The two men asked, “why do you stand here looking into the sky?” (Acts 1:11). What should the friends remember, even after Jesus is hidden from their sight?
Luke 24:52 says they worshiped him and returned to Jerusalem with great joy. Why is joy a fitting response if Jesus has gone away?

Jesus says all authority has been given to him, and “I am with you always” (Matthew 28:18, 20). How does that promise help you wait for the Father’s gift, which he told them not to leave Jerusalem without?
jordynAnswers: Jesus has been taken into heaven, and he will come back in the same way they saw him go (Acts 1:11). They do not lose him forever. A cloud hid him, but the promise stands.
He blessed them as he was taken up (Luke 24:50–51). He is not gone as if he were defeated. They worship him and return with great joy because he is Lord in heaven, and he will come again.

The one with all authority is also the one who stays with them. He told them to wait for the Father’s promise (Acts 1:4). They can wait with courage because he is with them always, even as they look for the gift still to come.
weeks.jordynApplication: Jesus went back to heaven, and he will come again (Acts 1:11). This week, remember that he is with you always (Matthew 28:20), and wait with hope for the Father’s promise. Next week we will see God send the Holy Spirit.
weeks.applicationCheck: Ask her later in the week whether she remembered that Jesus is with her always — at home, at school, or when she felt alone. If it is fitting, thank him together that he went back to heaven and will come again.
weeks.prayer: Father, thank you that Jesus was taken up into heaven and that he will come again. Thank you that he blessed his friends and is with us always. Help us wait for your promise with joy and trust. In Jesus’ name, Amen.

dailies.label: Day 2 · Passage
dailies.focus: Jesus is taken up, and a cloud hides him from their sight.
dailies.verse: After he said this, he was taken up before their very eyes, and a cloud hid him from their sight.
dailies.enoch: Look up for a moment, then wave and say: Jesus went back to heaven!
dailies.elijah: In Acts 1:6, what did the friends ask Jesus?
dailies.elijahAnswer: They asked him, “Lord, are you at this time going to restore the kingdom to Israel?”
dailies.jordyn: Jesus says it is not for them to know the times or dates the Father has set by his own authority (Acts 1:7). What does that teach you about waiting when you want God to act right now?
dailies.jordynAnswer: The times belong to the Father. The friends wanted the kingdom now, but Jesus pointed them to the Father’s authority and to the work still ahead. We can trust the Father’s timing instead of demanding our own.
dailies.action: Read Acts 1:6–11 together, then tell someone: Jesus was taken up, and a cloud hid him from their sight.
dailies.prayer: Father, thank you that Jesus was taken up before their very eyes. Help us trust your timing and remember that he is in heaven. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
dailies.teach: The friends asked if Jesus was going to restore the kingdom to Israel at that time. He said it was not for them to know the times or dates the Father has set by his own authority. Then, after he said this, he was taken up before their very eyes, and a cloud hid him from their sight. Jesus went back to heaven. The story is not over, because he will come again.
dailies.enochActivity: Help a grown-up make a small cloud with your hands, then open them and say: A cloud hid him, and Jesus went back to heaven.
dailies.elijah2: In Acts 1:9, what hid Jesus from their sight?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: A cloud hid him from their sight.
dailies.jordyn2: The friends wanted the kingdom restored at that time (Acts 1:6). Jesus was taken up instead. How does his going to heaven still keep the hope of the kingdom alive?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: He is not leaving the kingdom behind. The Father has set the times, and Jesus goes to heaven as Lord. Next they will be told that this same Jesus will come back.
dailies.passageText: 6 Then they gathered around him and asked him, “Lord, are you at this time going to restore the kingdom to Israel?” 7 He said to them: “It is not for you to know the times or dates the Father has set by his own authority. 8 But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit comes on you; and you will be my witnesses in Jerusalem, and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the ends of the earth.” 9 After he said this, he was taken up before their very eyes, and a cloud hid him from their sight. 10 They were looking intently up into the sky as he was going, when suddenly two men dressed in white stood beside them. 11 “Men of Galilee,” they said, “why do you stand here looking into the sky? This same Jesus, who has been taken from you into heaven, will come back in the same way you have seen him go into heaven.”

dailies.label: Day 3 · Game
dailies.focus: They look up as he is going, and they hear that he will come again.
dailies.verse: This same Jesus, who has been taken from you into heaven, will come back in the same way you have seen him go into heaven.
dailies.enoch: Look up, then look at a grown-up and say: Jesus will come again!
dailies.elijah: In Acts 1:10, what were the friends doing as Jesus was going, and who stood beside them?
dailies.elijahAnswer: They were looking intently up into the sky as he was going, when suddenly two men dressed in white stood beside them.
dailies.jordyn: The two men ask, “why do you stand here looking into the sky?” (Acts 1:11). What is the difference between remembering that Jesus will come again and only staring at the place he left?
dailies.jordynAnswer: Looking up without hope can freeze you in place. The message is not merely to keep staring at the sky. It is that this same Jesus will come back in the same way they saw him go. We remember, and then we live as his people until he comes.
dailies.action: Play a simple look-up-then-look-ahead: look at the sky for a moment, then look at each other and say, Jesus will come again.
dailies.prayer: Father, thank you that this same Jesus will come back in the same way they saw him go. Keep our eyes full of that hope, and help us live for him until he comes. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
dailies.teach: They were looking intently up into the sky as he was going, when suddenly two men dressed in white stood beside them. “Men of Galilee,” they said, “why do you stand here looking into the sky? This same Jesus, who has been taken from you into heaven, will come back in the same way you have seen him go into heaven.” Jesus went back to heaven, and he will come again.
dailies.enochActivity: Help a grown-up look up, then point forward and say: He will come again!
dailies.elijah2: In Acts 1:11, what two things do the men say about this same Jesus?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: He has been taken from them into heaven, and he will come back in the same way they have seen him go into heaven.
dailies.jordyn2: The promise is that he will come back “in the same way you have seen him go into heaven.” What does that tell you about the Jesus who will return?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: It is this same Jesus — the one they knew, who was taken up before their eyes. The return is not a different Lord. The one who went will come back.
dailies.passageText: 10 They were looking intently up into the sky as he was going, when suddenly two men dressed in white stood beside them. 11 “Men of Galilee,” they said, “why do you stand here looking into the sky? This same Jesus, who has been taken from you into heaven, will come back in the same way you have seen him go into heaven.”

dailies.label: Day 4 · Passage
dailies.focus: Jesus blesses them, is taken up, and they return with great joy.
dailies.verse: While he was blessing them, he left them and was taken up into heaven.
dailies.enoch: Hold your hands out like a blessing and say: Jesus blessed them!
dailies.elijah: In Luke 24:50, where did Jesus lead them, and what did he do with his hands?
dailies.elijahAnswer: He led them out to the vicinity of Bethany, and he lifted up his hands and blessed them.
dailies.jordyn: Luke 24:52 says they worshiped him and returned to Jerusalem with great joy. What does their worship tell you about who Jesus is, even after he is taken up?
dailies.jordynAnswer: They worship him. That is what you do for the Lord. He has been taken up into heaven, and they answer with worship and great joy, not only with sadness that he is out of sight.
dailies.action: Read Luke 24:50–53, then tell someone: While he was blessing them, he was taken up into heaven.
dailies.prayer: Jesus, thank you that you blessed your friends as you were taken up. Teach us to worship you with joy, like they did. In your name, Amen.
dailies.teach: When Jesus had led them out to the vicinity of Bethany, he lifted up his hands and blessed them. While he was blessing them, he left them and was taken up into heaven. Then they worshiped him and returned to Jerusalem with great joy, and they stayed continually at the temple, praising God. Jesus went back to heaven with a blessing, and his friends answered with worship and joy.
dailies.enochActivity: Help a grown-up lift your hands and say: We worship Jesus with joy!
dailies.elijah2: In Luke 24:52–53, what did the friends do after Jesus was taken up?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: They worshiped him and returned to Jerusalem with great joy, and they stayed continually at the temple, praising God.
dailies.jordyn2: Why is it important that Jesus was blessing them at the very moment he was taken up (Luke 24:51)?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: He does not leave them with an empty goodbye. The last thing they see is their Lord blessing them as he goes to heaven. That blessing helps explain their great joy.
dailies.passageText: 50 When he had led them out to the vicinity of Bethany, he lifted up his hands and blessed them. 51 While he was blessing them, he left them and was taken up into heaven. 52 Then they worshiped him and returned to Jerusalem with great joy. 53 And they stayed continually at the temple, praising God.

dailies.label: Day 5 · Challenge
dailies.focus: All authority is his, and he is with us always.
dailies.verse: And surely I am with you always, to the very end of the age.
dailies.enoch: Hold a grown-up’s hand and say: Jesus is with me always.
dailies.elijah: In Matthew 28:18, what does Jesus say has been given to him?
dailies.elijahAnswer: “All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to me.”
dailies.jordyn: Jesus gives a great job: go and make disciples of all nations (Matthew 28:19). How does “I am with you always” make that job possible, not just heavy?
dailies.jordynAnswer: The command comes from the one who has all authority, and he does not send them alone. He will be with them to the very end of the age. The work is his, and his presence goes with them.
dailies.action: Tell someone today: Jesus has all authority, and he is with me always. Then do one kind thing in his name.
dailies.prayer: Jesus, you have all authority in heaven and on earth. Thank you that you are with us always. Help us obey you and make disciples, not in our own strength. In your name, Amen.
dailies.teach: The eleven disciples went to Galilee, to the mountain where Jesus had told them to go. Jesus came to them and said, “All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to me.” He sent them to go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them and teaching them to obey everything he has commanded. And he promised, “And surely I am with you always, to the very end of the age.” Jesus went back to heaven, but he has not left his friends alone.
dailies.enochActivity: Help a grown-up point up and then to your heart and say: All authority is his, and he is with me always.
dailies.elijah2: In Matthew 28:19, what does Jesus tell them to go and do?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: Go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit.
dailies.jordyn2: Jesus promises to be with his friends “to the very end of the age” (Matthew 28:20), even as he is taken up into heaven. How can both of those be true?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: He goes to heaven, and he remains with his people. His authority and his presence are not limited to one hillside in Galilee. He is with us always, even until he comes again.
dailies.passageText: 16 Then the eleven disciples went to Galilee, to the mountain where Jesus had told them to go. 17 When they saw him, they worshiped him; but some doubted. 18 Then Jesus came to them and said, “All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to me. 19 Therefore go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, 20 and teaching them to obey everything I have commanded you. And surely I am with you always, to the very end of the age.”

dailies.label: Day 6 · Prayer
dailies.focus: He goes to prepare a place, and it is for our good that he goes away.
dailies.verse: And if I go and prepare a place for you, I will come back and take you to be with me that you also may be where I am.
dailies.enoch: Fold your hands and say: Jesus, you are getting a place ready for us.
dailies.elijah: In John 14:2, what does Jesus say he is going to do in his Father’s house?
dailies.elijahAnswer: He is going there to prepare a place for them.
dailies.jordyn: In John 16:7 Jesus says, “it is for your good that I am going away.” How can his leaving be for their good, if they are filled with grief?
dailies.jordynAnswer: He is going to the Father, and unless he goes away, the Advocate will not come to them. If he goes, he will send him to them (John 16:7). His going is not abandonment. It is for their good, and he will come back.
dailies.action: Pray together: thank Jesus that he is preparing a place, and ask for help to wait for the Father’s promise.
dailies.prayer: Jesus, thank you that you went to prepare a place for us, and that you will come back and take us to be with you. Thank you that it is for our good that you went away. Help us wait for the Father’s promise. In your name, Amen.
dailies.teach: Jesus said, “Do not let your hearts be troubled.” He is going to his Father’s house to prepare a place, and he will come back and take his friends to be with him. He also said, “it is for your good that I am going away. Unless I go away, the Advocate will not come to you; but if I go, I will send him to you.” After he rose, he told them not to leave Jerusalem, but to wait for the gift his Father promised. We wait with him, because his going is for our good.
dailies.enochActivity: Help a grown-up sit still for a short prayer and say: We will wait for the Father’s promise.
dailies.elijah2: In Acts 1:4, what command did Jesus give while he was eating with them?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: “Do not leave Jerusalem, but wait for the gift my Father promised, which you have heard me speak about.”
dailies.jordyn2: Jesus tells them both to wait for the Father’s promise (Acts 1:4) and not to let their hearts be troubled (John 14:1). How do those two words belong together this week?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: Waiting does not have to mean a troubled heart. He is preparing a place, he will come back, and the gift the Father promised is coming. We wait because he is faithful, not because he has forgotten us.
dailies.passageText: 1 “Do not let your hearts be troubled. You believe in God; believe also in me. 2 My Father’s house has many rooms; if that were not so, would I have told you that I am going there to prepare a place for you? 3 And if I go and prepare a place for you, I will come back and take you to be with me that you also may be where I am. But very truly I tell you, it is for your good that I am going away. Unless I go away, the Advocate will not come to you; but if I go, I will send him to you. On one occasion, while he was eating with them, he gave them this command: “Do not leave Jerusalem, but wait for the gift my Father promised, which you have heard me speak about.

dailies.label: Day 7 · Recap
dailies.focus: Jesus went back to heaven, he will come again, and we wait for the Father’s promise.
dailies.verse: God has ascended amid shouts of joy, the LORD amid the sounding of trumpets.
dailies.enoch: Clap once and say: God has ascended! Jesus will come again!
dailies.elijah: In Psalm 47:5, what has God done amid shouts of joy?
dailies.elijahAnswer: “God has ascended amid shouts of joy, the LORD amid the sounding of trumpets.”
dailies.jordyn: This week Jesus was taken up, he promised to come again, and he said he is with us always. How does that get your heart ready for next week, when we will see the Father’s promise come?
dailies.jordynAnswer: He told them to wait for the gift the Father promised. He went away for their good, and he will send the Advocate. Next week we will see God send the Holy Spirit. We wait with joy, because Jesus is in heaven, he is with us always, and he will come again.
dailies.action: Tell someone the week’s big idea: Jesus went back to heaven, and he will come again. Then thank him that he is with us always.
dailies.prayer: Father, thank you that Jesus went back to heaven and that he will come again. Thank you that he is with us always. Get our hearts ready for next week, when we see you send the Holy Spirit. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
dailies.teach: This week we learned that Jesus went back to heaven, and he will come again. He was taken up, and a cloud hid him from their sight. Two men said this same Jesus will come back in the same way they saw him go. He blessed his friends, and they worshiped him with great joy. He has all authority, and he is with us always. He is preparing a place, and he told them to wait for the Father’s promise. The psalm says, “God has ascended amid shouts of joy, the LORD amid the sounding of trumpets.” Next week we will see God send the Holy Spirit, and the church will begin in a new way.
dailies.enochActivity: Help a grown-up look up, then clap and say: Jesus went back to heaven, and he will come again!
dailies.elijah2: In Acts 1:4 and John 16:7, what are the friends told to wait for, and why is Jesus’ going for their good?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: They are to wait for the gift the Father promised. Jesus said it is for their good that he is going away, because if he goes, he will send the Advocate to them.
dailies.jordyn2: Psalm 47:5 says God has ascended amid shouts of joy. How does that line help you hold together this week’s goodbye and this week’s hope?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: His going up is not a quiet defeat. It is the Lord ascending with joy. The friends return with great joy, and we wait for him to come again, and for the promise he told them to wait for.
dailies.passageText: God has ascended amid shouts of joy, the LORD amid the sounding of trumpets. “Men of Galilee,” they said, “why do you stand here looking into the sky? This same Jesus, who has been taken from you into heaven, will come back in the same way you have seen him go into heaven.” and teaching them to obey everything I have commanded you. And surely I am with you always, to the very end of the age.” On one occasion, while he was eating with them, he gave them this command: “Do not leave Jerusalem, but wait for the gift my Father promised, which you have heard me speak about.

weeks.title: Pentecost: the Holy Spirit comes
weeks.selectLabel: Week 24 · Pentecost: the Holy Spirit comes
weeks.nextUp: Week 25 · Peter and John at the temple
weeks.bigIdea: God sent the Holy Spirit, and the church began.
weeks.scheduleNote: This is the Week 24 family lesson. The short daily bites are Days 2–7.

howSteps.title: Read together
howSteps.detail: Open the Read tab and read Acts 2:1–12 out loud, then Acts 2:36–41, then John 14:16–18.

howSteps.title: Talk it through
howSteps.detail: Still on Read, walk through the kid-language explanation so everyone gets the picture.

howSteps.title: Age parts
howSteps.detail: Use Enoch, Elijah, and Jordyn tabs. Keep the Parent key open for yourself.

howSteps.title: Pray
howSteps.detail: Close with the short family prayer on the Prayer tab.

readings.text: 1 When the day of Pentecost came, they were all together in one place. 2 Suddenly a sound like the blowing of a violent wind came from heaven and filled the whole house where they were sitting. 3 They saw what seemed to be tongues of fire that separated and came to rest on each of them. 4 All of them were filled with the Holy Spirit and began to speak in other tongues as the Spirit enabled them. 5 Now there were staying in Jerusalem God-fearing Jews from every nation under heaven. 6 When they heard this sound, a crowd came together in bewilderment, because each one heard their own language being spoken. 7 Utterly amazed, they asked: “Aren’t all these who are speaking Galileans? 8 Then how is it that each of us hears them in our native language? 9 Parthians, Medes and Elamites; residents of Mesopotamia, Judea and Cappadocia, Pontus and Asia, 10 Phrygia and Pamphylia, Egypt and the parts of Libya near Cyrene; visitors from Rome 11 (both Jews and converts to Judaism); Cretans and Arabs—we hear them declaring the wonders of God in our own tongues!” 12 Amazed and perplexed, they asked one another, “What does this mean?”

36 “Therefore let all Israel be assured of this: God has made this Jesus, whom you crucified, both Lord and Messiah.” 37 When the people heard this, they were cut to the heart and said to Peter and the other apostles, “Brothers, what shall we do?” 38 Peter replied, “Repent and be baptized, every one of you, in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of your sins. And you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit. 39 The promise is for you and your children and for all who are far off—for all whom the Lord our God will call.” 40 With many other words he warned them; and he pleaded with them, “Save yourselves from this corrupt generation.” 41 Those who accepted his message were baptized, and about three thousand were added to their number that day.

16 And I will ask the Father, and he will give you another advocate to help you and be with you forever— 17 the Spirit of truth.
