The world cannot accept him, because it neither sees him nor knows him. But you know him, for he lives with you and will be in you. 18 I will not leave you as orphans; I will come to you.

story: Last week we saw Jesus go back to heaven. A cloud hid him, and two men said he will come again. He told his friends not to leave Jerusalem, but to wait for the gift his Father promised. This week the wait is over. God sends the Holy Spirit, and the church begins in a new way.

When the day of Pentecost came, they were all together in one place. Suddenly a sound like the blowing of a violent wind came from heaven and filled the whole house where they were sitting. They saw what seemed to be tongues of fire that separated and came to rest on each of them. All of them were filled with the Holy Spirit and began to speak in other tongues as the Spirit enabled them.

God-fearing Jews from every nation under heaven were staying in Jerusalem. A crowd came together in bewilderment, because each one heard their own language being spoken. They were amazed: “Aren’t all these who are speaking Galileans?” Yet they heard them declaring the wonders of God in their own tongues. Some asked, “What does this mean?” Some made fun of them. But God was keeping his promise.

Peter stood up and told them the truth about Jesus. Jesus of Nazareth was handed over, and they put him to death by nailing him to the cross. But God raised him from the dead. “Therefore let all Israel be assured of this: God has made this Jesus, whom you crucified, both Lord and Messiah.” When the people heard this, they were cut to the heart and said, “Brothers, what shall we do?” Peter replied, “Repent and be baptized, every one of you, in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of your sins. And you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit.” Those who accepted his message were baptized, and about three thousand were added to their number that day.

Jesus had said he would ask the Father, and the Father would give them another advocate to help them and be with them forever. He would not leave them as orphans. The gift came, the church began, and the friends became witnesses, just as Jesus had said. Next week we will see Peter and John at the temple, bold to heal and bold to say that Jesus saves.
weeks.enochLine: God sent his Holy Spirit, and the church began!
enochActivities: Activity: A soft wind. Help a grown-up fan a little breeze and say: God sent his Holy Spirit!
Activity: The family grew. Hold up three fingers, then open your hands wide and say: Many people believed, and the church began!
elijahQuestions: In Acts 2:2–3, what did they hear, and what did they see, when the day of Pentecost came?
In Acts 2:4, what happened when they were filled with the Holy Spirit?
In Acts 2:36, what does Peter say God has made this Jesus, whom they crucified?
In Acts 2:41, what happened to those who accepted Peter’s message?
elijahAnswers: A sound like the blowing of a violent wind came from heaven and filled the house, and they saw what seemed to be tongues of fire that came to rest on each of them (Acts 2:2–3).
They began to speak in other tongues as the Spirit enabled them (Acts 2:4).
“God has made this Jesus, whom you crucified, both Lord and Messiah.” (Acts 2:36).
They were baptized, and about three thousand were added to their number that day (Acts 2:41).
jordynQuestions: People from many nations heard the wonders of God in their own languages (Acts 2:6–11). What does that tell you about who this good news is for?
When the people were cut to the heart, they asked, “Brothers, what shall we do?” (Acts 2:37). What does Peter tell them to do, and what gift does he promise?
Jesus had told them to wait for the Father’s promise, and he said the Father would give them another advocate (Acts 1:4; John 14:16). How does Pentecost show that Jesus keeps his word?
jordynAnswers: The good news is not only for one town or one language. God wanted people from every nation under heaven to hear the wonders of God in words they could understand.
“Repent and be baptized, every one of you, in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of your sins. And you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit.” (Acts 2:38).
They waited, as he said, and the gift came. The Spirit was poured out, they became witnesses, and about three thousand were added. Jesus did not leave them as orphans. He kept his promise.
weeks.jordynApplication: God sent the Holy Spirit, and the church began (Acts 2:4, 41). This week, thank Jesus that he kept his promise, and ask the Spirit to help you be a witness where you are. Next week we will see Peter and John at the temple, bold to say that Jesus saves.
weeks.applicationCheck: Ask her later in the week whether she remembered that God has given his Spirit to his people — when she prayed, told the truth, or belonged with the church family. If it is fitting, thank him together that the church began by his gift, not by our power.
weeks.prayer: Father, thank you that you sent the Holy Spirit, just as Jesus promised. Thank you that Jesus is Lord and Messiah, and that so many believed and were baptized that day. Help us live as your people by your Spirit, and make us ready for next week. In Jesus’ name, Amen.

dailies.label: Day 2 · Passage
dailies.focus: The promised Spirit comes with a sound like wind, and what seemed to be tongues of fire.
dailies.verse: All of them were filled with the Holy Spirit and began to speak in other tongues as the Spirit enabled them.
dailies.enoch: Fan a little breeze and say: God sent his Holy Spirit!
dailies.elijah: In Acts 2:1, where were they when the day of Pentecost came?
dailies.elijahAnswer: They were all together in one place.
dailies.jordyn: Acts 2:3 says they saw what seemed to be tongues of fire that separated and came to rest on each of them. Why is it important to stay with those words, and not turn the day into a show we invent?
dailies.jordynAnswer: The Bible tells us what they saw and heard: a sound like a violent wind, and what seemed to be tongues of fire that came to rest on each of them. We receive the story as it is written. The center of the day is that they were filled with the Holy Spirit.
dailies.action: Read Acts 2:1–4 together, then tell someone: God sent his Holy Spirit, just as Jesus promised.
dailies.prayer: Father, thank you that the wait was not empty. You sent your Holy Spirit, and you filled your people. Help us love this gift and tell the story as the Bible tells it. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
dailies.teach: When the day of Pentecost came, they were all together in one place. Suddenly a sound like the blowing of a violent wind came from heaven and filled the whole house where they were sitting. They saw what seemed to be tongues of fire that separated and came to rest on each of them. All of them were filled with the Holy Spirit and began to speak in other tongues as the Spirit enabled them. The gift the Father promised had come.
dailies.enochActivity: Help a grown-up cup your hands like a small flame, then open them and say: The Holy Spirit came to rest on them.
dailies.elijah2: In Acts 2:2, what filled the whole house where they were sitting?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: A sound like the blowing of a violent wind came from heaven and filled the whole house.
dailies.jordyn2: Last week Jesus told them to wait for the Father’s promise. How does Acts 2:1–4 show that the wait was worth it?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: They were together, as he had told them, and the Spirit came. They were filled, and the church’s new beginning started with God’s gift, not with their own plan.
dailies.passageText: 1 When the day of Pentecost came, they were all together in one place. 2 Suddenly a sound like the blowing of a violent wind came from heaven and filled the whole house where they were sitting. 3 They saw what seemed to be tongues of fire that separated and came to rest on each of them. 4 All of them were filled with the Holy Spirit and began to speak in other tongues as the Spirit enabled them.

dailies.label: Day 3 · Game
dailies.focus: People from many nations hear the wonders of God in their own languages.
dailies.verse: we hear them declaring the wonders of God in our own tongues!
dailies.enoch: Point to a few places on a map or around the room and say: They heard the wonders of God!
dailies.elijah: In Acts 2:6, why did the crowd come together in bewilderment?
dailies.elijahAnswer: Because each one heard their own language being spoken.
dailies.jordyn: Some were amazed and asked, “What does this mean?” Some made fun of them (Acts 2:12–13). What is a humble way to hear a work of God you do not yet understand?
dailies.jordynAnswer: The amazed question is better than the joke. The Spirit enabled them to declare the wonders of God so that people from many nations could hear. We ask what it means, and we listen to what God is doing, instead of making fun.
dailies.action: Play a simple many-places-one-wonder: take turns naming a place or a language you know, then say together, We hear them declaring the wonders of God.
dailies.prayer: Father, thank you that people from many nations heard the wonders of God in their own languages. Help us honor this gift, and help us tell your wonders clearly too. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
dailies.teach: God-fearing Jews from every nation under heaven were staying in Jerusalem. When they heard this sound, a crowd came together in bewilderment, because each one heard their own language being spoken. They were amazed that Galileans were declaring the wonders of God in tongues they could understand. This was not a game and not a joke. God was making his wonders known to the nations.
dailies.enochActivity: Help a grown-up say a simple good-news line, then you say it back: God is wonderful!
dailies.elijah2: In Acts 2:7–8, what two questions did the amazed people ask?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: “Aren’t all these who are speaking Galileans?” And, “Then how is it that each of us hears them in our native language?”
dailies.jordyn2: Why does Acts 2:11 matter as much as the wind and the fire — that they heard them declaring the wonders of God?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: The Spirit’s gift had a purpose: the wonders of God were being declared in words people could understand. The sign points to the news, not to itself.
dailies.passageText: 5 Now there were staying in Jerusalem God-fearing Jews from every nation under heaven. 6 When they heard this sound, a crowd came together in bewilderment, because each one heard their own language being spoken. 7 Utterly amazed, they asked: “Aren’t all these who are speaking Galileans? 8 Then how is it that each of us hears them in our native language? 9 Parthians, Medes and Elamites; residents of Mesopotamia, Judea and Cappadocia, Pontus and Asia, 10 Phrygia and Pamphylia, Egypt and the parts of Libya near Cyrene; visitors from Rome 11 (both Jews and converts to Judaism); Cretans and Arabs—we hear them declaring the wonders of God in our own tongues!” 12 Amazed and perplexed, they asked one another, “What does this mean?”

dailies.label: Day 4 · Passage
dailies.focus: Peter preaches Jesus: crucified, raised, and made Lord and Messiah.
dailies.verse: God has made this Jesus, whom you crucified, both Lord and Messiah.
dailies.enoch: Tap your heart gently and say: Jesus is Lord and Messiah!
dailies.elijah: In Acts 2:23–24, what did wicked men do to Jesus, and what did God do?
dailies.elijahAnswer: They put him to death by nailing him to the cross, but God raised him from the dead, freeing him from the agony of death.
dailies.jordyn: Peter does not leave the crowd with wind and fire alone. He says, “God has made this Jesus, whom you crucified, both Lord and Messiah.” Why must Pentecost be about Jesus, not only about a powerful day?
dailies.jordynAnswer: The Spirit was poured out because Jesus is exalted (Acts 2:33). The meaning of the day is that this Jesus is Lord and Messiah. The gift points to him.
dailies.action: Read Acts 2:22–24 and 2:32–36, then tell someone: God has made Jesus both Lord and Messiah.
dailies.prayer: Father, thank you that you raised Jesus from the dead, and that he is both Lord and Messiah. Cut our hearts with this good news, and help us honor him. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
dailies.teach: Peter stood up and told the crowd about Jesus of Nazareth. He was handed over by God’s deliberate plan, and they put him to death by nailing him to the cross. But God raised him from the dead, and they were all witnesses of it. Exalted to the right hand of God, Jesus has received the promised Holy Spirit and has poured out what they now see and hear. “Therefore let all Israel be assured of this: God has made this Jesus, whom you crucified, both Lord and Messiah.”
dailies.enochActivity: Help a grown-up make a small cross with two fingers, then raise a hand and say: God raised Jesus, and he is Lord!
dailies.elijah2: In Acts 2:32, what does Peter say they all are?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: “God has raised this Jesus to life, and we are all witnesses of it.”
dailies.jordyn2: Acts 2:33 says Jesus has received the promised Holy Spirit and has poured out what they now see and hear. How does that connect last week’s wait with this week’s gift?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: The promise came from the Father through the risen Jesus. He went to heaven, and from there he poured out the Spirit. Pentecost is Jesus keeping his word.
dailies.passageText: 22 “Fellow Israelites, listen to this: Jesus of Nazareth was a man accredited by God to you by miracles, wonders and signs, which God did among you through him, as you yourselves know. 23 This man was handed over to you by God’s deliberate plan and foreknowledge; and you, with the help of wicked men, put him to death by nailing him to the cross. 24 But God raised him from the dead, freeing him from the agony of death, because it was impossible for death to keep its hold on him. 32 God has raised this Jesus to life, and we are all witnesses of it. 33 Exalted to the right hand of God, he has received from the Father the promised Holy Spirit and has poured out what you now see and hear. 36 “Therefore let all Israel be assured of this: God has made this Jesus, whom you crucified, both Lord and Messiah.”

dailies.label: Day 5 · Challenge
dailies.focus: The people are cut to the heart, and about three thousand are added that day.
dailies.verse: Those who accepted his message were baptized, and about three thousand were added to their number that day.
dailies.enoch: Hold up three fingers, then open your hands and say: The church family grew!
dailies.elijah: In Acts 2:37, what did the people ask when they were cut to the heart?
dailies.elijahAnswer: They said to Peter and the other apostles, “Brothers, what shall we do?”
dailies.jordyn: Peter says, “Repent and be baptized, every one of you, in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of your sins. And you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit.” What is one way that answer still invites you today, even if you were baptized long ago, or are still learning what it means?
dailies.jordynAnswer: The first word is repent: turn to Jesus as Lord and Messiah. Baptism and forgiveness belong to his name, and the Spirit is God’s gift. If you already belong to him, keep turning to him. If you are still learning, this is the way in. The church began with people who accepted this message.
dailies.action: Tell someone: About three thousand were added that day. Then ask the Lord to make you ready to turn to Jesus and to belong with his people.
dailies.prayer: Jesus, you are Lord and Messiah. Thank you for forgiveness and for the gift of the Holy Spirit. Help us repent, belong to you, and welcome others into your family. In your name, Amen.
dailies.teach: When the people heard that Jesus is Lord and Messiah, they were cut to the heart and asked, “Brothers, what shall we do?” Peter replied, “Repent and be baptized, every one of you, in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of your sins. And you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit.” The promise is for them, for their children, and for all who are far off. Those who accepted his message were baptized, and about three thousand were added to their number that day. The church began.
dailies.enochActivity: Help a grown-up welcome you with a smile or a hug and say: You can belong in God’s family.
dailies.elijah2: In Acts 2:38, what two things does Peter tell them to do, and what gift will they receive?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: Repent and be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of their sins, and they will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit.
dailies.jordyn2: The promise, Peter says, is “for you and your children and for all who are far off” (Acts 2:39). How does that make room for your family, and for people who feel far away?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: The gift is not locked to that one crowd in Jerusalem. God calls people near and far, parents and children. The church that began that day was already open wider than they could see.
dailies.passageText: 37 When the people heard this, they were cut to the heart and said to Peter and the other apostles, “Brothers, what shall we do?” 38 Peter replied, “Repent and be baptized, every one of you, in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of your sins. And you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit. 39 The promise is for you and your children and for all who are far off—for all whom the Lord our God will call.” 40 With many other words he warned them; and he pleaded with them, “Save yourselves from this corrupt generation.” 41 Those who accepted his message were baptized, and about three thousand were added to their number that day.

dailies.label: Day 6 · Prayer
dailies.focus: Jesus promised another advocate, and the Spirit makes them witnesses.
dailies.verse: But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit comes on you; and you will be my witnesses in Jerusalem, and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the ends of the earth.
dailies.enoch: Fold your hands and say: Jesus, thank you for sending the Helper.
dailies.elijah: In John 14:16, what did Jesus say he would ask the Father to give them?
dailies.elijahAnswer: Another advocate to help them and be with them forever.
dailies.jordyn: Jesus said, “I will not leave you as orphans; I will come to you” (John 14:18). How does that promise comfort you, now that he has gone back to heaven and the Spirit has come?
dailies.jordynAnswer: He is not absent in the way an orphan is left alone. The Father gave another advocate to be with them forever, and the Spirit has come. Jesus keeps his people, and he makes them witnesses.
dailies.action: Pray together: thank Jesus that he did not leave us as orphans, and ask the Spirit to help you be a witness this week.
dailies.prayer: Jesus, thank you that you asked the Father, and he gave another advocate to be with us forever. Thank you that you have not left us as orphans. Give us power to be your witnesses, here and to the ends of the earth. In your name, Amen.
dailies.teach: Jesus had said he would ask the Father, and the Father would give them another advocate to help them and be with them forever. He would not leave them as orphans. He also said they would receive power when the Holy Spirit came on them, and they would be his witnesses in Jerusalem, and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the ends of the earth. Pentecost is that promise kept. The Helper has come, and the witnesses begin.
dailies.enochActivity: Help a grown-up sit still for a short prayer and say: You did not leave us as orphans.
dailies.elijah2: In John 14:16–17, how long will the advocate be with them, and why can the world not accept him?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: He will be with them forever. “The world cannot accept him, because it neither sees him nor knows him. But you know him, for he lives with you and will be in you.”
dailies.jordyn2: Acts 1:8 names Jerusalem, Judea and Samaria, and the ends of the earth. How does Acts 2 already begin to keep that word?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: People from every nation under heaven were in Jerusalem and heard the wonders of God in their own languages. The witnesses start in Jerusalem, and the nations are already listening. The road will run farther still.
dailies.passageText: 16 And I will ask the Father, and he will give you another advocate to help you and be with you forever— 17 the Spirit of truth. The world cannot accept him, because it neither sees him nor knows him. But you know him, for he lives with you and will be in you. 18 I will not leave you as orphans; I will come to you. But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit comes on you; and you will be my witnesses in Jerusalem, and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the ends of the earth.”

dailies.label: Day 7 · Recap
dailies.focus: God sent the Holy Spirit, the church began, and next we will see Peter and John at the temple.
dailies.verse: Those who accepted his message were baptized, and about three thousand were added to their number that day.
dailies.enoch: Clap once and say: God sent his Holy Spirit, and the church began!
dailies.elijah: In Acts 2:4 and 2:41, what two beginnings do we see on the day of Pentecost?
dailies.elijahAnswer: They were filled with the Holy Spirit, and about three thousand were added to their number that day.
dailies.jordyn: This week the wait ended, the Spirit came, Peter preached Jesus, and thousands were added. How does that get your heart ready for next week, when Peter and John go to the temple?
dailies.jordynAnswer: The same Peter who once needed to wait is now filled with the Spirit. Next week he and John will be at the temple, bold to heal and bold to say that Jesus saves. The gift that began the church will make them brave to speak.
dailies.action: Tell someone the week’s big idea: God sent the Holy Spirit, and the church began. Then thank him that Jesus is Lord and Messiah.
dailies.prayer: Father, thank you that you sent the Holy Spirit and that the church began. Thank you that Jesus is Lord and Messiah, and that you added so many to their number that day. Get our hearts ready for next week, when Peter and John are bold at the temple. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
dailies.teach: This week we learned that God sent the Holy Spirit, and the church began. They were all together, and a sound like a violent wind filled the house. What seemed to be tongues of fire came to rest on each of them, and they were filled with the Holy Spirit. People from many nations heard the wonders of God in their own languages. Peter preached that God has made Jesus, whom they crucified, both Lord and Messiah. About three thousand were added that day. Jesus had promised another advocate, and he had said they would be his witnesses. Next week we will see Peter and John at the temple, bold to say that Jesus heals and saves.
dailies.enochActivity: Help a grown-up look toward the door and say: Next week Peter and John will go to the temple, and Jesus saves!
dailies.elijah2: In John 14:16 and Acts 1:8, what two promises of Jesus were kept at Pentecost?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: The Father gave another advocate to be with them, and they received power to be Jesus’ witnesses.
dailies.jordyn2: Why is it fitting to say the church began, if Jesus already had friends before Pentecost?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: His friends were already his people, but on this day the promised Spirit was poured out, the wonders of God were declared to the nations, and thousands were added. The church began in a new way, as Jesus had told them to wait and see.
dailies.passageText: All of them were filled with the Holy Spirit and began to speak in other tongues as the Spirit enabled them. “Therefore let all Israel be assured of this: God has made this Jesus, whom you crucified, both Lord and Messiah.” Those who accepted his message were baptized, and about three thousand were added to their number that day. But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit comes on you; and you will be my witnesses in Jerusalem, and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the ends of the earth.”

weeks.planTitle: Peter and John at the temple
weeks.title: Peter and John at the temple
weeks.selectLabel: Week 25 · Peter and John at the temple
weeks.nextUp: Week 26 · The church shares what they have
weeks.bigIdea: Jesus heals and saves, and Peter and John are bold to say so.
weeks.scheduleNote: This is the Week 25 family lesson. The short daily bites are Days 2–7.

howSteps.title: Read together
howSteps.detail: Open the Read tab and read Acts 3:1–10 out loud, then Acts 3:12–16, then Acts 4:8–12.

howSteps.title: Talk it through
howSteps.detail: Still on Read, walk through the kid-language explanation so everyone gets the picture.

howSteps.title: Age parts
howSteps.detail: Use Enoch, Elijah, and Jordyn tabs. Keep the Parent key open for yourself.

howSteps.title: Pray
howSteps.detail: Close with the short family prayer on the Prayer tab.

readings.text: 1 One day Peter and John were going up to the temple at the time of prayer—at three in the afternoon. 2 Now a man who was lame from birth was being carried to the temple gate called Beautiful, where he was put every day to beg from those going into the temple courts. 3 When he saw Peter and John about to enter, he asked them for money. 4 Peter looked straight at him, as did John. Then Peter said, “Look at us!” 5 So the man gave them his attention, expecting to get something from them. 6 Then Peter said, “Silver or gold I do not have, but what I do have I give you. In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, walk.” 7 Taking him by the right hand, he helped him up, and instantly the man’s feet and ankles became strong. 8 He jumped to his feet and began to walk. Then he went with them into the temple courts, walking and jumping, and praising God. 9 When all the people saw him walking and praising God, 10 they recognized him as the same man who used to sit begging at the temple gate called Beautiful, and they were filled with wonder and amazement at what had happened to him.

12 When Peter saw this, he said to them: “Fellow Israelites, why does this surprise you? Why do you stare at us as if by our own power or godliness we had made this man walk? 13 The God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, the God of our fathers, has glorified his servant Jesus. You handed him over to be killed, and you disowned him before Pilate, though he had decided to let him go. 14 You disowned the Holy and Righteous One and asked that a murderer be released to you. 15 You killed the author of life, but God raised him from the dead. We are witnesses of this. 16 By faith in the name of Jesus, this man whom you see and know was made strong. It is Jesus’ name and the faith that comes through him that has completely healed him, as you can all see.

8 Then Peter, filled with the Holy Spirit, said to them: “Rulers and elders of the people! 9 If we are being called to account today for an act of kindness shown to a man who was lame and are being asked how he was healed, 10 then know this, you and all the people of Israel: It is by the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, whom you crucified but whom God raised from the dead, that this man stands before you healed. 11 Jesus is “‘the stone you builders rejected, which has become the cornerstone.’ 12 Salvation is found in no one else, for there is no other name under heaven given to mankind by which we must be saved.”

story: Last week God sent the Holy Spirit, and the church began. About three thousand were added in one day. Peter, who had been told to wait, was now filled with the Spirit and bold to preach that Jesus is Lord and Messiah. This week we see that same boldness at the temple. Jesus heals and saves, and Peter and John are bold to say so.

One day Peter and John were going up to the temple at the time of prayer. A man who had been lame from birth was being carried to the temple gate called Beautiful, where he sat and begged. When he saw Peter and John, he asked them for money. Peter looked straight at him, with John. Then Peter said, “Silver or gold I do not have, but what I do have I give you. In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, walk.” He helped him up, and instantly the man’s feet and ankles became strong. He jumped to his feet and began to walk. Then he went with them into the temple courts, walking and jumping, and praising God. The people recognized him and were filled with wonder.

A crowd ran together. Peter would not let them think the power was his. He asked why they stared, as if by their own power or godliness they had made the man walk. The God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob had glorified Jesus. “By faith in the name of Jesus, this man whom you see and know was made strong. It is Jesus’ name and the faith that comes through him that has completely healed him, as you can all see.”

The leaders had Peter and John arrested, and the next day they asked, “By what power or what name did you do this?” Peter, filled with the Holy Spirit, told them it was by the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, whom they crucified and whom God raised from the dead. “Salvation is found in no one else, for there is no other name under heaven given to mankind by which we must be saved.” The leaders saw their courage and took note that these men had been with Jesus. They commanded them not to speak or teach at all in the name of Jesus. But Peter and John said they must listen to God, and “we cannot help speaking about what we have seen and heard.”
Jesus heals and saves, and his friends are bold to say so. Next week we will see how this same church shared what they had, so that no one was in need.
weeks.enochLine: Jesus heals and saves, and we can be bold to say so!
enochActivities: Activity: Jump and praise. Help a grown-up take two happy jumps and say: Praise God! Jesus heals and saves!
Activity: The name of Jesus. Cup your hands like a gift and say: In the name of Jesus!
elijahQuestions: In Acts 3:6, what did Peter say he did not have, and what did he give the man instead?
In Acts 3:8, what did the man do after his feet and ankles became strong?
In Acts 3:16, whose name, and what kind of faith, made the man strong?
In Acts 4:12, where is salvation found?
elijahAnswers: He did not have silver or gold, but he said, “what I do have I give you. In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, walk.” (Acts 3:6).
He jumped to his feet and began to walk, then went with them into the temple courts, walking and jumping, and praising God (Acts 3:8).
By faith in the name of Jesus. It is Jesus’ name and the faith that comes through him that completely healed him (Acts 3:16).
“Salvation is found in no one else, for there is no other name under heaven given to mankind by which we must be saved.” (Acts 4:12).
jordynQuestions: Peter will not let the crowd think that he and John healed the man by their own power or godliness (Acts 3:12–16). Why does that matter?
The leaders commanded them not to speak or teach at all in the name of Jesus (Acts 4:18). What do Peter and John say they must do instead?
Acts 4:13 says the leaders took note that these men had been with Jesus. How does that help you get ready for next week, when we will see this same church share what they have?
jordynAnswers: The man was made strong by faith in the name of Jesus, not by Peter and John’s power (Acts 3:16). If they took the credit, the crowd would miss the Savior. Jesus heals and saves, and they are bold to say so.
They ask which is right in God’s eyes: to listen to the leaders, or to him. “As for us, we cannot help speaking about what we have seen and heard.” (Acts 4:19–20).

They had been with Jesus, and now they belong to his people. The same church that is bold to speak his name will also share, so that no one is in need. Being with Jesus changes how they speak and how they live together.
weeks.jordynApplication: Jesus heals and saves, and there is no other name by which we must be saved (Acts 3:16; 4:12). This week, be bold to say the name of Jesus, and get ready to see how his church also shares. Next week we will see that no one was in need.
weeks.applicationCheck: Ask her later in the week whether she was bold to say the name of Jesus — in thanks, in a hard moment, or when someone needed help. If it is fitting, thank him together that Jesus heals and saves, and that his friends do not have to stay quiet about him.
weeks.prayer: Father, thank you that in the name of Jesus the lame man walked, and that salvation is found in no one else. Make us bold, like Peter and John, to say what we have seen and heard. Get our hearts ready to share as your church. In Jesus’ name, Amen.

dailies.label: Day 2 · Passage
dailies.focus: At the temple gate, Peter gives what he has: the name of Jesus.
dailies.verse: Silver or gold I do not have, but what I do have I give you. In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, walk.
dailies.enoch: Cup your hands and say: In the name of Jesus, God can help!
dailies.elijah: In Acts 3:1–2, where were Peter and John going, and who was being carried to the temple gate called Beautiful?
dailies.elijahAnswer: They were going up to the temple at the time of prayer, and a man lame from birth was being carried to the gate called Beautiful, where he sat begging.
dailies.jordyn: The man asked for money, but Peter gave him something else (Acts 3:6). What does that teach you about the name of Jesus?
dailies.jordynAnswer: Peter did not have silver or gold, but he had the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth. That name was not a slogan. The man was told to walk, and Jesus made him strong.
dailies.action: Read Acts 3:1–10 together, then tell someone: In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, the man walked.
dailies.prayer: Father, thank you for the name of Jesus. We may not have silver or gold to give, but we can point to him. Help us give what we do have, in his name. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
dailies.teach: Peter and John were going up to the temple at the time of prayer. A man lame from birth was begging at the gate called Beautiful. Peter looked at him and said, “Silver or gold I do not have, but what I do have I give you. In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, walk.” He helped him up, and instantly the man’s feet and ankles became strong. He jumped to his feet and began to walk, and he went into the temple courts, walking and jumping, and praising God.
dailies.enochActivity: Help a grown-up take your hand, like Peter helped the man, and say: Jesus makes people strong.
dailies.elijah2: In Acts 3:7–8, what happened when Peter helped him up?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: Instantly the man’s feet and ankles became strong. He jumped to his feet and began to walk, then went into the temple courts, walking and jumping, and praising God.
dailies.jordyn2: Why is it important that the man went into the temple courts walking, jumping, and praising God, and not just walking away quietly?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: The healing leads to praise. The people can see the same man who used to sit begging, now in the courts of God, and they are filled with wonder. The gift points to God.
dailies.passageText: 1 One day Peter and John were going up to the temple at the time of prayer—at three in the afternoon. 2 Now a man who was lame from birth was being carried to the temple gate called Beautiful, where he was put every day to beg from those going into the temple courts. 3 When he saw Peter and John about to enter, he asked them for money. 4 Peter looked straight at him, as did John. Then Peter said, “Look at us!” 5 So the man gave them his attention, expecting to get something from them. 6 Then Peter said, “Silver or gold I do not have, but what I do have I give you. In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, walk.” 7 Taking him by the right hand, he helped him up, and instantly the man’s feet and ankles became strong. 8 He jumped to his feet and began to walk. Then he went with them into the temple courts, walking and jumping, and praising God. 9 When all the people saw him walking and praising God, 10 they recognized him as the same man who used to sit begging at the temple gate called Beautiful, and they were filled with wonder and amazement at what had happened to him.

dailies.label: Day 3 · Game
dailies.focus: The healed man walks, jumps, and praises God, and the people are filled with wonder.
dailies.verse: He jumped to his feet and began to walk. Then he went with them into the temple courts, walking and jumping, and praising God.
dailies.enoch: Take two happy jumps and say: Praise God!
dailies.elijah: In Acts 3:9–10, what did the people recognize, and how did they feel?
dailies.elijahAnswer: They recognized him as the same man who used to sit begging at the temple gate called Beautiful, and they were filled with wonder and amazement at what had happened to him.
dailies.jordyn: The man had been lame from birth, and now he is walking and jumping and praising God. How should we join his joy without turning his story into a joke?
dailies.jordynAnswer: We praise God with him. We do not pretend his need was funny. We tell the truth: Jesus made him strong, and the right answer is wonder, amazement, and praise.
dailies.action: Play a praising walk: walk to another room, take a small jump, and say, Praise God! Jesus heals and saves.
dailies.prayer: Father, thank you that the man walked and jumped and praised you. Fill us with wonder, not with jokes, and teach us to praise you for what Jesus does. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
dailies.teach: The man jumped to his feet and began to walk. He went with Peter and John into the temple courts, walking and jumping, and praising God. When all the people saw him walking and praising God, they recognized him as the same man who used to sit begging at the temple gate called Beautiful, and they were filled with wonder and amazement at what had happened to him.
dailies.enochActivity: Help a grown-up walk with you a few steps and say: Walking and jumping and praising God!
dailies.elijah2: In Acts 3:8, where did the man go after he began to walk?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: He went with them into the temple courts, walking and jumping, and praising God.
dailies.jordyn2: Why does it matter that the people recognized him as the same man who used to sit begging?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: This was not a stranger they had never seen. The man they knew was now walking and praising God. The wonder is tied to a real person Jesus made strong.
dailies.passageText: 8 He jumped to his feet and began to walk. Then he went with them into the temple courts, walking and jumping, and praising God. 9 When all the people saw him walking and praising God, 10 they recognized him as the same man who used to sit begging at the temple gate called Beautiful, and they were filled with wonder and amazement at what had happened to him.

dailies.label: Day 4 · Passage
dailies.focus: Peter will not take the credit. The man was healed by faith in the name of Jesus.
dailies.verse: By faith in the name of Jesus, this man whom you see and know was made strong.
dailies.enoch: Point up and say: It was Jesus who made him strong!
dailies.elijah: In Acts 3:12, what does Peter ask the crowd, as if he and John had made the man walk?
dailies.elijahAnswer: He asks why they stare at them as if by their own power or godliness they had made this man walk.
dailies.jordyn: Peter says it is Jesus’ name and the faith that comes through him that has completely healed the man (Acts 3:16). How does that keep the story centered on Jesus, not on Peter and John?
dailies.jordynAnswer: The apostles are witnesses, not the source. If the crowd looks only at Peter and John, they will miss the name that heals and saves. Peter is bold to give Jesus the credit.
dailies.action: Read Acts 3:12–16, then tell someone: This man was made strong by faith in the name of Jesus.
dailies.prayer: Father, keep us from taking credit for what you have done. Thank you that Jesus’ name, and the faith that comes through him, made this man strong. Help us point to him. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
dailies.teach: While the man held on to Peter and John, the people came running, astonished. Peter would not let them think the power was theirs. Why do you stare at us, he asked, as if by our own power or godliness we had made this man walk? The God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob had glorified Jesus. By faith in the name of Jesus, this man whom they could see and know was made strong. It is Jesus’ name and the faith that comes through him that has completely healed him, as they could all see.
dailies.enochActivity: Help a grown-up shake your head no, then point up and say: Not our power. Jesus’ name!
dailies.elijah2: In Acts 3:13, whom does Peter say the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob has glorified?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: His servant Jesus.
dailies.jordyn2: The man is someone “you see and know” (Acts 3:16). Why is that a strong way for Peter to preach Jesus in the temple courts?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: The proof is standing there. They do not have to imagine a rumor. The man they know has been completely healed, and Peter names the reason: Jesus’ name and the faith that comes through him.
dailies.passageText: 12 When Peter saw this, he said to them: “Fellow Israelites, why does this surprise you? Why do you stare at us as if by our own power or godliness we had made this man walk? 13 The God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, the God of our fathers, has glorified his servant Jesus. You handed him over to be killed, and you disowned him before Pilate, though he had decided to let him go. 14 You disowned the Holy and Righteous One and asked that a murderer be released to you. 15 You killed the author of life, but God raised him from the dead. We are witnesses of this. 16 By faith in the name of Jesus, this man whom you see and know was made strong. It is Jesus’ name and the faith that comes through him that has completely healed him, as you can all see.

dailies.label: Day 5 · Challenge
dailies.focus: Filled with the Holy Spirit, Peter says salvation is found in no one else.
dailies.verse: Salvation is found in no one else, for there is no other name under heaven given to mankind by which we must be saved.
dailies.enoch: Say it clearly: Jesus saves! There is no other name.
dailies.elijah: In Acts 4:7, what did the leaders ask Peter and John?
dailies.elijahAnswer: “By what power or what name did you do this?”
dailies.jordyn: Peter, filled with the Holy Spirit, answers that the man stands healed by the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, whom they crucified and whom God raised from the dead (Acts 4:10, 12). Why is “no other name” both a hard word and a kind one?
dailies.jordynAnswer: It is hard because it will not share the saving name with anyone else. It is kind because God has given a name, and that name is enough. Salvation is found in Jesus, and they are bold to say so.
dailies.action: Tell someone today: Salvation is found in no one else. Then thank God that he has given the name of Jesus.
dailies.prayer: Father, thank you that salvation is found in no one else, and that you have given the name of Jesus. Fill us with your Spirit, and make us bold to say that he heals and saves. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
dailies.teach: The leaders asked, “By what power or what name did you do this?” Peter, filled with the Holy Spirit, told them it was by the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, whom they crucified but whom God raised from the dead, that this man stood before them healed. Jesus is the stone the builders rejected, which has become the cornerstone. Salvation is found in no one else, for there is no other name under heaven given to mankind by which we must be saved.
dailies.enochActivity: Help a grown-up hold one finger up and say: No other name. Jesus saves!
dailies.elijah2: In Acts 4:11, what does Peter say about the stone the builders rejected?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: Jesus is the stone the builders rejected, which has become the cornerstone.
dailies.jordyn2: Acts 4:8 says Peter was filled with the Holy Spirit when he answered. How does that connect this week to last week, when the Spirit first came?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: The same gift that began the church now makes Peter bold before rulers. The Spirit was not only for one loud day. He fills Jesus’ friends to speak the saving name.
dailies.passageText: 8 Then Peter, filled with the Holy Spirit, said to them: “Rulers and elders of the people! 9 If we are being called to account today for an act of kindness shown to a man who was lame and are being asked how he was healed, 10 then know this, you and all the people of Israel: It is by the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, whom you crucified but whom God raised from the dead, that this man stands before you healed. 11 Jesus is “‘the stone you builders rejected, which has become the cornerstone.’ 12 Salvation is found in no one else, for there is no other name under heaven given to mankind by which we must be saved.”

dailies.label: Day 6 · Prayer
dailies.focus: They cannot help speaking about what they have seen and heard, and they ask God for boldness.
dailies.verse: As for us, we cannot help speaking about what we have seen and heard.
dailies.enoch: Fold your hands and say: Lord, make us bold to speak about Jesus.
dailies.elijah: In Acts 4:18–19, what did the leaders command, and what question did Peter and John ask?
dailies.elijahAnswer: The leaders commanded them not to speak or teach at all in the name of Jesus. They asked, “Which is right in God’s eyes: to listen to you, or to him?”
dailies.jordyn: After they were released, they prayed, and they were all filled with the Holy Spirit and spoke the word of God boldly (Acts 4:31). What does that teach you about courage?
dailies.jordynAnswer: Courage is not something they have to invent alone. They tell their people what happened, they ask God to enable them to speak with great boldness, and the Spirit fills them again. We can ask for the same boldness.
dailies.action: Pray together: thank God for what you have seen and heard about Jesus, and ask him to help you speak with boldness.
dailies.prayer: Father, we cannot help speaking about what we have seen and heard. Enable your servants to speak your word with great boldness. Fill us with the Holy Spirit, and make us brave in the name of Jesus. In his name, Amen.
dailies.teach: The leaders commanded them not to speak or teach at all in the name of Jesus. Peter and John said they must listen to God, and they could not help speaking about what they had seen and heard. When they were released, they went back to their own people and prayed. They asked God to enable them to speak his word with great boldness. After they prayed, the place where they were meeting was shaken, and they were all filled with the Holy Spirit and spoke the word of God boldly.
dailies.enochActivity: Help a grown-up pray a short sentence with you: Lord, help us speak about Jesus with boldness.
dailies.elijah2: In Acts 4:13, what did the leaders notice about Peter and John?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: They saw their courage, realized they were unschooled, ordinary men, and took note that these men had been with Jesus.
dailies.jordyn2: They are ordinary men, and yet they are courageous. What is the difference, according to Acts 4:13 and 4:31?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: They had been with Jesus, and they were filled with the Holy Spirit. The boldness is not that they were impressive on their own. It is that they belong to Jesus and are filled by his Spirit.
dailies.passageText: 18 Then they called them in again and commanded them not to speak or teach at all in the name of Jesus. 19 But Peter and John replied, “Which is right in God’s eyes: to listen to you, or to him? You be the judges! 20 As for us, we cannot help speaking about what we have seen and heard.” 23 On their release, Peter and John went back to their own people and reported all that the chief priests and the elders had said to them. 24 When they heard this, they raised their voices together in prayer to God. “Sovereign Lord,” they said, “you made the heavens and the earth and the sea, and everything in them. 25 You spoke by the Holy Spirit through the mouth of your servant, our father David: “‘Why do the nations rage and the peoples plot in vain? 26 The kings of the earth rise up and the rulers band together against the Lord and against his anointed one.’ 27 Indeed Herod and Pontius Pilate met together with the Gentiles and the people of Israel in this city to conspire against your holy servant Jesus, whom you anointed. 28 They did what your power and will had decided beforehand should happen. 29 Now, Lord, consider their threats and enable your servants to speak your word with great boldness. 30 Stretch out your hand to heal and perform signs and wonders through the name of your holy servant Jesus.” 31 After they prayed, the place where they were meeting was shaken. And they were all filled with the Holy Spirit and spoke the word of God boldly.

dailies.label: Day 7 · Recap
dailies.focus: Jesus heals and saves, Peter and John are bold to say so, and next the church will share.
dailies.verse: Salvation is found in no one else, for there is no other name under heaven given to mankind by which we must be saved.
dailies.enoch: Jump once and say: Jesus heals and saves, and we can be bold to say so!
dailies.elijah: In Acts 3:6 and 4:12, what two things does the name of Jesus do in this week’s story?
dailies.elijahAnswer: In his name the lame man walks, and in his name alone we must be saved.
dailies.jordyn: This week Jesus healed a man at the temple, Peter gave Jesus the credit, and the friends were bold even when they were told to be quiet. How does that get your heart ready for next week, when the church shares so that no one is in need?
dailies.jordynAnswer: The same people who speak Jesus’ name also live as his family. Next week we will see them share what they have, so that no one is in need. Bold speech and generous love belong to the same church.
dailies.action: Tell someone the week’s big idea: Jesus heals and saves, and Peter and John are bold to say so. Then thank him that there is no other name.
dailies.prayer: Father, thank you that Jesus heals and saves, and that there is no other name by which we must be saved. Make us bold to speak what we have seen and heard, and get our hearts ready to share as your church. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
dailies.teach: This week we learned that Jesus heals and saves, and Peter and John are bold to say so. At the temple gate, Peter said he did not have silver or gold, but he gave what he had: the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth. The man walked, jumped, and praised God. Peter would not take the credit. The man was made strong by faith in the name of Jesus. Salvation is found in no one else. They could not help speaking about what they had seen and heard, and they prayed for boldness. Next week we will see this same church share what they have, so that no one was in need.
dailies.enochActivity: Help a grown-up open your hands as if sharing, and say: Next week the church will share, and Jesus still saves!
dailies.elijah2: In Acts 4:13 and 4:20, what two things mark Peter and John after the healing?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: The leaders took note that they had been with Jesus, and they said they could not help speaking about what they had seen and heard.
dailies.jordyn2: Why is “no other name” a fitting last word for a week that began with a man begging at a gate?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: The man needed more than silver or gold. He needed the name of Jesus to walk, and the world needs that same name to be saved. The story begins with a gift at the gate and ends with the only saving name.
dailies.passageText: 6 Then Peter said, “Silver or gold I do not have, but what I do have I give you. In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, walk.” 16 By faith in the name of Jesus, this man whom you see and know was made strong. It is Jesus’ name and the faith that comes through him that has completely healed him, as you can all see. 12 Salvation is found in no one else, for there is no other name under heaven given to mankind by which we must be saved.” 20 As for us, we cannot help speaking about what we have seen and heard.”

weeks.planTitle: The church shares what they have
weeks.title: The church shares what they have
weeks.selectLabel: Week 26 · The church shares what they have
weeks.nextUp: Week 27 · Stephen: faithful to Jesus
weeks.bigIdea: The first church prayed, learned, and shared so no one was in need.
weeks.scheduleNote: This is the Week 26 family lesson. The short daily bites are Days 2–7.

howSteps.title: Read together
howSteps.detail: Open the Read tab and read Acts 2:42–47 out loud, then Acts 4:32–35.

howSteps.title: Talk it through
howSteps.detail: Still on Read, walk through the kid-language explanation so everyone gets the picture.

howSteps.title: Age parts
howSteps.detail: Use Enoch, Elijah, and Jordyn tabs. Keep the Parent key open for yourself.

howSteps.title: Pray
howSteps.detail: Close with the short family prayer on the Prayer tab.

readings.text: 42 They devoted themselves to the apostles’ teaching and to fellowship, to the breaking of bread and to prayer. 43 Everyone was filled with awe at the many wonders and signs performed by the apostles. 44 All the believers were together and had everything in common. 45 They sold property and possessions to give to anyone who had need. 46 Every day they continued to meet together in the temple courts. They broke bread in their homes and ate together with glad and sincere hearts, 47 praising God and enjoying the favor of all the people. And the Lord added to their number daily those who were being saved.

32 All the believers were one in heart and mind. No one claimed that any of their possessions was their own, but they shared everything they had. 33 With great power the apostles continued to testify to the resurrection of the Lord Jesus. And God’s grace was so powerfully at work in them all 34 that there were no needy persons among them. For from time to time those who owned land or houses sold them, brought the money from the sales 35 and put it at the apostles’ feet, and it was distributed to anyone who had need.

story: Last week Peter and John were bold at the temple. Jesus healed a lame man, and they said that salvation is found in no one else. This week we see the same church, not only speaking the name of Jesus, but sharing what they have, so that no one was in need. The first church prayed, learned, and shared.

The believers devoted themselves to the apostles’ teaching and to fellowship, to the breaking of bread and to prayer. All the believers were together and had everything in common. They sold property and possessions to give to anyone who had need. Every day they continued to meet together in the temple courts. They broke bread in their homes and ate together with glad and sincere hearts, praising God and enjoying the favor of all the people. And the Lord added to their number daily those who were being saved.

Acts says it again a little later. All the believers were one in heart and mind. No one claimed that any of their possessions was their own, but they shared everything they had. With great power the apostles continued to testify to the resurrection of the Lord Jesus. And God’s grace was so powerfully at work in them all that there were no needy persons among them. From time to time those who owned land or houses sold them, brought the money from the sales, and put it at the apostles’ feet, and it was distributed to anyone who had need.

This is what Jesus’ people looked like when the Spirit had come and they were bold to say his name: they learned, they prayed, they ate together, and they shared, so that no one was left in need. Need is not a joke, and sharing is not showing off. It is grace at work in a family that belongs to Jesus.
Next week we will see that this same church also had people who stayed faithful to Jesus when it was hard. We will meet Stephen, who told the truth about Jesus, even when it cost him.
weeks.enochLine: God’s church learns, prays, and shares, so no one is left in need!
enochActivities: Activity: Open hands. Hold your hands out like you are sharing a gift and say: We can share!
Activity: Learn, pray, share. Touch your head, fold your hands, then open them, and say: We learn, we pray, we share!
elijahQuestions: In Acts 2:42, what four things did the believers devote themselves to?
In Acts 2:44–45, how did the believers treat what they had, and why?
In Acts 4:32, what does it mean that the believers were one in heart and mind?
In Acts 4:34–35, why were there no needy persons among them?
elijahAnswers: They devoted themselves to the apostles’ teaching and to fellowship, to the breaking of bread and to prayer (Acts 2:42).
All the believers were together and had everything in common. They sold property and possessions to give to anyone who had need (Acts 2:44–45).
No one claimed that any of their possessions was their own, but they shared everything they had (Acts 4:32). They were united, and their unity showed in how they treated their things.
From time to time those who owned land or houses sold them, brought the money, put it at the apostles’ feet, and it was distributed to anyone who had need (Acts 4:34–35).
jordynQuestions: Acts 2:42–47 shows a church that learns, prays, eats together, and shares. Why do all of those belong together, not just one of them?

Acts 4:33 says the apostles testified to the resurrection of the Lord Jesus with great power, and God’s grace was powerfully at work so that there were no needy persons among them. How does the resurrection news belong with their sharing?
This week the church shares so no one is in need. Next week we will meet Stephen, who was faithful to Jesus even when it cost him. How are generosity and faithfulness both ways of belonging to Jesus?
jordynAnswers: They are one family. Learning the apostles’ teaching, praying, breaking bread, and sharing with anyone who had need are all part of the same new life. If they only learned and never shared, or only shared and never prayed, they would be missing what this church actually did.

The apostles are telling the truth that Jesus is alive, and that same grace is at work in how they treat one another. The risen Lord is not only a message they speak. His grace makes a people who will not leave a brother or sister in need.

The same people who share what they have also tell the truth about Jesus. Next week we will see Stephen stay faithful when it is hard. Belonging to Jesus changes how we use our things and how we stand for his name.
weeks.jordynApplication: The first church prayed, learned, and shared so no one was in need (Acts 2:42–47; 4:32–35). This week, share something you actually have — time, a belonging, or help — and get your heart ready to stay faithful to Jesus, as we will see in Stephen next week.
weeks.applicationCheck: Ask her later in the week whether she shared something, or noticed a need and helped. If it is fitting, thank God together that his grace can make a people who learn, pray, and share, so no one is left in need.
weeks.prayer: Father, thank you that the first church devoted themselves to the apostles’ teaching, to fellowship, to the breaking of bread, and to prayer, and that they shared so no one was in need. Make us that kind of people. Teach us, hear our prayers, and open our hands. Get us ready to be faithful to Jesus. In his name, Amen.

dailies.label: Day 2 · Passage
dailies.focus: The first church devoted themselves to learning, fellowship, bread, and prayer.
dailies.verse: They devoted themselves to the apostles’ teaching and to fellowship, to the breaking of bread and to prayer.
dailies.enoch: Fold your hands and say: We can learn and pray together!
dailies.elijah: In Acts 2:42, what did the believers devote themselves to?
dailies.elijahAnswer: The apostles’ teaching and fellowship, the breaking of bread, and prayer.
dailies.jordyn: Why does Luke start this picture of the church with devotion, not with a list of things they bought or sold?
dailies.jordynAnswer: Sharing grows out of a life together with Jesus. They first gave themselves to the teaching, to one another, to the table, and to prayer. The generous church is a devoted church.
dailies.action: Read Acts 2:42–47 together, then tell someone the four things the church devoted themselves to.
dailies.prayer: Father, make us devoted like this first church: eager to learn, glad to be together, faithful to pray, and ready to share. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
dailies.teach: The new believers did not treat Jesus as a one-day story. They devoted themselves to the apostles’ teaching and to fellowship, to the breaking of bread and to prayer. They were together and had everything in common. They sold property and possessions to give to anyone who had need. Every day they met in the temple courts, broke bread in their homes, and ate together with glad and sincere hearts, praising God. And the Lord added to their number daily those who were being saved.
dailies.enochActivity: Help a grown-up touch your head, then fold your hands, and say: We learn, and we pray!
dailies.elijah2: In Acts 2:46, where did they meet, and how did they eat together?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: They continued to meet together in the temple courts. They broke bread in their homes and ate together with glad and sincere hearts.
dailies.jordyn2: The Lord added to their number daily those who were being saved (Acts 2:47). How does that belong with a glad, sharing church?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: People could see a family that praised God and took care of one another. The Lord was saving people, and he was adding them to a church that already knew how to learn, pray, eat, and share.
dailies.passageText: 42 They devoted themselves to the apostles’ teaching and to fellowship, to the breaking of bread and to prayer. 43 Everyone was filled with awe at the many wonders and signs performed by the apostles. 44 All the believers were together and had everything in common. 45 They sold property and possessions to give to anyone who had need. 46 Every day they continued to meet together in the temple courts. They broke bread in their homes and ate together with glad and sincere hearts, 47 praising God and enjoying the favor of all the people. And the Lord added to their number daily those who were being saved.

dailies.label: Day 3 · Game
dailies.focus: They had everything in common, and they gave to anyone who had need.
dailies.verse: All the believers were together and had everything in common.
dailies.enoch: Hold out a toy or a snack and say: I can share!
dailies.elijah: In Acts 2:45, what did they sell, and what did they do with it?
dailies.elijahAnswer: They sold property and possessions to give to anyone who had need.
dailies.jordyn: How should we play a sharing game so that need is treated with dignity, not as a joke?
dailies.jordynAnswer: We do not pretend someone’s need is funny. We practice open hands. The first church gave so that anyone who had need received help, and the right feeling is gladness, not showing off or making fun.
dailies.action: Play a share-around: each person puts one small item in a basket, then you give those items out so no one is left with nothing. Then thank God that his church can share.
dailies.prayer: Father, thank you that the first church had everything in common and gave to anyone who had need. Teach us to share with glad hearts, and to treat every person with dignity. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
dailies.teach: All the believers were together and had everything in common. They sold property and possessions to give to anyone who had need. This was not a game to them, and it is not a joke to us. Jesus’ people used what they had so that a real person in need would be helped.
dailies.enochActivity: Help a grown-up pass a small item from your hands to theirs, then back again, and say: We can share what we have!
dailies.elijah2: In Acts 2:44, were the believers alone with their own things, or together?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: They were together and had everything in common.
dailies.jordyn2: Why does “anyone who had need” matter in Acts 2:45?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: The gift was aimed at a real need, not at impressing the room. The church watched for people who lacked something, and they gave so that those people were not left out.
dailies.passageText: 44 All the believers were together and had everything in common. 45 They sold property and possessions to give to anyone who had need.

dailies.label: Day 4 · Passage
dailies.focus: The believers were one in heart and mind, and there were no needy persons among them.
dailies.verse: All the believers were one in heart and mind. No one claimed that any of their possessions was their own, but they shared everything they had.
dailies.enoch: Put a hand on your heart and say: One in heart, and we can share!
dailies.elijah: In Acts 4:32, what did no one claim about their possessions?
dailies.elijahAnswer: No one claimed that any of their possessions was their own, but they shared everything they had.
dailies.jordyn: Acts 4:33–34 holds two things together: the apostles testify to the resurrection with great power, and God’s grace is so powerfully at work that there were no needy persons among them. What do you notice?
dailies.jordynAnswer: The risen Jesus is the center, and his grace does not stay in words only. The same church that preaches the resurrection also makes sure no one among them is left in need.
dailies.action: Read Acts 4:32–35, then tell someone: There were no needy persons among them, because they shared.
dailies.prayer: Father, make us one in heart and mind. Let your grace work in us so powerfully that we notice need and share what we have. We believe that Jesus is risen. In his name, Amen.
dailies.teach: All the believers were one in heart and mind. No one claimed that any of their possessions was their own, but they shared everything they had. With great power the apostles continued to testify to the resurrection of the Lord Jesus. And God’s grace was so powerfully at work in them all that there were no needy persons among them. From time to time those who owned land or houses sold them, brought the money, put it at the apostles’ feet, and it was distributed to anyone who had need.
dailies.enochActivity: Help a grown-up open both of your hands and say: God’s grace helps us share.
dailies.elijah2: In Acts 4:33, what did the apostles testify to with great power?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: The resurrection of the Lord Jesus.
dailies.jordyn2: The money was put at the apostles’ feet and then distributed to anyone who had need (Acts 4:35). Why is that a careful, not careless, kind of sharing?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: They did not throw gifts around to be seen. The gift was brought to the apostles and then given to real people who had need. Sharing was ordered, honest, and aimed at helping.
dailies.passageText: 32 All the believers were one in heart and mind. No one claimed that any of their possessions was their own, but they shared everything they had. 33 With great power the apostles continued to testify to the resurrection of the Lord Jesus. And God’s grace was so powerfully at work in them all 34 that there were no needy persons among them. For from time to time those who owned land or houses sold them, brought the money from the sales 35 and put it at the apostles’ feet, and it was distributed to anyone who had need.

dailies.label: Day 5 · Challenge
dailies.focus: Share something you have this week, the way the first church gave to anyone who had need.
dailies.verse: They sold property and possessions to give to anyone who had need.
dailies.enoch: Look around, point to one thing you can share, and say: I can share this!
dailies.elijah: In Acts 4:34, what does Luke say about needy persons among them?
dailies.elijahAnswer: There were no needy persons among them.
dailies.jordyn: You may not have land or a house to sell. What would it look like for you to share something you actually have, so that someone else’s need is met?
dailies.jordynAnswer: Share a belonging, a skill, your time, or a kind help. The first church used what they had, not what they wished they had. The challenge is not to pretend to be rich. It is to open your hands.
dailies.action: Choose one real thing to share today or tomorrow — a toy, a snack, help with a chore, or time with someone who is left out — and then do it.
dailies.prayer: Father, you have given us more than we need to keep for ourselves. Show us one person who has a need, and help us share with a glad heart. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
dailies.teach: The first church sold property and possessions to give to anyone who had need. Later Luke says there were no needy persons among them, because people brought what they had and it was distributed to anyone who had need. The challenge for us is the same kind of open hands, at the size of our life.
dailies.enochActivity: Help a grown-up choose one thing you can share this week, and say: This can help someone.
dailies.elijah2: In Acts 4:35, what happened after the money was put at the apostles’ feet?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: It was distributed to anyone who had need.
dailies.jordyn2: Why is “anyone who had need” a better goal than everyone getting the same thing?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: The church was watching for need, not running a contest. Some people needed help, and the gifts were given there. Sharing means paying attention to people, not only dividing a pile.
dailies.passageText: 45 They sold property and possessions to give to anyone who had need. 34 that there were no needy persons among them. For from time to time those who owned land or houses sold them, brought the money from the sales 35 and put it at the apostles’ feet, and it was distributed to anyone who had need.

dailies.label: Day 6 · Prayer
dailies.focus: Ask God to make you a people who learn, pray, and share, because his grace is at work.
dailies.verse: And God’s grace was so powerfully at work in them all
dailies.enoch: Fold your hands and say: Lord, teach us to share with glad hearts.
dailies.elijah: In Acts 2:42 and 4:33, what two things do we see God giving this church — a way to live, and a power to speak?
dailies.elijahAnswer: They devoted themselves to the teaching, fellowship, bread, and prayer, and the apostles testified to the resurrection of the Lord Jesus with great power, with God’s grace at work in them all.
dailies.jordyn: Why is prayer the right way to become a sharing church, not only a plan to try harder?
dailies.jordynAnswer: Luke says God’s grace was powerfully at work in them. The generosity was not a trick they invented. We ask the Lord to work that same grace in us, and then we open our hands.
dailies.action: Pray together: thank God for what you have, ask him to show you a need, and ask for a glad heart to share.
dailies.prayer: Father, thank you that your grace was powerfully at work in the first church. Make us devoted to Jesus, one in heart and mind, and ready to share so no one among us is left in need. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
dailies.teach: They devoted themselves to the apostles’ teaching and to fellowship, to the breaking of bread and to prayer. They were one in heart and mind, and they shared everything they had. With great power the apostles testified to the resurrection of the Lord Jesus, and God’s grace was so powerfully at work in them all. That is why we pray: we want that same grace to work in us.
dailies.enochActivity: Help a grown-up pray a short sentence with you: Lord, work your grace in us, and teach us to share.
dailies.elijah2: In Acts 4:32, what two things were true of the believers at the same time?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: They were one in heart and mind, and they shared everything they had.
dailies.jordyn2: God’s grace was at work “in them all” (Acts 4:33). What does that say about who gets to take part in a sharing church?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: It was not only the apostles, and not only the people who sold land. Grace was at work in them all. Every believer belongs in a church that learns, prays, and shares.
dailies.passageText: 42 They devoted themselves to the apostles’ teaching and to fellowship, to the breaking of bread and to prayer. 32 All the believers were one in heart and mind. No one claimed that any of their possessions was their own, but they shared everything they had. 33 With great power the apostles continued to testify to the resurrection of the Lord Jesus. And God’s grace was so powerfully at work in them all

dailies.label: Day 7 · Recap
dailies.focus: The first church prayed, learned, and shared so no one was in need, and next we will see Stephen stay faithful.
dailies.verse: They devoted themselves to the apostles’ teaching and to fellowship, to the breaking of bread and to prayer.
dailies.enoch: Open your hands and say: The church shares, and Jesus is faithful!
dailies.elijah: In Acts 2:42 and 4:34, what kind of church was this?
dailies.elijahAnswer: A church devoted to teaching, fellowship, bread, and prayer, and a church in which there were no needy persons among them.
dailies.jordyn: This week we saw a church that learned, prayed, ate together, and shared. How does that get your heart ready for next week, when we will meet Stephen, who was faithful to Jesus even when it cost him?
dailies.jordynAnswer: The same family that opens its hands also stands for Jesus’ name. Next week we will see Stephen tell the truth about Jesus and stay faithful. Sharing and faithfulness both belong to the people Jesus has made.
dailies.action: Tell someone the week’s big idea: The first church prayed, learned, and shared so no one was in need. Then thank God, and look ahead to Stephen.
dailies.prayer: Father, thank you that the first church prayed, learned, and shared so no one was in need. Make us that kind of people, and get our hearts ready to be faithful to Jesus, like Stephen. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
dailies.teach: This week we learned that the first church prayed, learned, and shared so no one was in need. They devoted themselves to the apostles’ teaching and to fellowship, to the breaking of bread and to prayer. They were together and had everything in common. They were one in heart and mind, and they shared everything they had. God’s grace was so powerfully at work that there were no needy persons among them. Next week we will meet Stephen, who was faithful to Jesus even when it cost him.
dailies.enochActivity: Help a grown-up stand tall, then open your hands, and say: Next week we will see Stephen stay faithful to Jesus!
dailies.elijah2: In Acts 4:32–34, what two marks sit side by side in this church?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: They were one in heart and mind, sharing everything they had, and there were no needy persons among them, while the apostles testified to the resurrection with great power.
dailies.jordyn2: Why is so no one was in need a fitting last word before a week about Stephen’s faithfulness?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: Jesus’ people belong to him in their things and in their courage. This week we saw their open hands. Next week we will see a man who will not let go of Jesus’ name, even when it costs him. Both are the life of the same church.
