readings.text: 1 At Caesarea there was a man named Cornelius, a centurion in what was known as the Italian Regiment. 2 He and all his family were devout and God-fearing; he gave generously to those in need and prayed to God regularly. 3 One day at about three in the afternoon he had a vision. He distinctly saw an angel of God, who came to him and said, “Cornelius!” 4 Cornelius stared at him in fear. “What is it, Lord?” he asked. The angel answered, “Your prayers and gifts to the poor have come up as a memorial offering before God. 5 Now send men to Joppa to bring back a man named Simon who is called Peter. 6 He is staying with Simon the tanner, whose house is by the sea.” 7 When the angel who spoke to him had gone, Cornelius called two of his servants and a devout soldier who was one of his attendants. 8 He told them everything that had happened and sent them to Joppa.

34 Then Peter began to speak: “I now realize how true it is that God does not show favoritism 35 but accepts from every nation the one who fears him and does what is right. 36 You know the message God sent to the people of Israel, announcing the good news of peace through Jesus Christ, who is Lord of all. 37 You know what has happened throughout the province of Judea, beginning in Galilee after the baptism that John preached— 38 how God anointed Jesus of Nazareth with the Holy Spirit and power, and how he went around doing good and healing all who were under the power of the devil, because God was with him. 39 “We are witnesses of everything he did in the country of the Jews and in Jerusalem. They killed him by hanging him on a cross, 40 but God raised him from the dead on the third day and caused him to be seen. 41 He was not seen by all the people, but by witnesses whom God had already chosen—by us who ate and drank with him after he rose from the dead. 42 He commanded us to preach to the people and to testify that he is the one whom God appointed as judge of the living and the dead. 43 All the prophets testify about him that everyone who believes in him receives forgiveness of sins through his name.”

44 While Peter was still speaking these words, the Holy Spirit came on all who heard the message. 45 The circumcised believers who had come with Peter were astonished that the gift of the Holy Spirit had been poured out even on Gentiles. 46 For they heard them speaking in tongues and praising God. Then Peter said, 47 “Surely no one can stand in the way of their being baptized with water. They have received the Holy Spirit just as we have.” 48 So he ordered that they be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ. Then they asked Peter to stay with them for a few days.

story: Last week Jesus met Saul on the road, and we learned that Jesus can change anyone, even someone who fought against him. Today the good news keeps going farther. In Caesarea there was a man named Cornelius, a centurion in what was known as the Italian Regiment. He and all his family were devout and God-fearing. He gave generously to those in need and prayed to God regularly.

One day at about three in the afternoon he had a vision. He distinctly saw an angel of God, who came to him and said, “Cornelius!” Cornelius stared at him in fear. “What is it, Lord?” he asked. The angel answered, “Your prayers and gifts to the poor have come up as a memorial offering before God. Now send men to Joppa to bring back a man named Simon who is called Peter. He is staying with Simon the tanner, whose house is by the sea.” Cornelius told them everything that had happened and sent them to Joppa.

God was also preparing Peter. When Peter arrived, he began to speak. He now realized how true it is that God does not show favoritism, but accepts from every nation the one who fears him and does what is right. Peter told them the good news of peace through Jesus Christ, who is Lord of all. Jesus went around doing good. They killed him by hanging him on a cross, but God raised him from the dead on the third day. All the prophets testify about him that everyone who believes in him receives forgiveness of sins through his name.

While Peter was still speaking these words, the Holy Spirit came on all who heard the message. The believers who had come with Peter were astonished that the gift of the Holy Spirit had been poured out even on Gentiles. Then Peter said, “Surely no one can stand in the way of their being baptized with water. They have received the Holy Spirit just as we have.” So he ordered that they be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ. Then they asked Peter to stay with them for a few days.
The good news of Jesus is for every nation and people. Next week we will see the church praying, and God setting Peter free. Peter will be in prison, and the church will pray.
weeks.enochLine: The good news of Jesus is for every nation and people!
enochActivities: Activity: Open arms. Open your arms wide and say: The good news is for everyone!
Activity: Welcome. Hold out a welcome hand and say: God shows no favoritism!
elijahQuestions: In Acts 10:1–2, who was Cornelius, and how did he and his family live before God?
In Acts 10:3–8, what did the angel tell Cornelius to do?
In Acts 10:34–35, what did Peter say he now realized about God?
In Acts 10:44–48, what happened while Peter was still speaking, and what did Peter order?
elijahAnswers: Cornelius was a centurion in the Italian Regiment. He and all his family were devout and God-fearing. He gave generously to those in need and prayed to God regularly (Acts 10:1–2).

The angel told him to send men to Joppa to bring back a man named Simon who is called Peter, who was staying with Simon the tanner by the sea. Cornelius told them everything and sent them (Acts 10:5–8).
Peter said he now realized how true it is that God does not show favoritism, but accepts from every nation the one who fears him and does what is right (Acts 10:34–35).

The Holy Spirit came on all who heard the message. The believers with Peter were astonished that the gift had been poured out even on Gentiles. Peter ordered that they be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ (Acts 10:44–48).
jordynQuestions: Cornelius already prayed and gave generously (Acts 10:2–4). Why did he still need Peter to come and speak about Jesus?

Peter says God does not show favoritism, and that everyone who believes in Jesus receives forgiveness of sins through his name (Acts 10:34–35, 43). What does that tell you about who the good news is for?
This week the Spirit is poured out even on Gentiles (Acts 10:44–45). Next week the church will pray, and God will set Peter free. What do both stories show you about how God keeps his work moving?
jordynAnswers: Praying and giving are real, and they are not yet the good news itself. Cornelius needed to hear about Jesus, who is Lord of all, who was raised, and through whose name everyone who believes receives forgiveness. God sent Peter to tell him that.

The good news is not for one nation, one family, or one kind of person. God accepts from every nation the one who fears him, and forgiveness is promised to everyone who believes in Jesus. No one is left out of that welcome by birth.

God is not stuck with one people, and he is not stuck when trouble comes. This week he pours out the Spirit on people Peter had not expected. Next week we will see the church pray, and God set Peter free, so the good news can keep going.
weeks.jordynApplication: The good news of Jesus is for every nation and people (Acts 10:1–8, 34–48). This week, welcome someone you might have quietly left out, or tell someone that forgiveness through Jesus is for everyone who believes. Next week we will see the church praying, and God setting Peter free.
weeks.applicationCheck: Ask her later in the week whether she welcomed someone with care, or told someone that the good news is for every nation. If it is fitting, thank God together that he shows no favoritism, and that the Spirit was poured out even on the people Peter had not expected.
weeks.prayer: Father, thank you that you heard Cornelius, and that you sent Peter to tell the good news of Jesus, who is Lord of all. Thank you that you do not show favoritism, and that everyone who believes in him receives forgiveness of sins through his name. Make us ready to welcome people from every nation, and to share this good news with joy. In Jesus’ name, Amen.

dailies.label: Day 2 · Passage
dailies.focus: God hears Cornelius and sends him to find Peter, so he can hear the good news.
dailies.verse: Your prayers and gifts to the poor have come up as a memorial offering before God.
dailies.enoch: Fold your hands, then hold them out, and say: God hears us, and he sends help!
dailies.elijah: In Acts 10:1–4, what kind of man was Cornelius, and what did the angel say about his prayers and gifts?
dailies.elijahAnswer: He was a devout, God-fearing centurion who gave generously and prayed regularly. The angel said his prayers and gifts to the poor had come up as a memorial offering before God.
dailies.jordyn: Cornelius already prayed and gave (Acts 10:2–4), and God still sent him to find Peter. What does that tell you about what God was preparing to give him?
dailies.jordynAnswer: God had already seen his prayers and gifts, and he was not finished. Cornelius still needed to hear the good news about Jesus. God was opening a door, not leaving him with only the life he already had.
dailies.action: Read Acts 10:1–8 together, then tell someone: God told Cornelius to send for a man named Peter.
dailies.prayer: Father, thank you that you heard Cornelius and sent him to Peter. Thank you that you still hear prayer, and that you send the good news. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
dailies.teach: Cornelius was a centurion in Caesarea, devout and God-fearing. He gave generously and prayed regularly. An angel called him by name and told him that his prayers and gifts had come up before God. He was to send men to Joppa for Simon who is called Peter. Cornelius told them everything and sent them.
dailies.enochActivity: Help a grown-up say Cornelius, then fold your hands and say: God heard him!
dailies.elijah2: In Acts 10:5–8, where was Peter staying, and what did Cornelius do?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: Peter was staying with Simon the tanner, whose house is by the sea. Cornelius told his men everything that had happened and sent them to Joppa.
dailies.jordyn2: Why is it important that this first reading ends with men on the road, before Peter even speaks?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: God is already at work on both sides. Cornelius obeys and sends. The good news will travel because someone was willing to go and get the messenger. Tomorrow and later this week we will hear what Peter says when he arrives.
dailies.passageText: 1 At Caesarea there was a man named Cornelius, a centurion in what was known as the Italian Regiment. 2 He and all his family were devout and God-fearing; he gave generously to those in need and prayed to God regularly. 3 One day at about three in the afternoon he had a vision. He distinctly saw an angel of God, who came to him and said, “Cornelius!” 4 Cornelius stared at him in fear. “What is it, Lord?” he asked. The angel answered, “Your prayers and gifts to the poor have come up as a memorial offering before God. 5 Now send men to Joppa to bring back a man named Simon who is called Peter. 6 He is staying with Simon the tanner, whose house is by the sea.” 7 When the angel who spoke to him had gone, Cornelius called two of his servants and a devout soldier who was one of his attendants. 8 He told them everything that had happened and sent them to Joppa.

dailies.label: Day 3 · Game
dailies.focus: Practice a wide welcome, because the good news of Jesus is for every nation and people.
dailies.verse: God does not show favoritism.
dailies.enoch: Open your arms wide and say: The good news is for everyone!
dailies.elijah: In Acts 10:34–35, what did Peter say God does not do, and whom does God accept?
dailies.elijahAnswer: God does not show favoritism, but accepts from every nation the one who fears him and does what is right.
dailies.jordyn: How should we play a wide-welcome game so that we honor every nation and people, and do not make anyone’s country, language, or family a joke?
dailies.jordynAnswer: We practice a real welcome, not a sketch that copies accents or pokes fun. We say the good news is for every nation, and we treat each person as someone God can welcome.
dailies.action: Play a wide-welcome game: stand in a small circle, take turns opening your arms toward someone, and say, The good news of Jesus is for you too. Then switch until everyone has been welcomed.
dailies.prayer: Father, thank you that you do not show favoritism. Teach us to welcome people from every nation with honor and joy. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
dailies.teach: When Peter arrived, he said he now realized that God does not show favoritism, but accepts from every nation the one who fears him and does what is right. Today we practice that kind of welcome: wide, glad, and respectful, because the good news of Jesus is for every nation and people.
dailies.enochActivity: Help a grown-up open their arms with you, and say: Jesus is for every nation!
dailies.elijah2: In Acts 10:35, whom does God accept?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: He accepts from every nation the one who fears him and does what is right.
dailies.jordyn2: Why is every nation a better line to practice than trying to act out armies or angels?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: The heart of the story is the welcome of God, not a show. Cornelius was a real officer, and Peter was a real apostle, and the good news crossed a line they had not expected. We honor that by practicing welcome, not by making a play of it.
dailies.passageText: 34 Then Peter began to speak: “I now realize how true it is that God does not show favoritism 35 but accepts from every nation the one who fears him and does what is right.

dailies.label: Day 4 · Passage
dailies.focus: Peter tells the good news of Jesus, and the Holy Spirit is poured out even on the Gentiles.
dailies.verse: Everyone who believes in him receives forgiveness of sins through his name.
dailies.enoch: Point up, then open your arms, and say: Jesus is Lord of all!
dailies.elijah: In Acts 10:36–43, what good news did Peter tell them about Jesus?
dailies.elijahAnswer: God sent the good news of peace through Jesus Christ, who is Lord of all. They killed him on a cross, but God raised him from the dead on the third day. Everyone who believes in him receives forgiveness of sins through his name.
dailies.jordyn: While Peter was still speaking, the Holy Spirit came on all who heard, even on Gentiles (Acts 10:44–45). What does that show you about God’s timing and God’s welcome?
dailies.jordynAnswer: God did not wait for the listeners to become like Peter’s group first. The Spirit was poured out while they were hearing the good news about Jesus. The welcome is God’s work, and it is wider than the believers with Peter had expected.
dailies.action: Read Acts 10:34–48 together, then tell someone: The Holy Spirit was poured out even on the Gentiles, and they were baptized.
dailies.prayer: Father, thank you that Jesus is Lord of all, and that everyone who believes in him receives forgiveness through his name. Thank you that you poured out your Spirit even on people some had not expected. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
dailies.teach: Peter said God does not show favoritism. He told them the good news of peace through Jesus Christ, who is Lord of all. They killed Jesus on a cross, but God raised him on the third day. Everyone who believes in him receives forgiveness of sins through his name. While Peter was still speaking, the Holy Spirit came on all who heard the message. Peter said no one could stand in the way of their being baptized, and they were baptized in the name of Jesus Christ.
dailies.enochActivity: Help a grown-up sprinkle a drop of water on a fingertip, then say: They were baptized in Jesus’ name!
dailies.elijah2: In Acts 10:47–48, what did Peter say, and what did he order?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: He said, “Surely no one can stand in the way of their being baptized with water. They have received the Holy Spirit just as we have.” Then he ordered that they be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ.
dailies.jordyn2: The believers with Peter were astonished (Acts 10:45). Why might astonishment be a fitting response, and not a reason to shut the door?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: They were seeing God do something larger than their old categories. Astonishment can turn into praise and baptism, or it can turn into a wall. Peter lets it turn into a welcome: no one can stand in the way.
dailies.passageText: 34 Then Peter began to speak: “I now realize how true it is that God does not show favoritism 35 but accepts from every nation the one who fears him and does what is right. 36 You know the message God sent to the people of Israel, announcing the good news of peace through Jesus Christ, who is Lord of all. 37 You know what has happened throughout the province of Judea, beginning in Galilee after the baptism that John preached— 38 how God anointed Jesus of Nazareth with the Holy Spirit and power, and how he went around doing good and healing all who were under the power of the devil, because God was with him. 39 “We are witnesses of everything he did in the country of the Jews and in Jerusalem. They killed him by hanging him on a cross, 40 but God raised him from the dead on the third day and caused him to be seen. 41 He was not seen by all the people, but by witnesses whom God had already chosen—by us who ate and drank with him after he rose from the dead. 42 He commanded us to preach to the people and to testify that he is the one whom God appointed as judge of the living and the dead. 43 All the prophets testify about him that everyone who believes in him receives forgiveness of sins through his name.” 44 While Peter was still speaking these words, the Holy Spirit came on all who heard the message. 45 The circumcised believers who had come with Peter were astonished that the gift of the Holy Spirit had been poured out even on Gentiles. 46 For they heard them speaking in tongues and praising God. Then Peter said, 47 “Surely no one can stand in the way of their being baptized with water. They have received the Holy Spirit just as we have.” 48 So he ordered that they be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ. Then they asked Peter to stay with them for a few days.

dailies.label: Day 5 · Challenge
dailies.focus: Welcome someone this week, or tell them that the good news of Jesus is for every nation and people.
dailies.verse: Surely no one can stand in the way of their being baptized with water.
dailies.enoch: Hold out a welcome hand and say: The good news is for you too!
dailies.elijah: In Acts 10:45–48, who was astonished, and what happened next?
dailies.elijahAnswer: The circumcised believers who had come with Peter were astonished that the gift of the Holy Spirit had been poured out even on Gentiles. Then Peter ordered that they be baptized, and they asked him to stay.
dailies.jordyn: Peter would not stand in the way (Acts 10:47). What would a right-sized challenge look like for you this week, so that you are not standing in the way of someone’s welcome?
dailies.jordynAnswer: You might welcome a person you usually pass by, sit with someone new, or tell a friend that Jesus is Lord of all and that forgiveness is for everyone who believes. The challenge is not to be Peter in Caesarea. It is to stop leaving someone out.
dailies.action: Choose one person this week to welcome with care, or to tell that the good news of Jesus is for every nation and people — then do it.
dailies.prayer: Father, you poured out your Spirit even on people some had not expected. Make us people who do not stand in the way, but who welcome and tell the good news. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
dailies.teach: The Holy Spirit came on all who heard the message, even on Gentiles. Peter said no one could stand in the way of their being baptized. They were baptized in the name of Jesus Christ, and they asked Peter to stay. The good news had crossed a line, and the church’s part was to welcome, not to block the way.
dailies.enochActivity: Help a grown-up name one person you can welcome or tell this week, and practice the words: The good news is for you too.
dailies.elijah2: In Acts 10:48, in whose name were they baptized?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: They were baptized in the name of Jesus Christ.
dailies.jordyn2: They also asked Peter to stay with them for a few days (Acts 10:48). Why is staying part of a real welcome, not only a moment of surprise?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: The good news made a new household of people who wanted to keep listening. Welcome is not only a sentence at the door. It can look like time, a table, and staying long enough to keep teaching about Jesus.
dailies.passageText: 44 While Peter was still speaking these words, the Holy Spirit came on all who heard the message. 45 The circumcised believers who had come with Peter were astonished that the gift of the Holy Spirit had been poured out even on Gentiles. 46 For they heard them speaking in tongues and praising God. Then Peter said, 47 “Surely no one can stand in the way of their being baptized with water. They have received the Holy Spirit just as we have.” 48 So he ordered that they be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ. Then they asked Peter to stay with them for a few days.

dailies.label: Day 6 · Prayer
dailies.focus: Thank God that the good news is for every nation, and ask for a wide, willing welcome.
dailies.verse: The gift of the Holy Spirit had been poured out even on Gentiles.
dailies.enoch: Open your arms and say: Thank you, God, that Jesus is for everyone!
dailies.elijah: In Acts 10:34–35 and 10:45, what did Peter realize, and what astonished the believers with him?
dailies.elijahAnswer: Peter realized that God does not show favoritism, but accepts from every nation the one who fears him. The believers were astonished that the Holy Spirit had been poured out even on Gentiles.
dailies.jordyn: Cornelius prayed regularly, and then a whole household heard the good news and received the Spirit (Acts 10:2, 44–48). What would it look like to pray this story, not only to retell it?
dailies.jordynAnswer: Thank God that he hears, that he shows no favoritism, and that forgiveness is through Jesus’ name for everyone who believes. Then ask him to give you a wide welcome, and to send the good news to people you have not expected.
dailies.action: Pray together: thank God that the good news is for every nation and people, and ask him to help you welcome others the way Peter finally did.
dailies.prayer: Father, thank you that you do not show favoritism, and that the good news of Jesus is for every nation and people. Thank you for pouring out your Spirit, and for forgiveness through Jesus’ name. Give us wide hearts, and make us glad to welcome. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
dailies.teach: Peter said God does not show favoritism, but accepts from every nation the one who fears him. While he was still speaking, the Holy Spirit came on all who heard, even on Gentiles. This is a story for thanking God, and for asking him to keep widening our welcome.
dailies.enochActivity: Help a grown-up thank God out loud that the good news is for every nation.
dailies.elijah2: In Acts 10:44, when did the Holy Spirit come on those who heard?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: While Peter was still speaking these words, the Holy Spirit came on all who heard the message.
dailies.jordyn2: How does praying this story keep both Cornelius’s house and Peter’s surprising yes in view?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: We thank God that he heard a praying household, and that he also changed Peter’s understanding. The good news needed a messenger who would go, and listeners who would hear. Both are gifts to ask for again.
dailies.passageText: 34 Then Peter began to speak: “I now realize how true it is that God does not show favoritism 35 but accepts from every nation the one who fears him and does what is right. 44 While Peter was still speaking these words, the Holy Spirit came on all who heard the message. 45 The circumcised believers who had come with Peter were astonished that the gift of the Holy Spirit had been poured out even on Gentiles.

dailies.label: Day 7 · Recap
dailies.focus: The good news of Jesus is for every nation and people, and next we will see the church pray and God set Peter free.
dailies.verse: God does not show favoritism.
dailies.enoch: Open your arms wide, then fold your hands, and say: The good news is for everyone! Next week, the church will pray.
dailies.elijah: In Acts 10:34–35 and 10:44–48, what did Peter realize, and what did God do while he was still speaking?
dailies.elijahAnswer: Peter realized that God does not show favoritism, but accepts from every nation the one who fears him. While Peter was still speaking, the Holy Spirit came on all who heard, and they were baptized in the name of Jesus Christ.
dailies.jordyn: This week the good news crossed a line Peter had not expected. How does that get your heart ready for next week, when the church will pray and God will set Peter free?
dailies.jordynAnswer: The same Lord who sent the good news to every nation can also set his servant free when trouble comes. Next week we will see Peter in prison, and the church praying, and God setting him free.
dailies.action: Tell someone the week’s big idea: The good news of Jesus is for every nation and people. Then thank God, and look ahead to the church praying for Peter.
dailies.prayer: Father, thank you that you do not show favoritism, and that the good news of Jesus is for every nation and people. Get our hearts ready to see the church pray, and to see you set Peter free. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
dailies.teach: This week we learned that the good news of Jesus is for every nation and people. God heard Cornelius and sent him to Peter. Peter realized that God does not show favoritism. He told them the good news of Jesus, who is Lord of all, and everyone who believes in him receives forgiveness through his name. While Peter was still speaking, the Holy Spirit came on all who heard, and they were baptized. Next week we will see the church praying, and God setting Peter free.
dailies.enochActivity: Help a grown-up fold their hands as if in prayer, and say: Next week the church will pray, and God will set Peter free!
dailies.elijah2: In Acts 10:48, what did they ask Peter to do after they were baptized?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: They asked Peter to stay with them for a few days.
dailies.jordyn2: Why is the good news is for every nation a fitting last word before a week about Peter in prison?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: This week we saw the good news going farther than Peter expected. Next week we will see that the same work can look like it has been stopped, when Peter is in prison. The church will pray, and God will keep his work moving.
dailies.passageText: 34 Then Peter began to speak: “I now realize how true it is that God does not show favoritism 35 but accepts from every nation the one who fears him and does what is right. 44 While Peter was still speaking these words, the Holy Spirit came on all who heard the message. 48 So he ordered that they be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ. Then they asked Peter to stay with them for a few days.

readings.text: 1 It was about this time that King Herod arrested some who belonged to the church, intending to persecute them. 2 He had James, the brother of John, put to death with the sword. 3 When he saw that this met with approval among the Jews, he proceeded to seize Peter also. This happened during the Festival of Unleavened Bread. 4 After arresting him, he put him in prison, handing him over to be guarded by four squads of four soldiers each. Herod intended to bring him out for public trial after the Passover. 5 So Peter was kept in prison, but the church was earnestly praying to God for him.

6 The night before Herod was to bring him to trial, Peter was sleeping between two soldiers, bound with two chains, and sentries stood guard at the entrance. 7 Suddenly an angel of the Lord appeared and a light shone in the cell. He struck Peter on the side and woke him up. “Quick, get up!” he said, and the chains fell off Peter’s wrists. 8 Then the angel said to him, “Put on your clothes and sandals.” And Peter did so. “Wrap your cloak around you and follow me,” the angel told him. 9 Peter followed him out of the prison, but he had no idea that what the angel was doing was really happening; he thought he was seeing a vision. 10 They passed the first and second guards and came to the iron gate leading to the city. It opened for them by itself, and they went through it. When they had walked the length of one street, suddenly the angel left him. 11 Then Peter came to himself and said, “Now I know without a doubt that the Lord has sent his angel and rescued me from Herod’s clutches and from everything the Jewish people were hoping would happen.”

12 When this had dawned on him, he went to the house of Mary the mother of John, also called Mark, where many people had gathered and were praying. 13 Peter knocked at the outer entrance, and a servant named Rhoda came to answer the door. 14 When she recognized Peter’s voice, she was so overjoyed she ran back without opening it and exclaimed, “Peter is at the door!” 15 “You’re out of your mind,” they told her. When she kept insisting that it was so, they said, “It must be his angel.” 16 But Peter kept on knocking, and when they opened the door and saw him, they were astonished. 17 Peter motioned with his hand for them to be quiet and described how the Lord had brought him out of prison. “Tell James and the other brothers and sisters about this,” he said, and then he left for another place.

story: Last week the good news of Jesus went to every nation and people, and Peter stayed with Cornelius’s household. Then a hard time came. King Herod arrested some who belonged to the church. He had James, the brother of John, put to death. When he saw that this met with approval, he seized Peter also, during the Festival of Unleavened Bread, and put him in prison, guarded by four squads of four soldiers each. Herod intended to bring him out for public trial after the Passover. So Peter was kept in prison, but the church was earnestly praying to God for him.

The night before the trial, Peter was sleeping between two soldiers, bound with two chains, and sentries stood guard at the entrance. Suddenly an angel of the Lord appeared and a light shone in the cell. He struck Peter on the side and woke him up. “Quick, get up!” he said, and the chains fell off Peter’s wrists. Then the angel said to him, “Put on your clothes and sandals.” And Peter did so. “Wrap your cloak around you and follow me,” the angel told him. Peter followed him out, but he thought he was seeing a vision. They passed the guards, the iron gate opened by itself, and they walked the length of one street. Then the angel left him.

Peter came to himself and said, “Now I know without a doubt that the Lord has sent his angel and rescued me from Herod’s clutches and from everything the Jewish people were hoping would happen.” He went to the house of Mary, the mother of John, also called Mark, where many people had gathered and were praying. Peter knocked at the outer entrance, and a servant named Rhoda came to answer the door. When she recognized Peter’s voice, she was so overjoyed she ran back without opening it and exclaimed, “Peter is at the door!” “You’re out of your mind,” they told her. When she kept insisting that it was so, they said, “It must be his angel.” But Peter kept on knocking, and when they opened the door and saw him, they were astonished.

Peter motioned with his hand for them to be quiet and described how the Lord had brought him out of prison. “Tell James and the other brothers and sisters about this,” he said, and then he left for another place. The James he wants them to tell is a leader in the church, not James the brother of John, who had already been put to death. The church prayed, and God set Peter free.
Next week we will see the church sending Paul and Barnabas to tell other towns about Jesus.
weeks.enochLine: The church prayed, and God set Peter free!
enochActivities: Activity: Pray. Fold your hands and say: The church prayed for Peter!
Activity: Knock. Gently knock, then open your hands, and say: God set Peter free!
elijahQuestions: In Acts 12:1–5, what did King Herod do, and what was the church doing while Peter was in prison?
In Acts 12:6–11, how did the Lord set Peter free, and what did Peter say when he came to himself?
In Acts 12:13–16, what did Rhoda do when she recognized Peter’s voice, and what did the people inside say?
In Acts 12:16–17, what happened when they finally opened the door, and what did Peter tell them to do?
elijahAnswers: Herod arrested some who belonged to the church, had James the brother of John put to death, and then seized Peter and put him in prison. The church was earnestly praying to God for him (Acts 12:1–5).

An angel of the Lord appeared, the chains fell off, and Peter followed the angel out past the guards. The iron gate opened by itself. Peter said, “Now I know without a doubt that the Lord has sent his angel and rescued me from Herod’s clutches and from everything the Jewish people were hoping would happen.” (Acts 12:7–11).
She was so overjoyed she ran back without opening the door and said, “Peter is at the door!” They told her, “You’re out of your mind,” and then, “It must be his angel.” (Acts 12:14–15).
They were astonished. Peter described how the Lord had brought him out of prison, and said, “Tell James and the other brothers and sisters about this,” then he left for another place (Acts 12:16–17).
jordynQuestions: The church was already earnestly praying (Acts 12:5, 12), and still they could not believe Rhoda (Acts 12:15). What does that tell you about praying, and about being ready for God to answer?
Peter is set free the night before the trial, while he is sleeping in chains (Acts 12:6–11). What does that show you about whose work this rescue is?
This week the church prayed, and God set Peter free. Next week the church will send Paul and Barnabas to other towns. What do both stories show you about how God keeps using his people?
jordynAnswers: Earnest prayer is real, and even praying people can be slow to believe an answer when it comes. Rhoda recognized Peter’s voice and kept insisting. The church was astonished when they opened the door. We can pray earnestly, and we can also be ready to rejoice when God answers.

Peter is not staging an escape. He is asleep, bound, and guarded. The angel comes, the chains fall, the gate opens, and only afterward does Peter know without a doubt that the Lord has rescued him. The church prayed, and God did the work they could not do.

God hears a praying church, and he also sends a going church. This week he sets Peter free. Next week we will see the church send Paul and Barnabas to tell other towns about Jesus. Prayer and sending both belong to his work.
weeks.jordynApplication: The church prayed, and God set Peter free (Acts 12:1–17). This week, pray earnestly for someone who is in a hard place, and be ready to rejoice if God answers in a way you did not expect. Next week we will see the church sending Paul and Barnabas to other towns.
weeks.applicationCheck: Ask her later in the week whether she prayed earnestly for someone, and whether she was ready to notice an answer. If it is fitting, thank God together that the church prayed, and that God set Peter free.
weeks.prayer: Father, thank you that the church was earnestly praying to you for Peter, and that you sent your angel and set him free. Thank you that Rhoda recognized his voice, and that you answered even when the praying church was slow to believe it. Teach us to pray earnestly, and to rejoice when you answer. In Jesus’ name, Amen.

dailies.label: Day 2 · Passage
dailies.focus: Peter is in prison, and the church is earnestly praying to God for him.
dailies.verse: The church was earnestly praying to God for him.
dailies.enoch: Fold your hands and say: The church prayed for Peter!
dailies.elijah: In Acts 12:1–5, why was Peter in prison, and what was the church doing?
dailies.elijahAnswer: King Herod had arrested some who belonged to the church, and after James the brother of John was put to death, he seized Peter and put him in prison. The church was earnestly praying to God for him.
dailies.jordyn: The church cannot open the prison, and still they pray earnestly (Acts 12:5). What does that tell you about what prayer is for, when a situation looks locked?
dailies.jordynAnswer: Prayer is not a last small try after every other plan. It is the church bringing Peter to God, when they cannot reach him themselves. God can do what they cannot do.
dailies.action: Read Acts 12:1–5 together, then tell someone: Peter was in prison, but the church was earnestly praying to God for him.
dailies.prayer: Father, thank you that the church prayed earnestly for Peter when he was in prison. Teach us to pray that way for people in hard places. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
dailies.teach: King Herod arrested some who belonged to the church. James, the brother of John, was put to death, and then Peter was seized and put in prison, guarded by many soldiers. Herod planned a public trial after the Passover. So Peter was kept in prison, but the church was earnestly praying to God for him.
dailies.enochActivity: Help a grown-up fold hands with you, and say: We can pray for people too!
dailies.elijah2: In Acts 12:4–5, how carefully was Peter guarded, and what contrast does verse 5 name?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: He was handed over to four squads of four soldiers each. Peter was kept in prison, but the church was earnestly praying to God for him.
dailies.jordyn2: Why is it important to tell this first part with care, including James, without turning it into a scary show?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: The harm is real, and the Bible names it simply. James was put to death, and Peter was next. We tell the truth with dignity, and then we stay with the main line of this week: the church prayed, and God set Peter free.
dailies.passageText: 1 It was about this time that King Herod arrested some who belonged to the church, intending to persecute them. 2 He had James, the brother of John, put to death with the sword. 3 When he saw that this met with approval among the Jews, he proceeded to seize Peter also. This happened during the Festival of Unleavened Bread. 4 After arresting him, he put him in prison, handing him over to be guarded by four squads of four soldiers each. Herod intended to bring him out for public trial after the Passover. 5 So Peter was kept in prison, but the church was earnestly praying to God for him.

dailies.label: Day 3 · Game
dailies.focus: Practice earnest prayer, and a glad knock-and-open welcome, like the church and Rhoda.
dailies.verse: Peter is at the door!
dailies.enoch: Gently knock, then fold your hands, and say: God can answer prayer!
dailies.elijah: In Acts 12:5 and 12:12, where were the believers, and what were they doing?
dailies.elijahAnswer: They were earnestly praying to God for Peter, and many had gathered at the house of Mary, the mother of John, also called Mark, and were praying.
dailies.jordyn: How should we play a pray-and-knock game so that we honor Rhoda, and do not make the prison, the soldiers, or James’s death into a joke or a fight?
dailies.jordynAnswer: We do not act out swords, chains, or guards. We practice folding our hands to pray, then a gentle knock, and the glad words Peter is at the door. We honor Rhoda’s joy, and we honor the God who answers.
dailies.action: Play a pray-and-knock game: one person prays a short sentence for someone, another knocks, and someone opens and says, God can answer prayer. Then switch.
dailies.prayer: Father, thank you that the church gathered to pray, and that Rhoda recognized Peter’s voice with joy. Teach us to pray earnestly, and to welcome your answers with gladness. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
dailies.teach: The church was earnestly praying for Peter. Many had gathered at Mary’s house and were still praying when Peter knocked. Rhoda recognized his voice and was so overjoyed she ran to tell them, “Peter is at the door!” Today we practice that kind of prayer, and that kind of glad welcome.
dailies.enochActivity: Help a grown-up pray one short sentence, then let you knock gently and say: Peter is at the door!
dailies.elijah2: In Acts 12:14, why did Rhoda run back without opening the door?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: When she recognized Peter’s voice, she was so overjoyed she ran back without opening it.
dailies.jordyn2: Why is Rhoda a better person to imitate in a game than Herod or the soldiers?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: She hears, she recognizes, and she runs with joy to tell the praying church. The rescue belongs to the Lord. Our part, like the church and like Rhoda, is to pray and to welcome the answer.
dailies.passageText: 5 So Peter was kept in prison, but the church was earnestly praying to God for him. 12 When this had dawned on him, he went to the house of Mary the mother of John, also called Mark, where many people had gathered and were praying. 13 Peter knocked at the outer entrance, and a servant named Rhoda came to answer the door. 14 When she recognized Peter’s voice, she was so overjoyed she ran back without opening it and exclaimed, “Peter is at the door!”

dailies.label: Day 4 · Passage
dailies.focus: The Lord sends his angel, Peter is set free, and the praying church is astonished.
dailies.verse: Now I know without a doubt that the Lord has sent his angel and rescued me.
dailies.enoch: Open your hands as if chains have fallen, and say: God set Peter free!
dailies.elijah: In Acts 12:7–11, what did the angel tell Peter to do, and what did Peter know when he came to himself?
dailies.elijahAnswer: The angel said, “Quick, get up!” then, “Put on your clothes and sandals.” And, “Wrap your cloak around you and follow me,” When Peter came to himself, he knew without a doubt that the Lord had sent his angel and rescued him.
dailies.jordyn: Peter is asleep, in chains, and guarded, and then the Lord sets him free (Acts 12:6–11). The church is praying, and still they are astonished at the door (Acts 12:12–16). How do those two pictures fit together?
dailies.jordynAnswer: God does the rescue they could not do, and he also surprises the people who were asking him to do it. Prayer does not mean they already had the whole answer pictured. They prayed, God acted, and then they had to open the door and see.
dailies.action: Read Acts 12:6–17 together, then tell someone: The Lord sent his angel and set Peter free, and the church was astonished.
dailies.prayer: Father, thank you that you sent your angel and rescued Peter, and that the praying church saw him at the door. Make us people who pray, and who are ready to be astonished by your answers. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
dailies.teach: The night before the trial, Peter was sleeping in chains between soldiers. An angel appeared, a light shone, and the chains fell off. “Quick, get up!” the angel said. Peter followed him out, the gate opened by itself, and then Peter knew the Lord had rescued him. He knocked at Mary’s house. Rhoda recognized his voice and said, “Peter is at the door!” They did not believe her at first, but Peter kept knocking. They opened, were astonished, and he told them how the Lord had brought him out.
dailies.enochActivity: Help a grown-up pretend to put on a cloak, then take a few steps and say: The Lord set Peter free!
dailies.elijah2: In Acts 12:16–17, what did the people do when they saw Peter, and what did he tell them?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: They were astonished. Peter motioned for them to be quiet, described how the Lord had brought him out of prison, and said, “Tell James and the other brothers and sisters about this,” then he left for another place.
dailies.jordyn2: Peter tells them to tell James, after James the brother of John has already been put to death (Acts 12:2, 17). Why is it important not to mix up those two men?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: The James who was killed was James the brother of John. The James Peter wants them to tell is a leader still in the church. God has set Peter free, and the news is to go to the family of believers who are still serving.
dailies.passageText: 6 The night before Herod was to bring him to trial, Peter was sleeping between two soldiers, bound with two chains, and sentries stood guard at the entrance. 7 Suddenly an angel of the Lord appeared and a light shone in the cell. He struck Peter on the side and woke him up. “Quick, get up!” he said, and the chains fell off Peter’s wrists. 8 Then the angel said to him, “Put on your clothes and sandals.” And Peter did so. “Wrap your cloak around you and follow me,” the angel told him. 9 Peter followed him out of the prison, but he had no idea that what the angel was doing was really happening; he thought he was seeing a vision. 10 They passed the first and second guards and came to the iron gate leading to the city. It opened for them by itself, and they went through it. When they had walked the length of one street, suddenly the angel left him. 11 Then Peter came to himself and said, “Now I know without a doubt that the Lord has sent his angel and rescued me from Herod’s clutches and from everything the Jewish people were hoping would happen.” 12 When this had dawned on him, he went to the house of Mary the mother of John, also called Mark, where many people had gathered and were praying. 13 Peter knocked at the outer entrance, and a servant named Rhoda came to answer the door. 14 When she recognized Peter’s voice, she was so overjoyed she ran back without opening it and exclaimed, “Peter is at the door!” 15 “You’re out of your mind,” they told her. When she kept insisting that it was so, they said, “It must be his angel.” 16 But Peter kept on knocking, and when they opened the door and saw him, they were astonished. 17 Peter motioned with his hand for them to be quiet and described how the Lord had brought him out of prison. “Tell James and the other brothers and sisters about this,” he said, and then he left for another place.

dailies.label: Day 5 · Challenge
dailies.focus: Pray earnestly this week for someone in a hard place, and be ready to notice God’s answer.
dailies.verse: The church was earnestly praying to God for him.
dailies.enoch: Fold your hands and say: I can pray for someone today!
dailies.elijah: In Acts 12:5 and 12:12, how was the church praying, and where had they gathered?
dailies.elijahAnswer: They were earnestly praying to God for Peter, and many had gathered at the house of Mary, the mother of John, also called Mark, and were praying.
dailies.jordyn: The church prayed earnestly, and God set Peter free in a way they were slow to believe (Acts 12:5, 15–16). What would a right-sized challenge look like for you this week?
dailies.jordynAnswer: Choose one person in a hard place and pray for them by name, more than once, not only in a rush. Then watch for an answer with a ready, glad heart, like Rhoda at the door. The challenge is not to force a miracle. It is to pray earnestly, and to be ready to rejoice.
dailies.action: Choose one person this week who is in a hard place. Pray for them earnestly by name, more than once, and tell a parent you are praying.
dailies.prayer: Father, the church prayed earnestly for Peter, and you set him free. Give us names to carry to you this week, and give us ready hearts if you answer. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
dailies.teach: Peter was in prison, but the church was earnestly praying to God for him. Many were still praying at Mary’s house when he knocked. They were astonished when they opened the door and saw him. Earnest prayer, and a ready welcome, belong together.
dailies.enochActivity: Help a grown-up name one person you can pray for this week, and say their name in a short prayer.
dailies.elijah2: In Acts 12:16, what did Peter do when they did not open the door at first?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: Peter kept on knocking, and when they opened the door and saw him, they were astonished.
dailies.jordyn2: Why is keeping on a fitting picture, both for Peter at the door and for a church at prayer?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: Peter does not walk away after one knock. The church had already been praying earnestly. God answers, and sometimes the people who asked still need time, and more knocking, before they open the door and see what he has done.
dailies.passageText: 5 So Peter was kept in prison, but the church was earnestly praying to God for him. 12 When this had dawned on him, he went to the house of Mary the mother of John, also called Mark, where many people had gathered and were praying. 16 But Peter kept on knocking, and when they opened the door and saw him, they were astonished.

dailies.label: Day 6 · Prayer
dailies.focus: Thank God that he heard the church and set Peter free, and ask for earnest, believing prayer.
dailies.verse: Now I know without a doubt that the Lord has sent his angel and rescued me.
dailies.enoch: Fold your hands, then open them, and say: Thank you, God, for answering prayer!
dailies.elijah: In Acts 12:11 and 12:17, what did Peter know, and what did he want the church to tell?
dailies.elijahAnswer: He knew without a doubt that the Lord had sent his angel and rescued him. He told them to tell James and the other brothers and sisters about this.
dailies.jordyn: Peter wants the news told (Acts 12:17). How can thanking God this week include both the rescue and the people who had been praying?
dailies.jordynAnswer: Thank God that he sent his angel and set Peter free, and thank him that the church was already praying. Then ask him to make you a person who prays earnestly, and who tells others when he answers, so the family of believers can rejoice too.
dailies.action: Pray together: thank God that the church prayed and he set Peter free, and ask him to teach you to pray earnestly and to rejoice at his answers.
dailies.prayer: Father, thank you that the church was earnestly praying, and that you sent your angel and rescued Peter. Thank you that Rhoda recognized his voice, and that the astonished church saw him at the door. Teach us to pray, and to give you thanks. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
dailies.teach: Peter knew the Lord had sent his angel and rescued him. He went to a house where people were praying, kept knocking, and then told them how the Lord had brought him out of prison. This is a story for thanking God, and for asking him to make us a praying church.
dailies.enochActivity: Help a grown-up thank God out loud that he set Peter free.
dailies.elijah2: In Acts 12:12, whose house did Peter go to, and what was happening there?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: He went to the house of Mary, the mother of John, also called Mark, where many people had gathered and were praying.
dailies.jordyn2: Why is a praying house a fitting last picture before we thank God at the end of this week?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: The rescue did not end in the street. Peter went to the people who had been asking God for him. Prayer began the story, and prayer was still happening when the answer arrived at the door.
dailies.passageText: 11 Then Peter came to himself and said, “Now I know without a doubt that the Lord has sent his angel and rescued me from Herod’s clutches and from everything the Jewish people were hoping would happen.” 12 When this had dawned on him, he went to the house of Mary the mother of John, also called Mark, where many people had gathered and were praying. 16 But Peter kept on knocking, and when they opened the door and saw him, they were astonished. 17 Peter motioned with his hand for them to be quiet and described how the Lord had brought him out of prison. “Tell James and the other brothers and sisters about this,” he said, and then he left for another place.

dailies.label: Day 7 · Recap
dailies.focus: The church prayed, and God set Peter free, and next the church will send Paul and Barnabas.
dailies.verse: The church was earnestly praying to God for him.
dailies.enoch: Fold your hands, then knock gently, and say: The church prayed, and God set Peter free!
dailies.elijah: In Acts 12:5 and 12:11, what was the church doing, and what did Peter know after he was free?
dailies.elijahAnswer: The church was earnestly praying to God for him. Peter knew without a doubt that the Lord had sent his angel and rescued him.
dailies.jordyn: This week a praying church saw God set Peter free. How does that get your heart ready for next week, when the church will send Paul and Barnabas to other towns?
dailies.jordynAnswer: The same God who hears prayer also sends people. This week he sets Peter free. Next week we will see the church send Paul and Barnabas to tell other towns about Jesus.
dailies.action: Tell someone the week’s big idea: The church prayed, and God set Peter free. Then thank God, and look ahead to the church sending Paul and Barnabas.
dailies.prayer: Father, thank you that the church prayed, and you set Peter free. Get our hearts ready to see you send Paul and Barnabas to tell other towns about Jesus. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
dailies.teach: This week we learned that the church prayed, and God set Peter free. Herod put Peter in prison, and the church prayed earnestly. An angel woke Peter, the chains fell off, and the Lord rescued him. Rhoda heard him at the door, the church was astonished, and Peter told them to share the news. Next week we will see the church sending Paul and Barnabas to tell other towns about Jesus.
dailies.enochActivity: Help a grown-up look down a hall as if toward another town, and say: Next week the church will send Paul and Barnabas!
dailies.elijah2: In Acts 12:17, what did Peter do after he told them what the Lord had done?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: He left for another place.
dailies.jordyn2: Why is the church prayed, and God set Peter free a fitting last word before a week about sending?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: God kept Peter for his work, and he keeps using a praying, obedient church. The next chapter of the story is not only safety. It is a church that will send people to other towns with the good news.
dailies.passageText: 5 So Peter was kept in prison, but the church was earnestly praying to God for him. 11 Then Peter came to himself and said, “Now I know without a doubt that the Lord has sent his angel and rescued me from Herod’s clutches and from everything the Jewish people were hoping would happen.” 16 But Peter kept on knocking, and when they opened the door and saw him, they were astonished. 17 Peter motioned with his hand for them to be quiet and described how the Lord had brought him out of prison. “Tell James and the other brothers and sisters about this,” he said, and then he left for another place.
